subtitle.en: Seven districts, from proof to probability
subtitle.zh: 七个街区：从证明到概率

description.en: A city of seven districts covering the core of an undergraduate mathematics education for computer scientists: logic and proof, sets and infinity, number theory and algebra, combinatorics and graphs, calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics.
description.zh: 一座七个街区的城市，覆盖计算机专业本科数学的核心：逻辑与证明、集合与无穷、数论与代数、组合与图论、微积分、线性代数、概率与统计。

metaphor.en: A city whose districts are fields of mathematics, each street lined with halls of theorems.
metaphor.zh: 一座以数学分支为街区的城市，每条街道两旁都是定理的展馆。

summary.en: The language of mathematics and the ways of establishing truth: propositions, quantifiers and the standard methods of proof.
summary.zh: 数学的语言与求真之道：命题、量词，以及几种基本的证明方法。

summary.en: Every statement on trial is either true or false; connectives, implication and quantifiers decide the verdict.
summary.zh: 受审的每个命题非真即假；联结词、蕴涵与量词决定判决。

summary.en: A proposition is either true or false; ¬, ∧, ∨, → and ↔ combine propositions, and a truth table settles every case.
summary.zh: 命题非真即假；¬、∧、∨、→、↔ 把命题组合起来，真值表穷举所有情形。

explain.en: A proposition is a statement that is either true or false. Connectives build compound propositions: negation ¬P, conjunction P ∧ Q (both true), disjunction P ∨ Q (at least one true, the inclusive or), implication P → Q and the biconditional P ↔ Q (same truth value). The value of a compound depends only on the values of its parts, so a truth table with 2ⁿ rows for n variables decides it completely. Two formulas are logically equivalent when they agree on every row; a tautology is true on every row, like P ∨ ¬P. De Morgan's laws, ¬(P ∧ Q) ≡ ¬P ∨ ¬Q and ¬(P ∨ Q) ≡ ¬P ∧ ¬Q, say that negation swaps ∧ and ∨. They are used constantly to negate statements and to simplify code.
explain.zh: 命题（proposition）是非真即假的陈述。联结词把简单命题组合成复合命题：否定 ¬P，合取 P∧Q（两者都真），析取 P∨Q（至少一个为真，是可兼的“或”），蕴涵 P→Q，双条件 P↔Q（真值相同）。复合命题的真值只取决于各部分的真值，所以 n 个变量的真值表共 2ⁿ 行，可以完全判定它。两个公式在每一行都取值相同，就称逻辑等价；每一行都为真的公式叫重言式（tautology），如 P∨¬P。德摩根律 ¬(P∧Q) ≡ ¬P∨¬Q、¬(P∨Q) ≡ ¬P∧¬Q 说明否定会把 ∧ 与 ∨ 互换，否定命题、化简代码时随时用到。

example.en: Check De Morgan with a truth table. For (P, Q) = (T, T), (T, F), (F, T), (F, F), the formula ¬(P ∧ Q) gives F, T, T, T and ¬P ∨ ¬Q also gives F, T, T, T. The columns agree, so the formulas are equivalent. In Python, not (a and b) equals (not a) or (not b), and 'x is not in [1, 10]', that is ¬(1 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 10), becomes x < 1 ∨ x > 10.
example.zh: 用真值表验证德摩根律：(P,Q) 依次取 (真,真)、(真,假)、(假,真)、(假,假) 时，¬(P∧Q) 得 假、真、真、真，¬P∨¬Q 也得 假、真、真、真，两列相同，故二者等价。Python 中 not (a and b) 等于 (not a) or (not b)；“x 不在 [1,10] 内”即 ¬(1≤x ∧ x≤10)，可化为 x<1 ∨ x>10。

image.en: In the courtroom the scales of justice weigh two formulas: ¬(P ∧ Q) on one pan and ¬P ∨ ¬Q on the other. Four jurors on the jury bench stand for the four rows of the truth table; each tries a different pair of truth values, and every time the scales stay perfectly level. The judge in her black robe raises her gavel: equivalent.
image.zh: 法庭上，正义天平一边托着 ¬(P∧Q)，一边托着 ¬P∨¬Q。陪审席上四位陪审员代表真值表的四行，各试一组真假取值，天平每次都纹丝不动地保持水平。身穿黑袍的法官举起法槌：两者等价。

means.en: logical equivalence: the same truth value on every row
means.zh: 逻辑等价：每一行的真值都相同

thing.en: the two plaques on the scales

means.en: De Morgan: negation turns ∧ into ∨ and negates each part
means.zh: 德摩根律：否定把 ∧ 变成 ∨，并逐项否定

means.en: the 2² = 4 rows of the truth table for P and Q
means.zh: P、Q 两个变量的真值表共 2²=4 行

means.en: a verdict: every proposition is either true or false
means.zh: 判决：每个命题非真即假

summary.en: P → Q fails only when P is true and Q is false; it is equivalent to its contrapositive ¬Q → ¬P, not to its converse.
summary.zh: P→Q 只在 P 真 Q 假时为假；它与逆否命题 ¬Q→¬P 等价，与逆命题不等价。

explain.en: The implication P → Q ('if P then Q') is false in exactly one case: P true and Q false. When P is false the implication is vacuously true. It is equivalent to its contrapositive ¬Q → ¬P, but not to its converse Q → P or its inverse ¬P → ¬Q, which are equivalent to each other. In P → Q, P is a sufficient condition for Q and Q is a necessary condition for P. 'P if and only if Q' means both directions, (P → Q) ∧ (Q → P), so an iff proof has two parts. Confusing an implication with its converse is one of the most common errors in reasoning.
explain.zh: 蕴涵 P→Q（“若 P 则 Q”）只在一种情形下为假：P 真而 Q 假。P 为假时蕴涵“空真”（vacuously true）。它与逆否命题 ¬Q→¬P 等价，但与逆命题 Q→P、否命题 ¬P→¬Q 都不等价（后两者彼此等价）。在 P→Q 中，P 是 Q 的充分条件，Q 是 P 的必要条件。“P 当且仅当 Q”要求两个方向都成立，即 (P→Q)∧(Q→P)，所以证明“当且仅当”要分两步。把蕴涵与它的逆命题混为一谈，是推理中最常见的错误之一。

example.en: Rule: if a person drinks beer, they are over 18. Four cases are on the table, each with one fact hidden: a beer drinker, a cola drinker, a 25-year-old and a 16-year-old. Only the beer drinker (P true) and the 16-year-old (Q false) can break the rule, so only they need checking. Likewise, 'if n² is even then n is even' is proved via its contrapositive: if n = 2k + 1, then n² = 2(2k² + 2k) + 1 is odd.
example.zh: 规则：喝啤酒的人必须年满 18 岁。桌上四个案例，各遮住一项信息：喝啤酒的、喝可乐的、25 岁的、16 岁的。只有喝啤酒者（P 真）和 16 岁者（Q 假）可能违规，只需查这两个。同理，证明“若 n² 为偶数则 n 为偶数”可改证逆否命题：n=2k+1 时 n²=2(2k²+2k)+1 为奇数。

image.en: Four giant exhibits stand before the judge: a beer bottle, a mug of cola, an ID card reading 25 and an ID card reading 16. The rule on trial: whoever drinks beer must be over 18. Two huge magnifying glasses stand only before the beer bottle and the 16 card, the two cases that could break the rule. The judge ignores the cola and the 25 entirely.
image.zh: 法官面前立着四件巨大的证物：一瓶啤酒、一杯可乐、一张写着 25 的证件、一张写着 16 的证件。受审的规则是：喝啤酒的人必须年满 18 岁。两只巨型放大镜只立在啤酒瓶和“16”前面——只有这两件可能违规；可乐和“25”法官看都不看。

means.en: P is true: check that Q holds
means.zh: P 为真：必须核实 Q

means.en: Q is false: check that P fails, the contrapositive ¬Q → ¬P
means.zh: Q 为假：必须核实 ¬P，即逆否命题 ¬Q→¬P

means.en: P is false: the rule holds vacuously
means.zh: P 为假：规则空真成立

means.en: Q true tells nothing: checking it would test the converse
means.zh: Q 为真说明不了什么：查它等于检验逆命题

summary.en: ∀ means 'for all' and ∃ means 'there exists'; negation swaps them and negates the inside, and their order matters.
summary.zh: ∀ 表示“对所有”，∃ 表示“存在”；否定时二者互换并否定内层，顺序也不能随意交换。

explain.en: The universal quantifier ∀x P(x) says P holds for every x in the domain; the existential quantifier ∃x P(x) says it holds for at least one. Negation flips each quantifier and moves inward: ¬∀x P(x) ≡ ∃x ¬P(x) and ¬∃x P(x) ≡ ∀x ¬P(x). So one counterexample disproves a universal claim, while no number of examples proves it. The order of mixed quantifiers matters: over the reals, ∀x ∃y (y > x) is true, since y = x + 1 works, but ∃y ∀x (y > x) is false, since no number exceeds every number. Definitions of limits and continuity are strings of alternating quantifiers, and negating them is a routine step in proofs.
explain.zh: 全称量词 ∀x P(x) 表示论域中每个 x 都满足 P；存在量词 ∃x P(x) 表示至少有一个 x 满足。否定时逐个翻转量词并向内推进：¬∀x P(x) ≡ ∃x ¬P(x)，¬∃x P(x) ≡ ∀x ¬P(x)。所以一个反例就能推翻全称命题，而再多的例子也证明不了它。混合量词的顺序很关键：在实数中 ∀x ∃y (y>x) 为真（取 y=x+1），∃y ∀x (y>x) 却为假（没有比所有数都大的数）。极限、连续等定义都是交替出现的量词串，证明中经常要对它们取否定。

example.en: Claim: every odd number greater than 1 is prime. Negation: some odd number greater than 1 is not prime, and the counterexample 9 = 3 · 3 settles it. Negating a nested statement step by step, ¬∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 ∀x (|x−a| < δ → |f(x)−f(a)| < ε) becomes ∃ε>0 ∀δ>0 ∃x (|x−a| < δ ∧ |f(x)−f(a)| ≥ ε), which is exactly what 'f is not continuous at a' means.
example.zh: 命题：大于 1 的奇数都是素数。否定：存在大于 1 且不是素数的奇数，反例 9=3·3 即可推翻。逐层否定嵌套命题：¬∀ε>0 ∃δ>0 ∀x (|x−a|<δ → |f(x)−f(a)|<ε) 变为 ∃ε>0 ∀δ>0 ∃x (|x−a|<δ ∧ |f(x)−f(a)|≥ε)，这正是“f 在 a 处不连续”的含义。

image.en: A prosecutor in a top hat declares that every bird in the courtroom is white. Five white doves perch along the jury pew as if to agree. Then one big black crow hops onto the floor in front of them. A single crow is enough: the defence lawyer points at it, and the prosecutor shrugs as his claim collapses.
image.zh: 戴礼帽的检察官宣称：法庭里所有的鸟都是白的。五只白鸽排在陪审席的长椅上，像在附和。这时一只硕大的黑乌鸦跳上了它们面前的地板。一只就够了：辩护律师指着它，检察官耸耸肩，论断当场崩塌。

means.en: a universal statement ∀x P(x)
examples: however many, they never prove a ∀ claim
means.zh: 例子再多也证明不了全称命题

means.en: ∃x ¬P(x): one counterexample refutes ∀x P(x)
negation flips ∀ to ∃ and negates the inside
means.zh: 否定把 ∀ 换成 ∃，并否定内层

summary.en: Direct proof, contradiction and induction: the standard ways to turn a conjecture into a theorem.
summary.zh: 直接证明、反证与归纳：把猜想变成定理的标准方法。

title.en: Direct Proof and Proof by Contradiction

summary.en: Prove P → Q by deriving Q from P, by proving ¬Q → ¬P, or by assuming the claim false and reaching a contradiction.
summary.zh: 直接从 P 推出 Q，或改证 ¬Q→¬P，或假设结论不成立并推出矛盾。

explain.en: A direct proof assumes the hypotheses and chains valid steps to the conclusion. A proof by contrapositive proves P → Q by proving the equivalent ¬Q → ¬P. A proof by contradiction assumes the statement is false and derives something impossible, such as R ∧ ¬R; since the assumption leads to absurdity, the statement must be true. The classic proof that √2 is irrational uses all three: a direct computation shows that odd numbers have odd squares, the contrapositive gives 'p² even ⇒ p even', and the whole argument is a contradiction. Euclid's proof that there are infinitely many primes is the other model; it is often written as a contradiction but is really a direct construction.
explain.zh: 直接证明从前提出发，经有效推理一步步得到结论。逆否证法通过证明等价的 ¬Q→¬P 来证明 P→Q。反证法先假设命题不成立，再推出不可能的结果（如 R∧¬R）；既然假设导致荒谬，命题只能为真。经典的“√2 是无理数”同时用到三种方法：直接计算可知奇数的平方是奇数，由逆否得“p² 为偶数则 p 为偶数”，整个论证则是反证。欧几里得证明素数有无穷多个是另一个范例，它常被写成反证，其实是一个直接构造。

example.en: √2 is irrational. Suppose √2 = p/q with integers p, q in lowest terms. Then p² = 2q², so p² is even, hence p is even: p = 2k. Substituting, 4k² = 2q², so q² = 2k² and q is even too. Both p and q are even, contradicting lowest terms. So no such fraction exists.
example.zh: 证明 √2 是无理数。假设 √2 = p/q，p、q 为整数且已约成最简分数。则 p² = 2q²，p² 为偶数，故 p 为偶数，设 p = 2k。代入得 4k² = 2q²，即 q² = 2k²，q 也是偶数。p、q 都是偶数，与“最简分数”矛盾，所以这样的分数不存在。

image.en: A student chalks the assumption √2 = p/q, in lowest terms, on the blackboard and starts calculating. A lightning bolt of contradiction strikes the board, p and q both turn out to be even, and the student topples over backwards. The teacher in a mortarboard cheers. Beside the board a signpost shows the two roads to a theorem: the direct one and the one through contradiction.
image.zh: 学生在黑板上写下假设“√2 = p/q（最简分数）”，埋头推算。一道矛盾的闪电劈中黑板：p 和 q 竟然都是偶数，学生仰面摔倒。戴学位帽的老师欢呼起来。黑板旁的路标指向通往定理的两条路：直接证明与反证法。

means.en: the assumption that the claim is false
the contradiction: p and q both even despite lowest terms
means.zh: 矛盾：最简分数的分子分母竟都为偶数

means.en: the false assumption collapses, so √2 is irrational
means.zh: 错误假设崩塌，所以 √2 是无理数

means.en: two routes: direct (or contrapositive) proof and contradiction
means.zh: 两条路：直接（或逆否）证明与反证法

summary.en: Prove P(1), then prove P(k) ⇒ P(k + 1) for every k ≥ 1; together they give P(n) for all n ≥ 1, like falling dominoes.
summary.zh: 先证 P(1)，再证对每个 k≥1 有 P(k)⇒P(k+1)，二者合起来就得到所有 n 的 P(n)，像多米诺骨牌依次倒下。

explain.en: To prove a statement P(n) for all integers n ≥ n₀, prove the base case P(n₀), then the inductive step: for every k ≥ n₀, if P(k) holds then P(k + 1) holds. The assumption P(k) inside the step is the inductive hypothesis. Like dominoes, the first falls and each knocks over the next, so all fall. Both parts are needed, and the step must work for every k, including the smallest. The classic fake proof that all horses are the same colour breaks exactly there: going from 1 horse to 2, the two groups of one horse each do not overlap, so nothing links their colours. Induction is the standard tool for sums, inequalities, recursive algorithms and loop invariants.
explain.zh: 要证明对所有 n≥n₀ 都有 P(n)，先证基础情形 P(n₀)，再证归纳步骤：对每个 k≥n₀，若 P(k) 成立则 P(k+1) 成立。步骤中假设的 P(k) 叫归纳假设。就像多米诺骨牌：第一块倒下，每一块又推倒下一块，于是全部倒下。两部分缺一不可，而且步骤必须对每个 k 都成立，包括最小的那个。著名的伪证“所有马颜色相同”正坏在这里：从 1 匹马到 2 匹马时，两组各 1 匹马互不重叠，没有什么能把它们的颜色联系起来。归纳法是证明求和公式、不等式、递归算法和循环不变式的标准工具。

example.en: Claim: 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2. Base case: n = 1 gives 1 = 1·2/2. Step: assume 1 + … + k = k(k + 1)/2. Then 1 + … + k + (k + 1) = k(k + 1)/2 + (k + 1) = (k + 1)(k + 2)/2, which is the formula for n = k + 1. So it holds for every n ≥ 1; for n = 100 the sum is 5050.

image.en: A giant finger rises from the classroom floor and flicks the first of a long row of dominoes, and each one topples into the next, all the way down the line. At the far end two horses, one chestnut and one white, stand apart and refuse to match: the bogus proof that all horses are the same colour broke at its very first step, from one horse to two.
image.zh: 一根巨大的手指从教室地板伸出，弹倒了长长一排多米诺骨牌的第一块，每一块又撞倒下一块，一路倒到底。队尾站着两匹马，一匹栗色、一匹白色，各站一边，偏不一样：那个“所有马颜色都相同”的伪证，在最初从 1 匹到 2 匹的那一步就断了。

thing.en: the finger flicking the first domino

means.en: the base case P(1)
the inductive step P(k) ⇒ P(k + 1), for every k
P(n) holds for every n
the 'all horses one colour' fake: its step fails from 1 to 2
means.zh: “马同色”伪证：从 1 到 2 的步骤失效

summary.en: In the inductive step you may assume P(k) for every k < n, not only for n − 1; this is equivalent to the well-ordering principle.
summary.zh: 归纳步骤中可以假设所有 k<n 的 P(k) 都成立，而不只是 n−1；它与良序原理等价。

explain.en: Strong (complete) induction proves P(n) for all n ≥ n₀ by showing that P(k) for every k with n₀ ≤ k < n implies P(n); for n = n₀ nothing is assumed, so this includes the base case. Use it when case n depends on cases further back than n − 1. The standard example: every integer n ≥ 2 is a product of primes. If n is prime, done; otherwise n = ab with 2 ≤ a, b < n, both factor by hypothesis, so n does too. The well-ordering principle says every non-empty set of natural numbers has a least element. It is equivalent to induction and gives proofs by minimal counterexample: if some n ≥ 2 had no factorization, the least such n is not prime, so n = ab with smaller a and b that do factor, a contradiction.
explain.zh: 强归纳法（完全归纳法）：只要“对所有 n₀≤k<n 都有 P(k)”能推出 P(n)，就对所有 n≥n₀ 都有 P(n)；n=n₀ 时什么也不假设，基础情形已包含在内。当第 n 步要依赖比 n−1 更早的情形时就用它。标准例子：每个整数 n≥2 都是素数之积。若 n 是素数，结论成立；否则 n=ab，2≤a,b<n，由归纳假设 a、b 都能分解，于是 n 也能。良序原理说：自然数的每个非空子集都有最小元。它与归纳法等价，并带来“最小反例”式证明：若有不能分解的 n≥2，取最小的那个，它不是素数，n=ab 中更小的 a、b 却能分解，矛盾。

example.en: Factor 60 the strong-induction way: 60 is not prime, so 60 = 6 × 10. Neither 6 nor 10 is 59, so the single step back of ordinary induction would not help, but both are smaller than 60: 6 = 2 × 3 and 10 = 2 × 5. Hence 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. Another classic: every postage of n ≥ 12 cents can be paid with 4- and 5-cent stamps, using the base cases 12, 13, 14, 15 and the step from n − 4 to n.
example.zh: 按强归纳的思路分解 60：60 不是素数，60 = 6×10。6 和 10 都不是 59，普通归纳“只退一步”帮不上忙，但它们都小于 60：6 = 2×3，10 = 2×5，所以 60 = 2×2×3×5。另一个经典例子：12 分及以上的邮资都能用 4 分和 5 分邮票凑出，基础情形取 12、13、14、15，再从 n−4 推到 n。

image.en: In the classroom a geologist in a hard hat swings her hammer at a huge boulder, the number 60. It splits into two smaller rocks, 6 and 10, and these crack into four glittering crystals, 2 and 3, 2 and 5, that no hammer can split again. Every blow gives smaller rocks of any size, and each smaller one is already known to end in crystals.
image.zh: 教室里，戴安全帽的地质学家抡锤砸向一块巨石，它是数字 60。巨石裂成两块小石头 6 和 10，它们又裂成四颗闪亮的晶体 2 和 3、2 和 5，再也砸不开。每砸一次都得到大小不一的更小石块，而每块更小的石头都早已知道最终会碎成晶体。

means.en: case n: either prime or n = ab with smaller a, b
means.zh: 第 n 种情形：要么是素数，要么 n=ab 且 a、b 更小

means.en: smaller cases of any size, all covered by the strong hypothesis
means.zh: 任意更小的情形，都由强归纳假设覆盖

means.en: well-ordering: no endless descent in the naturals
means.zh: 良序原理：自然数不能无限下降

summary.en: Sets and functions are the material mathematics is built from; comparing sets by bijections reveals that infinity comes in different sizes.
summary.zh: 集合与函数是构建数学的材料；用双射比较集合的大小，会发现无穷也分大小。

summary.en: Sets, the maps between them and the relations that sort them, handled like the mail.
summary.zh: 集合、集合之间的映射，以及给元素分类的关系，像邮件一样分拣投递。

summary.en: A set is determined by its members; union, intersection, difference, complement and product build new sets, and n elements have 2ⁿ subsets.
summary.zh: 集合由其元素决定；并、交、差、补与笛卡儿积构造新集合，n 元集合有 2ⁿ 个子集。

explain.en: A set is a collection of distinct objects, determined by its members alone: order and repetition do not matter. x ∈ A means x is a member; A ⊆ B means every member of A is in B, and A = B exactly when A ⊆ B and B ⊆ A. The basic operations are union A ∪ B (in either), intersection A ∩ B (in both), difference A ∖ B (in A but not B) and complement Aᶜ (relative to a universe U). The Cartesian product A × B is the set of ordered pairs (a, b), and |A × B| = |A|·|B|. The power set P(A) is the set of all subsets of A; if |A| = n it has 2ⁿ members, since each element is either in or out of a subset. These operations obey the same laws as the logical connectives.
explain.zh: 集合是一些互不相同的对象的总体，只由其元素决定，与顺序和重复无关。x∈A 表示 x 是 A 的元素；A⊆B 表示 A 的每个元素都在 B 中，A=B 当且仅当 A⊆B 且 B⊆A。基本运算有并 A∪B（属于其一）、交 A∩B（同时属于）、差 A∖B（属于 A 而不属于 B）和补 Aᶜ（相对于全集 U）。笛卡儿积 A×B 是全部有序对 (a,b) 的集合，|A×B| = |A|·|B|。幂集 P(A) 是 A 的全部子集组成的集合；若 |A|=n，它有 2ⁿ 个元素，因为每个元素要么在子集里、要么不在。这些运算遵循与逻辑联结词相同的规律。

example.en: Let A = {1, 2, 3} and B = {2, 3, 4}. Then A ∪ B = {1, 2, 3, 4}, A ∩ B = {2, 3} and A ∖ B = {1}; in the universe U = {1, …, 5} the complement of A ∪ B is {5}. A × B has 3 · 3 = 9 pairs. P(A) has 2³ = 8 members: ∅, {1}, {2}, {3}, {1, 2}, {1, 3}, {2, 3} and {1, 2, 3}.

image.en: On the post-office floor a red rug for fragile parcels overlaps a blue rug for express ones. Two parcels sit on red only, two on blue only, and a gold parcel sits right in the overlap: fragile and express at once. One lost grey parcel lies outside both rugs, sniffed by a dog, while a postal clerk scratches his head over where it belongs.
image.zh: 邮局地板上，放易碎件的红地毯和放加急件的蓝地毯部分重叠。两个包裹只在红毯上，两个只在蓝毯上，一个金色包裹正好压在重叠处：既易碎又加急。还有一个灰色包裹孤零零地躺在两块地毯之外，一只狗凑过去嗅，邮局职员挠着头，不知该把它放哪儿。

means.en: the sets A and B

thing.en: the gold parcel in the overlap

means.en: A ∩ B: in both sets
A ∪ B; the red-only parcels form A ∖ B
means.zh: A∪B；只在红毯上的构成 A∖B

means.en: the complement (A ∪ B)ᶜ within the universe

summary.en: A function sends each input to exactly one output; injective means no two inputs share an output, surjective means every output is hit.
summary.zh: 函数让每个输入恰好对应一个输出；单射指不同输入不共用输出，满射指每个输出都被取到。

explain.en: A function f: A → B assigns to every a in the domain A exactly one f(a) in the codomain B. It is injective (one-to-one) if f(a) = f(a′) forces a = a′, surjective (onto) if every b ∈ B equals f(a) for some a, and bijective if both. Composition (g ∘ f)(a) = g(f(a)) preserves each property: composites of injections are injective, composites of surjections surjective. A function has an inverse f⁻¹, with f⁻¹ ∘ f = id_A and f ∘ f⁻¹ = id_B, exactly when it is a bijection. For finite sets an injection A → B needs |A| ≤ |B|, which is the pigeonhole principle, and a surjection needs |A| ≥ |B|. Bijections are how sizes are compared, even for infinite sets.
explain.zh: 函数 f: A→B 给定义域 A 中每个 a 指定陪域 B 中唯一的 f(a)。若 f(a)=f(a′) 必有 a=a′，称为单射（injective）；若 B 中每个 b 都等于某个 f(a)，称为满射（surjective）；两者兼备称为双射（bijective）。复合 (g∘f)(a)=g(f(a)) 保持这些性质：单射的复合仍是单射，满射的复合仍是满射。f 有逆 f⁻¹（满足 f⁻¹∘f=id_A、f∘f⁻¹=id_B）当且仅当 f 是双射。对有限集，单射 A→B 要求 |A|≤|B|，这就是鸽巢原理；满射要求 |A|≥|B|。比较集合的大小，包括无穷集合，靠的正是双射。

example.en: On the integers, f(n) = 2n is injective but not surjective, since 3 is never hit. g(n) = ⌊n/2⌋ is surjective but not injective, since g(4) = g(5) = 2. h(n) = n + 1 is a bijection with inverse h⁻¹(n) = n − 1. On the reals, x ↦ x³ is a bijection, while x ↦ x² is neither injective (2 and −2 collide) nor surjective (−1 is missed).
example.zh: 在整数上，f(n)=2n 是单射但不是满射（取不到 3）；g(n)=⌊n/2⌋ 是满射但不是单射（g(4)=g(5)=2）；h(n)=n+1 是双射，逆为 h⁻¹(n)=n−1。在实数上，x↦x³ 是双射，而 x↦x² 既非单射（2 与 −2 撞到一起）也非满射（取不到 −1）。

image.en: A postman has delivered four letters to four red post boxes. The first two boxes hold one letter each, the third has two letters jammed on top, and the fourth is empty, with a dog waiting forlornly beside it. Now he is told to run his round backwards and take exactly one letter back from each box. He scratches his head: one box offers two letters and another has none.
image.zh: 邮递员把四封信投进了四个红色邮筒：前两个各一封，第三个上面硬塞着两封，第四个空空如也，一只狗守在旁边眼巴巴地等。现在要他把投递路线倒着走一遍，从每个邮筒恰好取回一封信。他挠起了头：一个邮筒有两封可选，另一个一封也没有。

means.en: a function: each letter goes to exactly one box
means.zh: 函数：每封信恰好进一个邮筒

means.en: not injective: two inputs share an output
means.zh: 不是单射：两个输入共用一个输出

thing.en: the empty box and the waiting dog

means.en: not surjective: an output that nothing maps to
means.zh: 不是满射：有输出没有原像

means.en: an inverse exists only for a bijection

summary.en: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; its equivalence classes split the set into disjoint pieces.
summary.zh: 满足自反、对称、传递的关系；它的等价类把集合分成互不相交的若干块。

explain.en: A relation ~ on a set A is an equivalence relation if it is reflexive (a ~ a), symmetric (a ~ b implies b ~ a) and transitive (a ~ b and b ~ c imply a ~ c). The equivalence class of a is [a] = {x ∈ A : x ~ a}. Two classes are either identical or disjoint, and every element lies in its own class, so the classes partition A. Conversely, every partition of A defines an equivalence relation: 'in the same block'. Equivalence relations make precise the idea of 'the same in the respects we care about'. The main example is congruence mod n on the integers, whose n classes correspond to the remainders 0, 1, …, n − 1; others are 'same postcode', 'same parity' and similarity of matrices.
explain.zh: 集合 A 上的关系 ~ 若满足自反性（a~a）、对称性（a~b 则 b~a）和传递性（a~b 且 b~c 则 a~c），就是等价关系。a 的等价类是 [a] = {x∈A : x~a}。任意两个等价类要么相同、要么不相交，而每个元素都在自己的类里，所以等价类构成 A 的一个划分。反过来，A 的每个划分也定义一个等价关系：“在同一块里”。等价关系把“在我们关心的方面相同”说得精确。最重要的例子是整数上的模 n 同余，它的 n 个类对应余数 0, 1, …, n−1；其他例子有“邮编相同”、“奇偶性相同”、矩阵相似等。

example.en: Congruence mod 3 on ℤ: a ~ b when 3 divides a − b. Reflexive: 3 | 0. Symmetric: if 3 | a − b then 3 | b − a. Transitive: a − c = (a − b) + (b − c). The classes are [0] = {…, −3, 0, 3, 6, …}, [1] = {…, −2, 1, 4, 7, …} and [2] = {…, −1, 2, 5, 8, …}; every integer is in exactly one. A non-example: 'differs by at most 1' is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive, since 0 ~ 1 and 1 ~ 2 but not 0 ~ 2.

image.en: In the sorting hall parcels ride a conveyor belt from left to right. At the end an industrial robot arm reads the number on each parcel and, by its remainder mod 3, drops it into one of three baskets: red, green or blue. Every parcel lands in exactly one basket, and no two baskets share a parcel: the baskets split the whole mail into classes.
image.zh: 分拣大厅里，包裹在传送带上从左往右移动。尽头的工业机械臂读出每个包裹上的数字，按除以 3 的余数把它丢进红、绿、蓝三个筐之一。每个包裹恰好落进一个筐，任何两个筐都没有共用的包裹：三个筐把全部邮件分成了三类。

means.en: elements of the set ℤ
the relation a ~ b ⇔ 3 | a − b
the classes [0], [1], [2]

thing.en: each parcel in exactly one basket

means.en: the classes partition the set
means.zh: 等价类构成集合的划分

summary.en: Infinite sets compared by bijections: some infinities are countable, others are strictly larger.
summary.zh: 用双射比较无穷集合：有的无穷可数，有的严格更大。

title.zh: 可数集与希尔伯特旅馆

summary.en: Two sets have the same size when a bijection pairs them up; ℕ, ℤ and ℚ all have the same size, called countable.
summary.zh: 两个集合之间存在双射就算一样大；ℕ、ℤ、ℚ 都一样大，称为可数集。

explain.en: Sets A and B have the same cardinality, |A| = |B|, if there is a bijection between them. A set is countably infinite if it has the cardinality of ℕ, that is, if its elements can be listed as a₁, a₂, a₃, … with every element appearing; countable means finite or countably infinite. Infinite sets defy intuition: a set can be the same size as a proper subset of itself. In Hilbert's Hotel, with infinitely many rooms all full, a new guest still fits: everyone moves from room n to room n + 1, and room 1 is free. Infinitely many new guests fit too, if each guest moves from room n to room 2n. ℤ is countable (list 0, 1, −1, 2, −2, …), and so is ℚ: walk through the grid of fractions p/q and skip repeats.
explain.zh: 若 A、B 之间存在双射，就说它们基数相同，|A| = |B|。与 ℕ 基数相同的集合叫可数无穷集，即它的元素可以排成 a₁, a₂, a₃, … 而一个不漏；有限或可数无穷统称可数。无穷集合违反直觉：它可以和自己的真子集一样大。希尔伯特旅馆有无穷多个房间且全部住满，新来一位客人照样能住下：每位客人从 n 号房搬到 n+1 号房，1 号房就空出来了。来了无穷多位新客人也不怕，让每人从 n 号搬到 2n 号即可。ℤ 可数（按 0, 1, −1, 2, −2, … 排列），ℚ 也可数：走遍分数 p/q 的网格并跳过重复。

example.en: A bijection from ℕ = {0, 1, 2, …} to ℤ: send n to n/2 if n is even and to −(n + 1)/2 if n is odd, giving 0, −1, 1, −2, 2, …. For ℚ, list the positive fractions by p + q: 1/1; 1/2, 2/1; 1/3, 3/1 (skipping 2/2); 1/4, 2/3, 3/2, 4/1; …. Every positive fraction appears at a finite position, and interleaving 0 and the negatives covers all of ℚ.
example.zh: ℕ={0,1,2,…} 到 ℤ 的双射：n 为偶数时映到 n/2，为奇数时映到 −(n+1)/2，得到 0, −1, 1, −2, 2, …。对 ℚ，按 p+q 由小到大列出正分数：1/1；1/2, 2/1；1/3, 3/1（跳过 2/2）；1/4, 2/3, 3/2, 4/1；……每个正分数都出现在有限位置上，再穿插 0 和负数，就覆盖了整个 ℚ。

image.en: In the Hall of Mirrors a corridor of hotel doors runs on forever in the reflections, and every room is taken. A new guest arrives holding a room key. The bellhop waves and shouts, 'Everyone move from room n to room n + 1!', and three guests step sideways to the next door at once, leaving room 1 free for the newcomer.
image.zh: 镜厅里，一排旅馆房门在镜中的倒影里无穷无尽地延伸，每间都住满了。一位新客人拿着钥匙到来。门童挥手大喊：“所有人从 n 号房搬到 n+1 号房！”三位客人同时侧身走向下一扇门，1 号房空了出来，留给新客人。

means.en: rooms 1, 2, 3, …: the set ℕ

thing.en: guests stepping to the next door

means.en: the bijection n ↦ n + 1 from ℕ onto ℕ ∖ {1}
means.zh: 双射 n↦n+1：ℕ 与 ℕ∖{1} 一一对应

means.en: a full infinite set still has room: one more element, same size
means.zh: 住满的无穷集合还能再加一个，大小不变

means.en: an infinite set can match a proper part of itself
means.zh: 无穷集合可以与自己的真子集一样大

summary.en: No list of real numbers can be complete: change the n-th digit of the n-th number and you get a real number missing from the list.
summary.zh: 任何实数列表都不可能完整：改掉第 n 个数的第 n 位，就得到一个不在表中的实数。

explain.en: Suppose the reals in (0, 1) could be listed as r₁, r₂, r₃, … with decimal expansions rₙ = 0.dₙ₁dₙ₂dₙ₃…. Build x = 0.x₁x₂x₃… by choosing xₙ = 4 if dₙₙ = 5 and xₙ = 5 otherwise. Then x differs from rₙ in the n-th digit for every n, so x is not on the list. Using only the digits 4 and 5 avoids the one ambiguity of decimals, numbers with two expansions such as 0.0999… = 0.1000…, because x has a unique expansion. So no list covers (0, 1): ℝ is uncountable, and |ℕ| < |ℝ|. The same diagonal trick proves Cantor's theorem, and in computer science it shows that the halting problem is undecidable.
explain.zh: 假设 (0,1) 中的实数能排成 r₁, r₂, r₃, …，其小数展开为 rₙ = 0.dₙ₁dₙ₂dₙ₃…。构造 x = 0.x₁x₂x₃…：若 dₙₙ = 5 则取 xₙ = 4，否则取 xₙ = 5。于是对每个 n，x 与 rₙ 在第 n 位不同，x 不在表中。只用数字 4 和 5，是为了避开小数表示唯一的歧义——有些数有两种写法，如 0.0999… = 0.1000…，而 x 的展开是唯一的。所以没有列表能覆盖 (0,1)：ℝ 不可数，|ℕ| < |ℝ|。同样的对角线技巧能证明康托尔定理，在计算机科学中还能证明停机问题不可判定。

example.en: Take a list that starts r₁ = 0.1415…, r₂ = 0.2500…, r₃ = 0.7182…, r₄ = 0.3333…. The diagonal digits are 1, 5, 8, 3. Replace the 5 by 4 and every other digit by 5: x = 0.5455…. It differs from r₁ in digit 1, from r₂ in digit 2, from r₃ in digit 3 and from r₄ in digit 4, and, continuing the rule down the list, from every rₙ in digit n.
example.zh: 设列表开头为 r₁=0.1415…，r₂=0.2500…，r₃=0.7182…，r₄=0.3333…。对角线上的数字是 1、5、8、3。把 5 换成 4，其余都换成 5，得 x = 0.5455…。它与 r₁ 第 1 位不同，与 r₂ 第 2 位不同，与 r₃ 第 3 位、r₄ 第 4 位不同；照此规则一路向下，它与每个 rₙ 都在第 n 位不同。

image.en: A gentleman in a top hat shows off his 'complete' list of real numbers on a big board of digits, row after row. A girl with a pencil walks down the diagonal, changing every digit she meets: 5 becomes 4, anything else becomes 5. Above the board her new number lights up in neon, 0.5455…, and the gentleman scratches his head: it is on none of his rows.
image.zh: 戴礼帽的绅士在一块写满数字的大板上展示他“完整”的实数列表，一行接一行。一个拿铅笔的女孩沿对角线走下来，见到哪一位就改哪一位：5 改成 4，其余都改成 5。大板上方，她的新数亮起霓虹：0.5455…。绅士挠着头：哪一行都不是它。

means.en: a supposed list of all reals in (0, 1), one per row
means.zh: 假想中 (0,1) 全部实数的列表，每行一个

means.en: look at the n-th digit of the n-th number
means.zh: 看第 n 个数的第 n 位

means.en: change that digit; only 4s and 5s avoid 0.0999… = 0.1000…
a real that differs from every row: ℝ is uncountable
means.zh: 与每行都不同的实数：ℝ 不可数

summary.en: For every set A, the power set P(A) is strictly larger: no function from A onto P(A) exists, so infinities come in endless sizes.
summary.zh: 对任意集合 A，幂集 P(A) 都严格更大：不存在 A 到 P(A) 的满射，所以无穷的大小没有尽头。

explain.en: Cantor's theorem: for every set A, |A| < |P(A)|. The map a ↦ {a} is an injection, so |A| ≤ |P(A)|. To see that no f: A → P(A) is onto, form the diagonal set D = {a ∈ A : a ∉ f(a)}. If D = f(d) for some d, then d ∈ D exactly when d ∉ f(d) = D, which is impossible. So D is never hit. Applied repeatedly, ℕ, P(ℕ), P(P(ℕ)), … have strictly increasing sizes: there is no largest infinity. Since |P(ℕ)| = |ℝ|, the uncountability of ℝ is a special case. The same self-reference drives Russell's paradox and the halting problem. Whether some size lies strictly between |ℕ| and |ℝ| is the continuum hypothesis, which the standard axioms (ZFC) can neither prove nor refute.
explain.zh: 康托尔定理：对任意集合 A，|A| < |P(A)|。映射 a↦{a} 是单射，所以 |A| ≤ |P(A)|。要说明任何 f: A→P(A) 都不是满射，构造对角集 D = {a∈A : a∉f(a)}。若 D = f(d)，则 d∈D 当且仅当 d∉f(d) = D，矛盾。所以 D 永远取不到。反复应用，ℕ、P(ℕ)、P(P(ℕ))、… 的大小严格递增：不存在最大的无穷。由于 |P(ℕ)| = |ℝ|，ℝ 不可数只是它的特例。同样的自指结构也出现在罗素悖论和停机问题中。|ℕ| 与 |ℝ| 之间是否还有别的大小，就是连续统假设，标准公理系统 ZFC 既不能证明也不能否定它。

example.en: Let A = {1, 2, 3} with f(1) = {1, 3}, f(2) = {1} and f(3) = ∅. Then 1 ∈ f(1), but 2 ∉ f(2) and 3 ∉ f(3), so D = {2, 3}. D differs from f(1) at 1, from f(2) at 2 and from f(3) at 3, so f misses D. In general a set of n elements has 2ⁿ > n subsets.

image.en: Three guests each own a mirror that shows a group of guests. Annie appears in her own mirror; Bob and Carl are missing from theirs. A pale ghost of the 'missing club', Bob and Carl, drifts from mirror to mirror and finds itself in none: a mirror showing it would have to include its owner exactly when it doesn't. In front, three infinity loops stand in a row, each bigger than the last.
image.zh: 三位客人各有一面镜子，镜中映出一群客人。安妮在自己的镜子里看得见自己；鲍勃和卡尔却在各自的镜子里找不到自己。他俩组成的“缺席俱乐部”化作一个苍白的幽灵，从一面镜子飘到另一面，却哪面都照不出它：若有镜子映出它，镜子的主人就会既在其中又不在其中。前方立着三个无穷符号，一个比一个大。

means.en: a function f: A → P(A) giving each a a subset f(a)
means.zh: 函数 f: A→P(A)，给每个 a 一个子集 f(a)

thing.en: the ghost of the missing club

means.en: the diagonal set D = {a : a ∉ f(a)}, which no mirror shows
means.zh: 对角集 D={a : a∉f(a)}，没有镜子映得出

summary.en: Integers, remainders and primes, the modular arithmetic built on them, and the algebraic structures behind it all, up to RSA.
summary.zh: 整数、余数与素数，建立其上的模运算，以及背后的代数结构，一直通到 RSA。

summary.en: Division with remainder, greatest common divisors and primes, counted out at a market stall.
summary.zh: 带余除法、最大公约数与素数，在集市摊位上一一清点。

summary.en: For integers a and b > 0 there are unique q and r with a = qb + r and 0 ≤ r < b; b divides a exactly when r = 0.
summary.zh: 对整数 a 与 b>0，存在唯一的 q、r 使 a = qb + r 且 0 ≤ r < b；r = 0 时 b 整除 a。

explain.en: Division with remainder: for any integer a and any integer b > 0 there are unique integers q, the quotient, and r, the remainder, with a = qb + r and 0 ≤ r < b. Existence: take q = ⌊a/b⌋, the largest q with qb ≤ a; then r = a − qb lies in [0, b). Uniqueness: if qb + r = q′b + r′, then b divides r − r′, which lies strictly between −b and b, so r = r′ and q = q′. We say b divides a, written b | a, when a = kb for some integer k, which happens exactly when r = 0. The theorem drives Euclid's algorithm, positional notation and modular arithmetic. Languages differ on negative a: Python follows the theorem, while C truncates toward zero.
explain.zh: 带余除法：对任意整数 a 和整数 b>0，存在唯一的整数 q（商）和 r（余数），使 a = qb + r 且 0 ≤ r < b。存在性：取 q = ⌊a/b⌋，即满足 qb ≤ a 的最大整数，则 r = a − qb 落在 [0, b) 内。唯一性：若 qb + r = q′b + r′，则 b 整除 r − r′，而 r − r′ 严格介于 −b 与 b 之间，故 r = r′、q = q′。若 a = kb（k 为整数），称 b 整除 a，记作 b | a，这恰好等价于 r = 0。该定理是欧几里得算法、进位制和模运算的基础。对负数 a，编程语言各有约定：Python 符合该定理，C 则向零截断。

example.en: 14 eggs packed in nests of 4: 14 = 3 · 4 + 2, so q = 3 full nests and r = 2 eggs left over, with 2 < 4. With 12 eggs, 12 = 3 · 4 + 0, so 4 | 12. For negative a: −7 = (−3) · 3 + 2, so q = −3 and r = 2. Python's divmod(−7, 3) gives (−3, 2), while in C −7 / 3 is −2 and −7 % 3 is −1.

image.en: At an egg stall a proud duck has laid 14 eggs. The farmer packs them four to a nest: three full nests sit in a row, and two leftover eggs roll on the cobbles in front, too few to fill a fourth nest. The farmer kneels beside them, and the duck eyes the leftovers as if planning to lay two more.
image.zh: 蛋摊上，一只得意的鸭子下了 14 个蛋。农夫每窝装 4 个：三个装满的鸟巢排成一排，剩下两个蛋滚落在前面的石板上，凑不满第四窝。农夫跪在一旁，鸭子盯着这两个蛋，像是打算再下两个补上。

means.en: the quotient q = 3
the divisor b = 4
the remainder r = 2, always less than b

title.zh: 最大公约数、欧几里得算法与裴蜀定理

summary.en: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b) until the remainder hits 0; running the steps backwards writes gcd(a, b) as ax + by.
summary.zh: 反复令 gcd(a,b)=gcd(b, a mod b)，直到余数为 0；倒推各步，可得 gcd(a,b)=ax+by。

explain.en: The greatest common divisor gcd(a, b) is the largest integer dividing both a and b. Euclid's algorithm rests on one fact: if a = qb + r, the common divisors of a and b are exactly those of b and r, so gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, r). Replace (a, b) by (b, a mod b) until the remainder is 0; the last non-zero remainder is the gcd. The remainders at least halve every two steps, so it takes O(log min(a, b)) steps. Back-substitution gives Bézout's identity: there are integers x, y with ax + by = gcd(a, b), and gcd(a, b) is the smallest positive number of that form. The extended algorithm computes x and y; it is how modular inverses are found, for example in RSA.
explain.zh: 最大公约数 gcd(a,b) 是同时整除 a 与 b 的最大整数。欧几里得算法（辗转相除法）基于一个事实：若 a = qb + r，则 a、b 的公约数恰好就是 b、r 的公约数，所以 gcd(a,b) = gcd(b,r)。不断把 (a,b) 换成 (b, a mod b)，直到余数为 0，最后一个非零余数就是最大公约数。余数每两步至少减半，所以只需 O(log min(a,b)) 步。把各步倒推回去得到裴蜀等式（Bézout's identity）：存在整数 x、y 使 ax + by = gcd(a,b)，而且 gcd(a,b) 是这种形式的最小正整数。扩展欧几里得算法算出 x、y，求模逆元（例如在 RSA 中）就靠它。

image.en: An oil merchant's containers shrink along the stall: a huge barrel of 240, a bucket of 46, a jar of 10, a mug of 6, a small flask of 4 and, on a crate, a tiny golden cup of 2. Each new container holds what is left over from measuring the pair before it: 240 by 46 leaves 10, 46 by 10 leaves 6, then 4, then 2. The golden cup measures the flask exactly, so it is the last, and the merchant points at it in triumph.
image.zh: 油商的容器在摊位上越排越小：240 的大桶、46 的水桶、10 的罐子、6 的杯子、4 的小瓶，最后是木箱上 2 的金色小盅。从罐子起，每个容器装的都是前面两个容器相量后剩下的油：240 用 46 量剩 10，46 用 10 量剩 6，接着剩 4、剩 2。金盅正好量尽小瓶，于是到此为止，油商得意地指着它。

means.en: the inputs a and b
the successive remainders 10, 6, 4, 2
the last non-zero remainder: gcd(240, 46) = 2
the gcd divides a, b and every remainder; 2 = 47·46 − 9·240
means.zh: gcd 整除 a、b 和每个余数；2 = 47·46 − 9·240

summary.en: Every integer greater than 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, up to order, and there are infinitely many primes.
summary.zh: 每个大于 1 的整数都能唯一地（不计顺序）写成素数之积，而素数有无穷多个。

explain.en: A prime is an integer p > 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and p. Euclid's lemma: if a prime p divides ab, then p divides a or p divides b. (If p ∤ a, Bézout gives 1 = ax + py, so b = abx + pby is a multiple of p.) The fundamental theorem of arithmetic: every integer n > 1 is a product of primes, uniquely up to order. Existence follows by strong induction; uniqueness follows from Euclid's lemma, since a prime dividing one factorization must equal a prime of the other. Euclid also proved there are infinitely many primes: for any finite list p₁, …, pₖ, the number N = p₁⋯pₖ + 1 leaves remainder 1 when divided by each pᵢ, so its prime factors are not on the list.
explain.zh: 素数是只有 1 和自身两个正因数的整数 p>1。欧几里得引理：若素数 p 整除 ab，则 p 整除 a 或 p 整除 b（若 p∤a，由裴蜀等式 1 = ax + py，于是 b = abx + pby 是 p 的倍数）。算术基本定理：每个整数 n>1 都能写成素数之积，且不计顺序时写法唯一。存在性由强归纳法得到；唯一性来自欧几里得引理：整除一种分解的素数，必等于另一种分解中的某个素数。欧几里得还证明了素数有无穷多个：对任意有限个素数 p₁,…,pₖ，数 N = p₁⋯pₖ + 1 除以每个 pᵢ 都余 1，所以它的素因数都不在表中。

example.en: 360 = 2³ · 3² · 5, and no other product of primes gives 360. Euclid's construction: 2·3·5·7 + 1 = 211, which is itself prime. But N need not be prime: 2·3·5·7·11·13 + 1 = 30031 = 59 · 509, whose factors are new primes. Uniqueness can fail in other number systems: among numbers a + b√−5, 6 = 2 · 3 = (1 + √−5)(1 − √−5).
example.zh: 360 = 2³·3²·5，再没有别的素数乘积等于 360。欧几里得的构造：2·3·5·7 + 1 = 211，本身就是素数。但 N 不一定是素数：2·3·5·7·11·13 + 1 = 30031 = 59·509，它的因数是表外的新素数。在别的数系里唯一分解可能失效：在形如 a + b√−5 的数中，6 = 2·3 = (1+√−5)(1−√−5)。

image.en: A spice merchant boasts that his four jars hold every prime there is: 2, 3, 5 and 7. A girl tips all four into a big golden cauldron, multiplying them together, then tosses in one extra apple: plus one. A brand-new star rises glowing out of the brew, 211, a prime from none of his jars. The merchant shrugs: his collection can never be complete.
image.zh: 香料商夸口说，他的四个罐子装着世上所有的素数：2、3、5、7。一个女孩把四罐全倒进金色大锅里相乘，又丢进一个苹果：再加一。锅里升起一颗闪亮的新星——211，哪个罐子里都没有它。香料商只能耸肩：他的收藏永远不可能齐全。

means.en: a supposedly complete finite list p₁, …, pₖ
means.zh: 假想中完整的有限素数表 p₁,…,pₖ

means.en: N = p₁⋯pₖ + 1, remainder 1 on division by each pᵢ
means.zh: N = p₁⋯pₖ + 1，除以每个 pᵢ 都余 1

means.en: a prime factor of N not on the list: infinitely many primes
means.zh: N 的素因数不在表中：素数有无穷多个

means.en: no finite list of primes is complete
means.zh: 任何有限素数表都不完整

summary.en: Arithmetic on a clock: congruences, Fermat and Euler, the Chinese remainder theorem, and RSA.
summary.zh: 钟面上的算术：同余、费马与欧拉定理、中国剩余定理，以及 RSA。

summary.en: a ≡ b (mod n) when n divides a − b; arithmetic mod n wraps around like a clock, and a is invertible mod n exactly when gcd(a, n) = 1.
summary.zh: n 整除 a−b 时记 a ≡ b (mod n)；模 n 运算像钟面一样绕圈，a 模 n 可逆当且仅当 gcd(a,n)=1。

explain.en: For an integer n ≥ 1, a ≡ b (mod n) means that n divides a − b, that is, a and b leave the same remainder on division by n. Congruence is an equivalence relation, and it respects arithmetic: if a ≡ a′ and b ≡ b′, then a + b ≡ a′ + b′ and ab ≡ a′b′. So we can compute with the n remainders 0, …, n − 1, which wrap around like the hours on a clock; this is ℤₙ. Division is subtler: a has a multiplicative inverse mod n, a number x with ax ≡ 1, exactly when gcd(a, n) = 1, and the extended Euclidean algorithm finds it. The linear congruence ax ≡ b (mod n) is solvable exactly when d = gcd(a, n) divides b, and then it has d solutions mod n.
explain.zh: 对整数 n≥1，a ≡ b (mod n) 指 n 整除 a−b，即 a、b 除以 n 的余数相同。同余是等价关系，并且与运算相容：若 a≡a′、b≡b′，则 a+b ≡ a′+b′，ab ≡ a′b′。所以可以只用 n 个余数 0,…,n−1 来计算，它们像钟面上的钟点一样绕圈，这就是 ℤₙ。除法要小心：a 在模 n 下有乘法逆元（满足 ax≡1 的 x）当且仅当 gcd(a,n)=1，可用扩展欧几里得算法求出。线性同余方程 ax ≡ b (mod n) 有解当且仅当 d = gcd(a,n) 整除 b，此时模 n 下恰有 d 个解。

example.en: On a 12-hour clock, 10 + 5 = 15 ≡ 3: a five-hour trip that leaves at 10 arrives at 3. Since 3 · 5 = 15 ≡ 1 (mod 7), 3⁻¹ ≡ 5 (mod 7). To solve 3x ≡ 4 (mod 7), multiply by 5: x ≡ 20 ≡ 6, and indeed 3 · 6 = 18 ≡ 4. But 2 has no inverse mod 4, since 2x is always 0 or 2 mod 4. Casting out nines works because 10 ≡ 1 (mod 9), so every number is congruent to its digit sum mod 9.
example.zh: 12 小时钟面上 10+5=15≡3：10 点出发、走 5 小时，3 点到达。因为 3·5=15≡1 (mod 7)，所以模 7 下 3⁻¹≡5。解 3x≡4 (mod 7)：两边乘 5 得 x≡20≡6，验证 3·6=18≡4。但 2 在模 4 下没有逆元，因为 2x 模 4 只能是 0 或 2。“弃九法”成立，是因为 10≡1 (mod 9)，每个数都与它的各位数字之和模 9 同余。

image.en: Under the great station clock a traveller holds a ticket for the 10 o'clock train, a five-hour trip, and wonders when he will arrive. A thought bubble over his head reads '10 + 5 = 3?'. The stationmaster in a peaked cap points up at the clock face: past twelve the hands simply go round again, so fifteen o'clock is three.
image.zh: 巨大的车站钟下，旅客攥着一张 10 点开车、行程 5 小时的车票，琢磨几点能到。他头顶的思考泡里写着“10 + 5 = 3？”。戴大檐帽的站长指着钟面：过了 12 点，指针只是再转一圈，所以“15 点”就是 3 点。

means.en: arithmetic mod 12: only the remainders 0–11 matter
15 ≡ 3 (mod 12), because 12 divides 15 − 3
congruence classes wrap around: ℤₙ
add or multiply, then reduce mod n: the result is the same
means.zh: 先加或乘、再对 n 取余，结果不变

title.en: Fermat's Little Theorem and Euler's Theorem
title.zh: 费马小定理与欧拉定理

summary.en: If p is prime and p ∤ a, then a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p); more generally a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) whenever gcd(a, n) = 1.
summary.zh: 素数 p∤a 时 a^(p−1)≡1 (mod p)；更一般地，gcd(a,n)=1 时 a^φ(n)≡1 (mod n)。

explain.en: Fermat's little theorem: if p is prime and p does not divide a, then a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p); equivalently aᵖ ≡ a (mod p) for every integer a. Euler's totient φ(n) counts the numbers in 1, …, n that are coprime to n, and Euler's theorem says a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n) whenever gcd(a, n) = 1. Since φ(p) = p − 1, Fermat is the special case n = p. Both follow from Lagrange's theorem, because the invertible residues mod n form a group of order φ(n). Consequences: exponents can be reduced mod φ(n), and huge powers are cheap by repeated squaring, about 2 log₂ k multiplications for aᵏ. The converse fails: Carmichael numbers such as 561 pass Fermat's test without being prime.
explain.zh: 费马小定理：若 p 是素数且 p 不整除 a，则 a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p)；等价地，对所有整数 a 有 aᵖ ≡ a (mod p)。欧拉函数 φ(n) 计数 1,…,n 中与 n 互素的数，欧拉定理说：只要 gcd(a,n)=1，就有 a^φ(n) ≡ 1 (mod n)。因为 φ(p) = p−1，费马小定理是 n = p 的特例。两者都可由拉格朗日定理推出，因为模 n 的可逆余数构成 φ(n) 阶群。由此，指数可以对 φ(n) 取模；大幂次用反复平方法计算也很便宜，求 aᵏ 约需 2log₂k 次乘法。逆命题不成立：561 这样的卡迈克尔数能通过费马检验，却不是素数。

example.en: Powers of 3 mod 7 run 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1, so 3⁶ ≡ 1, as Fermat predicts with p − 1 = 6. Hence 3¹⁰⁰ = 3^(6·16 + 4) ≡ 3⁴ = 81 ≡ 4 (mod 7). Repeated squaring for 3¹³ mod 7: 13 = 8 + 4 + 1, and 3² ≡ 2, 3⁴ ≡ 4, 3⁸ ≡ 2, so 3¹³ ≡ 2 · 4 · 3 = 24 ≡ 3. Euler: φ(10) = 4, and 7⁴ = 2401 ≡ 1 (mod 10).

image.en: A toy steam train circles a ring of six lamp-lit stations, named in the order it reaches them: 3, 2, 6, 4, 5 and 1. At every stop it multiplies by 3, mod 7. In the middle the stationmaster checks her stopwatch, and the bell on top of station 1 rings each time the train comes home, always after exactly six stops.
image.zh: 一列玩具蒸汽火车绕着六座亮灯的小站转圈，站名按到达顺序依次是 3、2、6、4、5、1：每到一站就乘一次 3，再模 7。站长站在圆心看着秒表；每当火车回到 1 号站，站顶的铃就响一次——每次都恰好走了六站。

means.en: the non-zero residues mod 7
the powers 3¹, 3², 3³, … taken mod 7

thing.en: the bell at station 1 after six stops
thing.zh: 六站后 1 号站的铃声

means.en: 3⁶ ≡ 1, an instance of a^(p−1) ≡ 1 (mod p)
exponents can be reduced mod p − 1
means.zh: 指数可以对 p−1 取模

summary.en: If the moduli are pairwise coprime, a system x ≡ aᵢ (mod nᵢ) has exactly one solution modulo n₁n₂⋯nₖ.
summary.zh: 若各模数两两互素，同余方程组 x ≡ aᵢ (mod nᵢ) 在模 n₁n₂⋯nₖ 下有唯一解。

explain.en: The Chinese remainder theorem: if n₁, …, nₖ are pairwise coprime and N = n₁⋯nₖ, then for any remainders a₁, …, aₖ the system x ≡ aᵢ (mod nᵢ) has a solution, and it is unique mod N. Equivalently, the map x mod N ↦ (x mod n₁, …, x mod nₖ) is a bijection that respects + and ×. Construction: let Mᵢ = N/nᵢ and yᵢ = Mᵢ⁻¹ mod nᵢ, which exists because gcd(Mᵢ, nᵢ) = 1; then x = Σ aᵢMᵢyᵢ. The problem appears in the Sunzi Suanjing, usually dated to the 3rd to 5th century AD, and is known in China as 'Han Xin counts his soldiers'. Uses include computing with big numbers residue by residue and speeding up RSA decryption.
explain.zh: 中国剩余定理：若 n₁,…,nₖ 两两互素，N = n₁⋯nₖ，则对任意余数 a₁,…,aₖ，方程组 x ≡ aᵢ (mod nᵢ) 有解，且模 N 唯一。等价地说，映射 x mod N ↦ (x mod n₁, …, x mod nₖ) 是双射，并且保持加法和乘法。构造法：令 Mᵢ = N/nᵢ，yᵢ = Mᵢ⁻¹ mod nᵢ（因 gcd(Mᵢ,nᵢ)=1 而存在），则 x = Σ aᵢMᵢyᵢ。此问题见于《孙子算经》（一般认为成书于公元 3 至 5 世纪），民间称为“韩信点兵”。应用包括把大数拆成各个余数分别计算、加速 RSA 解密等。

image.en: On the station platform a general reviews a troop of toy soldiers waiting for their train. Counted off in threes, two are left over; in fives, three; in sevens, two. Right now they stand in rows of five: four full rows and three stragglers in front. From the leftovers alone the general announces the total: 23.
image.zh: 站台上，将军检阅一队等车的玩具士兵。三人一排数，剩两人；五人一排，剩三人；七人一排，剩两人。此刻他们正按五人一排站着：四排站满，前面还剩三个落单的。将军只凭这几个余数，就报出了总数：23。

thing.en: rows of five, three left over

means.en: the condition x ≡ 3 (mod 5)
x ≡ 2 (mod 3) and x ≡ 2 (mod 7)
the unique solution mod 3 · 5 · 7 = 105

text.zh: 三三剩二，五五剩三，七七剩二

summary.en: Publish n = pq and e; anyone can encrypt c = mᵉ mod n, but decrypting m = cᵈ mod n needs d, and finding d requires p and q.
summary.zh: 公开 n=pq 与 e，人人都能加密 c=mᵉ mod n；解密 m=cᵈ mod n 要用 d，而求 d 须知道 p 和 q。

explain.en: Key generation: choose large primes p and q, set n = pq and φ(n) = (p − 1)(q − 1), pick e with gcd(e, φ(n)) = 1, and compute d ≡ e⁻¹ (mod φ(n)) with the extended Euclidean algorithm. The public key is (n, e); the private key is d. Encrypt a message 0 ≤ m < n as c = mᵉ mod n and decrypt it as m = cᵈ mod n. This works because ed = 1 + kφ(n), so m^(ed) = m · (m^φ(n))ᵏ ≡ m by Euler's theorem when gcd(m, n) = 1, and the Chinese remainder theorem extends this to every m. Anyone who could factor n could compute φ(n) and d, so security rests on factoring being hard. Real RSA uses primes of 1024 bits or more and randomised padding; textbook RSA is not secure.
explain.zh: 生成密钥：取大素数 p、q，令 n = pq，φ(n) = (p−1)(q−1)，选 e 使 gcd(e, φ(n)) = 1，再用扩展欧几里得算法求 d ≡ e⁻¹ (mod φ(n))。公钥是 (n, e)，私钥是 d。对消息 0 ≤ m < n，加密 c = mᵉ mod n，解密 m = cᵈ mod n。原理：ed = 1 + kφ(n)，当 gcd(m,n)=1 时由欧拉定理 m^(ed) = m·(m^φ(n))ᵏ ≡ m，再借助中国剩余定理推广到所有 m。谁能分解 n，谁就能算出 φ(n) 和 d，所以安全性依赖于大数分解的困难。实际的 RSA 使用 1024 位以上的素数和随机填充；教科书式的 RSA 并不安全。

example.en: Toy key: p = 3, q = 11, so n = 33 and φ(n) = 20; take e = 3 and d = 7, since 3 · 7 = 21 ≡ 1 (mod 20). Encrypt m = 4: c = 4³ = 64 ≡ 31 (mod 33). Decrypt: 31 ≡ −2, so 31⁷ ≡ (−2)⁷ = −128 ≡ 4 (mod 33), because −128 + 132 = 4. The message is back.

image.en: At the left-luggage office a stationmaster hands out open padlocks from a bench to anyone who asks. A traveller has already snapped one shut on the chest that holds her letter, and the giant lock now hangs on its front. Only the stationmaster holds the key that opens these locks. A hooded spy kneels with a magnifying glass, squinting at the lock and trying to forge a key by splitting its number into two primes.
image.zh: 行李寄存处，站长把长椅上一把把开着的挂锁分给任何来要的人。一位旅客已用其中一把锁住了装信的箱子，巨大的锁挂在箱子正面。能打开这些锁的钥匙只握在站长手里。一个戴兜帽的间谍跪在地上举着放大镜，眯眼端详那把锁，想把锁上的号码拆成两个素数，好配出钥匙。

means.en: the public key (n, e): anyone can encrypt c = mᵉ mod n
means.zh: 公钥 (n, e)：人人都能加密 c = mᵉ mod n

means.en: the ciphertext c
the private key d = e⁻¹ mod φ(n), giving m = cᵈ mod n
means.zh: 私钥 d = e⁻¹ mod φ(n)，解出 m = cᵈ mod n

means.en: an attacker must factor n = pq to find d
means.zh: 攻击者必须分解 n = pq 才能求出 d

summary.en: Complex numbers, then the abstract structures, groups, rings and fields, that capture how arithmetic behaves.
summary.zh: 复数，以及刻画运算规律的抽象结构：群、环与域。

title.en: Complex Numbers and Roots of Unity

summary.en: z = a + bi = r·e^(iθ); multiplying multiplies lengths and adds angles, and the n-th roots of unity form a regular n-gon.
summary.zh: z = a + bi = r·e^(iθ)；相乘时模相乘、辐角相加，n 次单位根构成单位圆上的正 n 边形。

explain.en: A complex number z = a + bi, with i² = −1, is a point (a, b) in the plane. In polar form z = r(cos θ + i sin θ) = r·e^(iθ), where r = |z| = √(a² + b²) is the modulus and θ the argument; Euler's formula e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ links the two. Multiplication multiplies moduli and adds arguments, so multiplying by e^(iθ) rotates the plane by θ, and multiplying by i is a quarter turn: two quarter turns give i² = −1. De Moivre's formula follows: (cos θ + i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ + i sin nθ. The equation zⁿ = 1 has exactly n solutions e^(2πik/n), k = 0, …, n − 1, the vertices of a regular n-gon on the unit circle; they underlie the fast Fourier transform.
explain.zh: 复数 z=a+bi（i²=−1）对应平面上的点 (a,b)。极坐标形式 z=r(cos θ+i sin θ)=r·e^(iθ)，其中 r=|z|=√(a²+b²) 是模，θ 是辐角；欧拉公式 e^(iθ)=cos θ+i sin θ 把两者联系起来。相乘时模相乘、辐角相加，所以乘以 e^(iθ) 就是把平面旋转 θ，乘以 i 是转四分之一圈，转两次就是 i²=−1。由此得棣莫弗公式：(cos θ+i sin θ)ⁿ = cos nθ+i sin nθ。方程 zⁿ=1 恰有 n 个解 e^(2πik/n)（k=0,…,n−1），它们是单位圆上正 n 边形的顶点，也是快速傅里叶变换的基础。

example.en: (1 + i)(1 − i) = 1 − i² = 2. In polar form 1 + i = √2·e^(iπ/4), so (1 + i)⁸ = (√2)⁸·e^(2πi) = 16. The sixth roots of unity are e^(iπk/3), k = 0, …, 5: 1, ½ ± (√3/2)i, −½ ± (√3/2)i and −1, a regular hexagon. Multiplying all six by ω = e^(iπ/3) only permutes them, and their sum is 0.
example.zh: (1+i)(1−i) = 1 − i² = 2。极坐标下 1+i = √2·e^(iπ/4)，所以 (1+i)⁸ = (√2)⁸·e^(2πi) = 16。六次单位根是 e^(iπk/3)（k = 0,…,5）：1、½ ± (√3/2)i、−½ ± (√3/2)i 和 −1，组成正六边形。把六个根都乘以 ω = e^(iπ/3) 只是把它们轮换一下，它们的和为 0。

image.en: In the gallery an artist has planted a giant drawing compass at the centre of the stage and traced the unit circle. Six golden butterflies hover around it at equal spacing, a perfect hexagon, and the whole formation slowly turns: each sixth of a turn lands every butterfly on its neighbour's spot. Nearby a spiral sculpture coils outwards, turning and growing at every step.
image.zh: 美术馆里，艺术家把一只巨大的圆规立在舞台中央，画出了单位圆。六只金蝴蝶等距悬停在圆周上，正好构成正六边形，整个阵型缓缓旋转：每转六分之一圈，每只蝴蝶都正好落到邻居的位置上。旁边一座螺旋雕塑向外盘绕，每绕一步都在转动、在长大。

means.en: the origin and the unit circle |z| = 1
the sixth roots of unity e^(2πik/6)
multiplying by e^(iθ) rotates by θ; by ω it maps the hexagon onto itself
means.zh: 乘 e^(iθ) 即旋转 θ；乘 ω 把六边形映到自身

means.en: powers zⁿ with |z| > 1: each step rotates and scales
means.zh: |z|>1 时的幂 zⁿ：每一步都边转边放大

summary.en: A group is a set with an associative operation, an identity element and an inverse for every element.
summary.zh: 群是带有一个满足结合律的运算、有单位元、且每个元素都有逆元的集合。

explain.en: A group (G, ·) is a set G with an operation that is closed (a·b ∈ G) and associative ((a·b)·c = a·(b·c)), has an identity e with e·a = a·e = a, and gives every a an inverse a⁻¹ with a·a⁻¹ = a⁻¹·a = e. It is abelian if a·b = b·a for all a and b. Examples: (ℤ, +) with identity 0 and inverse −a; ℤₙ under addition mod n; the non-zero rationals under ×. The symmetries of a square form the dihedral group D₄ (written D₈ in some books): 8 elements, 4 rotations and 4 reflections, and not abelian. The permutations of {1, 2, 3} form S₃, the smallest non-abelian group, with 6 elements. Groups describe symmetry wherever it appears: in geometry, cryptography, puzzles like the Rubik's cube, and physics.
explain.zh: 群 (G, ·) 是一个集合 G 加一种运算，满足：封闭（a·b∈G）、结合（(a·b)·c = a·(b·c)）、有单位元 e 使 e·a = a·e = a、每个 a 都有逆元 a⁻¹ 使 a·a⁻¹ = a⁻¹·a = e。若对所有 a、b 都有 a·b = b·a，称为阿贝尔群（交换群）。例子：(ℤ, +)，单位元 0，逆元 −a；模 n 加法下的 ℤₙ；乘法下的非零有理数。正方形的对称构成二面体群 D₄（有的书记作 D₈），共 8 个元素（4 个旋转、4 个反射），不可交换。{1,2,3} 的置换构成 S₃，有 6 个元素，是最小的非交换群。哪里有对称，哪里就有群：几何、密码学、魔方这样的谜题，以及物理学。

example.en: Three paintings L, P and A hang in positions 1, 2, 3. Let s swap positions 1 and 2, and t swap positions 2 and 3. Doing s then t turns LPA into PLA and then PAL; doing t then s gives LAP and then ALP. Since PAL ≠ ALP, the shuffles do not commute. Each swap is its own inverse, doing nothing is the identity, and the six possible arrangements form the group S₃.
example.zh: 三幅画 L、P、A 挂在 1、2、3 号位。令 s 交换 1、2 号位，t 交换 2、3 号位。先 s 后 t：LPA 变成 PLA，再变成 PAL；先 t 后 s：LPA 变成 LAP，再变成 ALP。PAL ≠ ALP，所以这两种调换不可交换。每次交换都是自己的逆，什么都不做是单位元，六种排法构成群 S₃。

image.en: Three paintings on easels, a landscape, a portrait and an abstract, keep changing places. A robot art handler swaps the left pair while a human handler swaps the right pair, and two chunky double arrows on the floor mark the two swaps. The handlers argue: swapping left then right, or right then left, leaves the wall in a different order.
image.zh: 三个画架上的风景画、肖像画和抽象画不停地换位置。机器人搬运工调换左边两幅，人类搬运工调换右边两幅，地上两支粗大的双向箭头标出这两种调换。两个搬运工争执起来：先换左再换右，和先换右再换左，墙上的顺序竟然不一样。

means.en: the elements: the 6 permutations in S₃
means.zh: 元素：S₃ 的 6 个置换

means.en: the swaps s and t, each its own inverse
means.zh: 交换 s 与 t，各自是自己的逆

means.en: the operation: composition of moves
st ≠ ts: the group is not abelian

summary.en: In a finite group the order of a subgroup divides the order of the group: its cosets cut the group into equal pieces.
summary.zh: 有限群中，子群的阶整除群的阶：子群的陪集把群切成大小相等的几块。

explain.en: Let H be a subgroup of a finite group G. For g ∈ G, the left coset gH = {gh : h ∈ H} has exactly |H| elements, since h ↦ gh is a bijection. Two cosets are equal or disjoint, being the classes of the equivalence g ~ g′ ⇔ g⁻¹g′ ∈ H, and together they cover G. So G splits into [G : H] cosets of equal size, and |G| = [G : H]·|H|: the order of H divides the order of G. Corollaries: the order of any element a, the size of the subgroup it generates, divides |G|, so a^|G| = e; a group of prime order is cyclic. Applied to the invertible residues mod n, a group of order φ(n), this gives Euler's theorem, and Fermat's when n is prime. The converse fails: A₄ has order 12 but no subgroup of order 6.
explain.zh: 设 H 是有限群 G 的子群。对 g∈G，左陪集 gH = {gh : h∈H} 恰有 |H| 个元素，因为 h↦gh 是双射。两个陪集要么相同、要么不相交（它们是等价关系 g~g′ ⇔ g⁻¹g′∈H 的等价类），合起来覆盖整个 G。于是 G 被分成 [G:H] 个大小相等的陪集，|G| = [G:H]·|H|：子群的阶整除群的阶。推论：元素 a 的阶（它生成的子群的大小）整除 |G|，所以 a^|G| = e；素数阶的群都是循环群。用于模 n 的可逆余数构成的 φ(n) 阶群，就得到欧拉定理，n 为素数时即费马小定理。逆命题不成立：A₄ 的阶是 12，却没有 6 阶子群。

example.en: In ℤ₁₂ under addition, H = {0, 3, 6, 9} is a subgroup of order 4. Its cosets are H, 1 + H = {1, 4, 7, 10} and 2 + H = {2, 5, 8, 11}: three disjoint blocks of four, and 12 = 3 · 4. So subgroups of ℤ₁₂ can only have order 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 12, never 5. Every element's order divides 12: for example 4 generates {0, 4, 8} and has order 3.
example.zh: 在加法群 ℤ₁₂ 中，H = {0,3,6,9} 是 4 阶子群。它的陪集是 H、1+H = {1,4,7,10}、2+H = {2,5,8,11}：三块互不相交、各含 4 个元素，12 = 3·4。所以 ℤ₁₂ 的子群只能是 1、2、3、4、6 或 12 阶，不可能是 5 阶。每个元素的阶都整除 12：例如 4 生成 {0,4,8}，阶为 3。

image.en: Twelve visitors in the gallery sit on three identical benches, four to a bench: red coats on the left, gold in the middle, blue on the right. The gold bench, where the guide sits with her flag, is the subgroup; the other two are its cosets, the same size and sharing no one. A family of five waits in front, shrugging: no block of five can ever be seated, since 5 does not divide 12.
image.zh: 美术馆里，十二位参观者坐在三条一模一样的长椅上，每条坐四人：左边穿红衣，中间穿金衣，右边穿蓝衣。举着小旗的导游所在的金色长椅是子群，另外两条是它的陪集，人数相同、互不重叠。前面站着五口之家，无奈地耸肩：五个人永远凑不成一块，因为 5 不整除 12。

thing.en: the gold bench with the guide

means.en: the subgroup H, which contains the identity
means.zh: 包含单位元的子群 H

means.en: the cosets gH: the same size as H, pairwise disjoint
means.zh: 陪集 gH：与 H 一样大，两两不交

means.en: no subgroup of order 5, since 5 ∤ 12

summary.en: Rings have + and × with the usual laws; fields also allow division by any non-zero element. ℤₙ is a field exactly when n is prime.
summary.zh: 环有满足通常运算律的加法与乘法；域还允许除以任何非零元。ℤₙ 是域当且仅当 n 是素数。

explain.en: A ring (R, +, ×) is an abelian group under + with an associative multiplication that distributes over addition; here rings are commutative with a 1. ℤ is the model ring, and ℤₙ and the polynomial rings R[x] are rings too. A field is a ring with 1 ≠ 0 in which every non-zero element has a multiplicative inverse: ℚ, ℝ and ℂ are fields, but ℤ is not, since 2 has no integer inverse. In a field ab = 0 forces a = 0 or b = 0, while a ring may have zero divisors, like 2 · 3 = 0 in ℤ₆. ℤₙ is a field exactly when n is prime, because a is invertible mod n iff gcd(a, n) = 1. Over a field F, the polynomial ring F[x] has division with remainder, just like ℤ. Finite fields such as ℤ₂ underlie coding theory and much of cryptography.
explain.zh: 环 (R, +, ×) 在加法下是交换群，乘法满足结合律并对加法满足分配律；这里约定环可交换且有单位元 1。ℤ 是典型的环，ℤₙ 和多项式环 R[x] 也是环。域是 1 ≠ 0 且每个非零元都有乘法逆元的环：ℚ、ℝ、ℂ 是域，ℤ 不是，因为 2 在整数中没有逆元。域中 ab = 0 必有 a = 0 或 b = 0，环中却可能有零因子，如 ℤ₆ 中 2·3 = 0。ℤₙ 是域当且仅当 n 是素数，因为 a 模 n 可逆当且仅当 gcd(a,n)=1。域 F 上的多项式环 F[x] 像 ℤ 一样可以做带余除法。ℤ₂ 这样的有限域是编码理论和许多密码算法的基础。

example.en: In ℤ₇ every non-zero element has an inverse: 1·1 = 2·4 = 3·5 = 6·6 = 1 (mod 7), so ℤ₇ is a field. In ℤ₆, 2 · 3 = 0, and 2, 3, 4 have no inverses: 2x mod 6 is always 0, 2 or 4. The multiples of 2 mod 7 run 2, 4, 6, 1, so 2 · 4 ≡ 1; the multiples of 2 mod 6 run 2, 4, 0 and never reach 1.
example.zh: 在 ℤ₇ 中每个非零元都有逆元：1·1 = 2·4 = 3·5 = 6·6 ≡ 1 (mod 7)，所以 ℤ₇ 是域。在 ℤ₆ 中 2·3 = 0，而 2、3、4 都没有逆元：2x 模 6 只能是 0、2、4。2 的倍数模 7 依次为 2、4、6、1，所以 2·4 ≡ 1；2 的倍数模 6 依次为 2、4、0，永远到不了 1。

image.en: Two round ponds sit side by side in the gallery, one with seven lily pads in a ring, the other with six. On each pond a frog starts on pad 0 and hops two pads at a time. On the seven-pad pond it lands on 2, 4, 6 and then 1, and in the end visits every pad. On the six-pad pond it lands on 2, 4 and back on 0, again and again, and never reaches pad 1.
image.zh: 美术馆里并排两座圆池，一座里有七片荷叶围成一圈，另一座有六片。每座池里都有一只青蛙从 0 号叶出发，每次跳两片。七叶池里它依次落在 2、4、6，然后是 1，最终跳遍所有荷叶；六叶池里它只在 2、4 和 0 之间来回打转，永远到不了 1 号叶。

means.en: ℤ₇: 7 is prime, so it is a field
ℤ₆: not a field

thing.en: hopping two pads at a time

means.en: the multiples of 2; reaching pad 1 means 2 has an inverse
means.zh: 2 的倍数；能跳到 1 号叶说明 2 有逆元

thing.en: back on pad 0 after three hops

means.en: a zero divisor: 2 · 3 = 0 in ℤ₆

summary.en: Counting without listing, sequences defined by recurrences, and graphs: the mathematics of choices and networks.
summary.zh: 不必逐一列举的计数、由递推定义的数列，以及图：关于选择与网络的数学。

summary.en: The basic counting principles, cooked up in a kitchen: menus multiply, selections are chosen, and crowded baskets force collisions.
summary.zh: 在厨房里学计数：菜单相乘、挑选成组、篮子装不下就必有重复。

summary.en: Add the counts of disjoint alternatives; multiply the counts of choices made one after another.
summary.zh: 互不重叠的几类选择，种数相加；一步接一步的选择，种数相乘。

explain.en: Sum rule: if a task can be done in one of m ways or in one of n ways, and no way appears in both lists, it can be done in m + n ways. Product rule: if a task is a sequence of two steps, with m ways to do the first and n ways to do the second whatever the first choice was, there are m·n ways. In the language of sets, |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| when A and B are disjoint, and |A × B| = |A|·|B|. Both rules extend to any finite number of cases or steps. Almost every counting formula is built from them; when the cases overlap, the sum rule must be corrected by inclusion–exclusion.
explain.zh: 加法原理：一件事可以用第一类的 m 种方法之一完成，也可以用第二类的 n 种方法之一完成，且两类没有重复，则共有 m+n 种方法。乘法原理：一件事分两步完成，第一步有 m 种做法，而无论第一步怎么做，第二步都有 n 种做法，则共有 m·n 种。用集合的语言：A 与 B 不相交时 |A∪B|=|A|+|B|，笛卡儿积满足 |A×B|=|A|·|B|。两条原理都能推广到任意有限多类或多步。几乎所有计数公式都由它们搭成；各类之间若有重叠，加法原理就要用容斥原理来修正。

example.en: A café pairs one of 3 drinks with one of 4 fruits: 3 × 4 = 12 snacks. A menu with 3 starters, 4 mains and 2 desserts gives 3 × 4 × 2 = 24 three-course meals; if you order just one dish, the options are disjoint, so there are 3 + 4 + 2 = 9. Each of the 8 bits of a byte has 2 values, so there are 2⁸ = 256 bytes.
example.zh: 3 种饮料配 4 种水果：3×4=12 种组合。菜单有 3 道前菜、4 道主菜、2 道甜点，一套三道菜有 3×4×2=24 种；如果只点一道菜，各类互不重叠，共 3+4+2=9 种。一个字节 8 位，每位 2 种取值，共 2⁸=256 种。

image.en: A chef in a tall white hat points at a giant menu board split into twelve cells, A1 to C4. In front stand three huge mugs, drinks A, B and C, and four giant fruits numbered 1 to 4; every cell of the board is one mug paired with one fruit. Beside them a child who may take only one thing, a mug or a fruit, hops between the 3 + 4 = 7 choices.
image.zh: 戴高白帽的厨师指着一块巨大的菜单板，板上分成 A1 到 C4 共十二格。板前摆着三只巨大的杯子（饮料 A、B、C）和四个巨型水果（编号 1 到 4）；每一格都是一杯配一果。旁边的小孩只能拿一样，杯子或水果，在 3+4=7 个选择之间蹦来蹦去。

means.en: first step: 3 ways (drink A, B or C)
means.zh: 第一步：3 种做法（饮料 A、B、C）

means.en: second step: 4 ways, the same 4 whatever the drink
means.zh: 第二步：4 种做法，与第一步选了什么无关

means.en: product rule: 3 × 4 = 12 pairs, the set A × B
means.zh: 乘法原理：3×4=12 对，即集合 A×B

means.en: sum rule: disjoint options add, 3 + 4 = 7
means.zh: 加法原理：互不重叠的选项相加，3+4=7

items.text: A1 A2 A3 A4;B1 B2 B3 B4;C1 C2 C3 C4

summary.en: Ordered selections of k from n number n!/(n−k)!; unordered ones number C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!).
summary.zh: 从 n 个中有序取 k 个有 n!/(n−k)! 种；不计顺序则有 C(n,k)=n!/(k!(n−k)!) 种。

explain.en: To arrange k of n distinct objects in order there are n choices for the first place, n − 1 for the second, and so on, so by the product rule P(n, k) = n!/(n − k)!. If order does not matter, each set of k objects has been counted k! times, once per ordering, so the number of k-subsets is C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n − k)!), read 'n choose k'. With repetition allowed there are nᵏ ordered sequences, and C(n + k − 1, k) multisets of size k: write the k chosen items as stars and separate the n kinds with n − 1 bars (stars and bars). Which formula applies depends on two questions: does order matter, and may an item repeat?
explain.zh: 把 n 个不同物体中的 k 个排成一列：第一位有 n 种选法，第二位有 n−1 种……由乘法原理得排列数 P(n,k)=n!/(n−k)!。若不计顺序，每个 k 元子集恰好被数了 k! 次（每种排法一次），所以组合数 C(n,k)=n!/(k!(n−k)!)，读作“n 选 k”。允许重复时，有序序列有 nᵏ 个；从 n 类中可重复地取 k 个（多重集）有 C(n+k−1,k) 种：把取出的 k 个画成星号，用 n−1 块隔板把 n 类隔开（隔板法）。用哪个公式，取决于两个问题：顺序是否重要？能否重复？

example.en: Five cakes compete for gold, silver and bronze: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 possible podiums. Choosing 3 of the 5 for a tasting basket, where order is irrelevant: C(5, 3) = 60/3! = 10. Buying 3 doughnuts from 4 flavours, repeats allowed: C(4 + 3 − 1, 3) = C(6, 3) = 20.
example.zh: 5 个蛋糕争夺金、银、铜牌：5×4×3=60 种领奖结果。从中挑 3 个装进试吃篮，不计顺序：C(5,3)=60/3!=10 种。从 4 种口味中可重复地买 3 个甜甜圈：C(4+3−1,3)=C(6,3)=20 种。

image.en: A baking contest: five cakes stand in a row while a judge in a top hat hangs gold, silver and bronze medals on three of them. Which cake gets which medal matters, so there are 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 possible podiums. In front, a kneeling child drops three little cakes into a basket, where their order is lost: only C(5, 3) = 10 different baskets.
image.zh: 烘焙大赛：五个蛋糕排成一排，戴高礼帽的评委给其中三个挂上金、银、铜牌。哪个蛋糕拿哪块牌是有区别的，领奖结果有 5×4×3=60 种。前面一个跪着的孩子把三块小蛋糕丢进篮子，篮子里不分先后：只有 C(5,3)=10 种篮子。

means.en: n = 5 distinct objects
ordered choice: P(5, 3) = 5·4·3 = 60

thing.zh: 装 3 块小蛋糕的篮子

means.en: unordered choice: each 3-set is one basket, 60/3! = 10
means.zh: 无序选取：每个 3 元组只算一篮，60/3!=10

summary.en: (x + y)ⁿ = Σ C(n, k) xᵏ yⁿ⁻ᵏ: the coefficients are the binomial coefficients, the rows of Pascal's triangle.
summary.zh: (x+y)ⁿ=ΣC(n,k)xᵏyⁿ⁻ᵏ：展开式的系数就是二项式系数，也就是杨辉三角的各行。

explain.en: For every natural number n, (x + y)ⁿ = Σ C(n, k) xᵏ yⁿ⁻ᵏ, with k running from 0 to n. Combinatorial proof: expanding the product of n factors (x + y) means picking x or y from each factor, and the term xᵏyⁿ⁻ᵏ arises once for each way of choosing which k factors give x, that is C(n, k) times. The coefficients form Pascal's triangle, built row by row with Pascal's rule C(n, k) = C(n − 1, k − 1) + C(n − 1, k): a k-subset of {1, …, n} either contains n or it does not. Setting x = y = 1 gives Σ C(n, k) = 2ⁿ, the number of subsets of an n-element set.
explain.zh: 对每个自然数 n，(x+y)ⁿ=ΣC(n,k)xᵏyⁿ⁻ᵏ（k 从 0 到 n）。组合证明：把 n 个因子 (x+y) 乘开，就是从每个因子里挑 x 或 y；项 xᵏyⁿ⁻ᵏ 出现的次数等于“选哪 k 个因子出 x”的方法数，即 C(n,k)。这些系数排成杨辉三角（Pascal's triangle），按帕斯卡法则 C(n,k)=C(n−1,k−1)+C(n−1,k) 逐行生成：{1,…,n} 的 k 元子集要么含 n，要么不含。令 x=y=1 得 ΣC(n,k)=2ⁿ，正是 n 元集合的子集个数。

example.en: (x + y)³ = x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³, matching the row 1 3 3 1. The next row is 1 4 6 4 1, where 6 = 3 + 3 by Pascal's rule, and 1 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 1 = 16 = 2⁴. Since 11 = 10 + 1, the rows also appear as 11² = 121, 11³ = 1331 and 11⁴ = 14641.

image.en: Mugs are stacked into a pyramid four rows high: one on top, then two, three and four. A kettle hovers over the top mug and pours, and every mug overflows into the two mugs below it. The two middle mugs of the bottom row glow gold, because tea can reach each of them by 3 routes and the outer mugs by only 1. A cook in a beret points at the blackboard, where the rows 1, 1 1, 1 2 1, 1 3 3 1 are chalked.
image.zh: 杯子搭成四层金字塔：顶上一只，往下两只、三只、四只。一把水壶悬在顶杯上方倒茶，每只杯子溢出的茶流进下面相邻的两只。底层中间两只杯子金光闪闪：茶有 3 条路线能流到它们，两端的杯子各只有 1 条。戴贝雷帽的厨师指着黑板，上面写着 1、1 1、1 2 1、1 3 3 1。

means.en: Pascal's triangle, rows n = 0 to 3
means.zh: 杨辉三角的第 0 到 3 行

thing.en: each mug spills into the two below

means.en: Pascal's rule: each entry is the sum of the two above it
means.zh: 帕斯卡法则：每个数等于上方两数之和

thing.en: a route: left or right at each level

means.en: picking x or y from each factor (x + y)
means.zh: 从每个因子 (x+y) 中挑 x 或 y

means.en: 3 routes = C(3, 1) = C(3, 2): the coefficients of x²y and xy²
means.zh: 3 条路线=C(3,1)=C(3,2)，即 x²y 与 xy² 的系数

summary.en: Put n + 1 objects into n boxes and some box holds at least two; in general some box holds at least ⌈N/k⌉.
summary.zh: n+1 个物体放进 n 个盒子，必有一盒至少两个；一般地，必有一盒至少 ⌈N/k⌉ 个。

explain.en: If more than n objects are placed in n boxes, some box holds at least two, since otherwise there would be at most n objects. In general, N objects in k boxes force some box to hold at least ⌈N/k⌉: if every box held at most ⌈N/k⌉ − 1 < N/k objects, the total would be less than N. In the language of functions, a map from a finite set to a smaller set cannot be injective. The principle proves that a crowded box exists without saying which one, and it drives many proofs in combinatorics, number theory and computer science, from hash collisions to the fact that no lossless compressor shortens every file.
explain.zh: 把多于 n 个物体放进 n 个盒子，必有一盒至少装两个，否则总数至多为 n。一般地，N 个物体放进 k 个盒子，必有一盒至少装 ⌈N/k⌉ 个：若每盒至多 ⌈N/k⌉−1（小于 N/k）个，总数就不足 N。用函数的语言说，从有限集到更小集合的映射不可能是单射。它只证明拥挤的盒子“存在”，不指出是哪一个；在组合、数论和计算机科学中用途极广，从哈希冲突到“没有能把每个文件都变短的无损压缩”。

example.en: Nobody has more than 500,000 hairs (a typical head has about 100,000 to 150,000), so a city of 1,000,000 people contains two with exactly the same number of hairs: there are only 500,001 possible counts. Among any 367 people, two share a birthday. Any 5 points in a unit square include two at distance at most √2/2: cut the square into 4 squares of side 1/2.
example.zh: 没有人的头发超过 50 万根（通常约 10 万到 15 万根），所以百万人口的城市里必有两人头发根数完全相同：根数只有 500001 种可能。任意 367 人中必有两人同一天生日。单位正方形内任取 5 点，必有两点距离不超过 √2/2：把它切成 4 个边长 1/2 的小正方形即可。

image.en: A robot arm in the kitchen sorts five eggs into four baskets. Three baskets get one egg each, but the fourth has to take two, and the pair squeezed together starts to crack. A cook in a cap shrugs: with more eggs than baskets, some basket was always going to get two, though nobody could say in advance which one.
image.zh: 厨房里一只机械臂把五个鸡蛋分进四个篮子。三个篮子各放一个，第四个篮子只好放两个，挤在一起的那一对开始裂开。戴帽子的厨工耸耸肩：蛋比篮子多，总有一个篮子要装两个，只是事先说不准是哪个。

means.en: k = 4 boxes
N = 5 objects, more than the boxes

thing.en: the cracking pair in one basket

means.en: some box holds at least ⌈5/4⌉ = 2
a pure existence proof: it does not say which box
means.zh: 纯粹的存在性证明：不指出是哪一盒

summary.en: To count a union, add the sets, subtract the pairwise overlaps, add back the triple overlaps, and so on.
summary.zh: 求并集大小：先把各集合相加，减去两两交集，再加回三重交集，依此类推。

explain.en: For two finite sets, |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|: elements in both are counted twice by |A| + |B|, so one copy is removed. For three sets, |A ∪ B ∪ C| = |A| + |B| + |C| − |A ∩ B| − |A ∩ C| − |B ∩ C| + |A ∩ B ∩ C|. In general the signs alternate over intersections of 1, 2, 3, … sets, and each element of the union is counted exactly once: an element lying in m ≥ 1 of the sets contributes Σ (−1)ʲ⁺¹ C(m, j) = 1 − (1 − 1)ᵐ = 1. A classic application counts derangements, permutations with no fixed point: n hats handed back so that nobody gets their own.
explain.zh: 两个有限集：|A∪B|=|A|+|B|−|A∩B|，因为两者共有的元素在 |A|+|B| 中被数了两次，要减去一次。三个集合：|A∪B∪C|=|A|+|B|+|C|−|A∩B|−|A∩C|−|B∩C|+|A∩B∩C|。一般地，对 1 个、2 个、3 个……集合的交集交替加减，并集中每个元素恰好被数一次：属于 m 个集合（m≥1）的元素贡献 Σ(−1)ʲ⁺¹C(m,j)=1−(1−1)ᵐ=1。经典应用是错排计数：n 顶帽子发还回去，没有人拿到自己的那顶。

example.en: In a class of 30, 18 study French, 15 study Spanish and 7 study both: 18 + 15 − 7 = 26 study at least one, so 4 study neither. Derangements: D(n) = n! Σ (−1)ʲ/j! for j = 0..n. For 4 hats, D(4) = 24 − 24 + 12 − 4 + 1 = 9 of the 24 ways give nobody their own hat, and D(n)/n! → 1/e ≈ 0.368.
example.zh: 全班 30 人，18 人学法语、15 人学西班牙语、7 人两门都学：至少学一门的有 18+15−7=26 人，两门都不学的有 4 人。错排数 D(n)=n!Σ(−1)ʲ/j!（j 从 0 到 n）。4 顶帽子：D(4)=24−24+12−4+1=9，即 24 种发法中有 9 种人人拿错；而 D(n)/n!→1/e≈0.368。

image.en: Two big rugs, one red and one blue, overlap in the middle of the dining room. Two guests in red stand on the red-only part, two in blue on the blue-only part, and two in purple on the overlap. A waiter counts 4 on the red rug and 4 on the blue rug, gets 8, then realises the purple pair was counted twice: 4 + 4 − 2 = 6 chairs.
image.zh: 红、蓝两块大地毯在餐厅中央部分重叠。两位红衣客人站在只属于红毯的部分，两位蓝衣客人站在只属于蓝毯的部分，两位紫衣客人站在重叠处。服务员数红毯 4 人、蓝毯 4 人，得 8，随即发现紫衣二人被数了两次：4+4−2=6 把椅子。

thing.en: the red rug and the blue rug

means.en: sets A and B, each with 4 elements
means.zh: 集合 A 与 B，各有 4 个元素

means.en: A ∩ B, counted twice by |A| + |B|

summary.en: Sequences that grow from their own earlier terms, and the algebra that solves them.
summary.zh: 由自身前项长出来的数列，以及求解它们的代数方法。

summary.en: A recurrence defines each term of a sequence from earlier terms; with initial values it fixes the whole sequence.
summary.zh: 递推关系用前面的项定义后面的项；再给定初值，整个数列就唯一确定。

explain.en: A recurrence relation expresses aₙ in terms of earlier terms, for example aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + aₙ₋₂; together with enough initial values it determines the sequence uniquely, by induction. Recurrences arise naturally in counting: describe how an object of size n is built from smaller ones. Fibonacci's rabbits start with one newborn pair; from the age of two months each pair produces one new pair every month, and no rabbit dies. The pairs alive in month n are those alive in month n − 1 plus the newborns, one for each pair already alive in month n − 2, so Fₙ = Fₙ₋₁ + Fₙ₋₂ with F₁ = F₂ = 1. Recurrences are also how the running time of recursive algorithms is analysed.
explain.zh: 递推关系用前面的项来表示 aₙ，例如 aₙ=aₙ₋₁+aₙ₋₂；再给定足够的初值，数列就由归纳法唯一确定。计数时递推关系自然出现：只要说清规模为 n 的对象怎样由更小的对象搭成。斐波那契的兔子：起初有一对新生兔子，每对兔子从两个月大起每月生一对，且兔子不死。第 n 个月的兔子＝第 n−1 个月已有的兔子＋新生兔子，而新生的对数等于第 n−2 个月已有的对数，所以 Fₙ=Fₙ₋₁+Fₙ₋₂，F₁=F₂=1。分析递归算法的运行时间也靠递推关系。

example.en: Tower of Hanoi: to move n discs, move the top n − 1 to the spare peg, move the largest, then move the n − 1 back on top of it. So T(n) = 2T(n − 1) + 1 with T(1) = 1, giving 1, 3, 7, 15, …, and by induction T(n) = 2ⁿ − 1; 64 discs need 2⁶⁴ − 1 ≈ 1.8 × 10¹⁹ moves. The rabbits give 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, …
example.zh: 汉诺塔：要移动 n 个盘子，先把上面 n−1 个移到备用柱，再移最大的，最后把 n−1 个移回它上面。于是 T(n)=2T(n−1)+1，T(1)=1，得 1, 3, 7, 15, …，归纳可证 T(n)=2ⁿ−1；64 个盘子需要 2⁶⁴−1≈1.8×10¹⁹ 步。兔子数列则是 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, …

image.en: In the greenhouse, rabbits sit on each other's heads in five towers, one per month: 1, 1, 2, 3 and 5 rabbits tall. In every tower the brown adults at the bottom match the whole tower before it, and the white newborns on top match the tower two places back. A gardener points at the tallest tower: 5 = 3 + 2.
image.zh: 温室里，兔子一只叠一只，坐成五座塔，每月一座：高 1、1、2、3、5 只。每座塔下面的棕色成年兔与前一座塔一样多，上面的白色新生兔与再往前一座塔一样多。园丁指着最高的那座：5=3+2。

means.en: the sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, one term per month
Fₙ₋₁: every pair alive last month
means.zh: Fₙ₋₁：上个月已有的全部兔子

means.en: Fₙ₋₂: one new pair per pair alive two months ago
means.zh: Fₙ₋₂：两个月前已有的每对各生一对

means.en: the recurrence Fₙ = Fₙ₋₁ + Fₙ₋₂

summary.en: Try aₙ = rⁿ: the roots of the characteristic equation give the general solution, as in Binet's formula for Fibonacci.
summary.zh: 试探 aₙ=rⁿ：特征方程的根给出通解，斐波那契数列的比内公式就是一例。

explain.en: A linear recurrence with constant coefficients, such as aₙ = c₁aₙ₋₁ + c₂aₙ₋₂, has geometric solutions: aₙ = rⁿ works exactly when r² = c₁r + c₂, the characteristic equation. If its roots r₁ ≠ r₂ are distinct, every solution has the form aₙ = A·r₁ⁿ + B·r₂ⁿ, because solutions can be added and scaled (the recurrence is linear) and two initial values fix A and B. A repeated root r gives (A + Bn)rⁿ instead, and higher orders work the same way. For Fibonacci, r² = r + 1 has roots φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618 and ψ = (1 − √5)/2 ≈ −0.618, and F₀ = 0, F₁ = 1 give Binet's formula Fₙ = (φⁿ − ψⁿ)/√5. Since |ψ| < 1, the ψⁿ term fades and Fₙ grows like φⁿ.
explain.zh: 常系数线性递推，如 aₙ=c₁aₙ₋₁+c₂aₙ₋₂，有几何数列形式的解：aₙ=rⁿ 满足递推当且仅当 r²=c₁r+c₂，即特征方程。若两根 r₁≠r₂，则一切解都形如 aₙ=A·r₁ⁿ+B·r₂ⁿ：递推是线性的，解可以相加和数乘，两个初值定出 A、B。重根 r 对应 (A+Bn)rⁿ，更高阶同理。斐波那契的特征方程 r²=r+1 的根是 φ=(1+√5)/2≈1.618 与 ψ=(1−√5)/2≈−0.618，由 F₀=0、F₁=1 得比内公式 Fₙ=(φⁿ−ψⁿ)/√5。因为 |ψ|<1，ψⁿ 一项逐渐消失，Fₙ 按 φⁿ 增长。

example.en: Solve aₙ = 5aₙ₋₁ − 6aₙ₋₂ with a₀ = 0, a₁ = 1. The characteristic equation r² = 5r − 6 has roots 2 and 3, so aₙ = A·2ⁿ + B·3ⁿ; A + B = 0 and 2A + 3B = 1 give A = −1, B = 1, hence aₙ = 3ⁿ − 2ⁿ (0, 1, 5, 19, …). Checking Binet: F₁₀ = 55, and φ¹⁰/√5 ≈ 55.004.
example.zh: 解 aₙ=5aₙ₋₁−6aₙ₋₂，a₀=0，a₁=1。特征方程 r²=5r−6 的根为 2 和 3，故 aₙ=A·2ⁿ+B·3ⁿ；由 A+B=0、2A+3B=1 得 A=−1、B=1，所以 aₙ=3ⁿ−2ⁿ（0, 1, 5, 19, …）。验证比内公式：F₁₀=55，而 φ¹⁰/√5≈55.004。

image.en: Five sunflowers stand in a row, each exactly 1.618 times as tall as the one before, the last towering over everyone. In front, three little daisies shrink the other way, each 0.618 times the last and alternating white and black. A botanist in a mortarboard holds up a magnifier: the giants grow like φⁿ, while the daisies, ψⁿ, fade away.
image.zh: 五株向日葵排成一排，每株恰好是前一株的 1.618 倍高，最后一株高过所有人。前面三朵小雏菊反向缩小，每朵是前一朵的 0.618 倍，黑白交替。戴学位帽的植物学家举着放大镜：巨人们按 φⁿ 增长，而雏菊 ψⁿ 渐渐消失。

thing.zh: 按 1.618 倍长高的向日葵

means.en: the geometric solution φⁿ, from the dominant root
means.zh: 几何解 φⁿ，来自主导根

means.en: ψⁿ with ψ ≈ −0.618: the sign flips and the size dies out
try aₙ = rⁿ: then r must solve r² = r + 1
means.zh: 试探 aₙ=rⁿ，r 须满足 r²=r+1

summary.en: Encode a sequence a₀, a₁, a₂, … as the power series Σ aₙxⁿ, then count and solve recurrences with algebra.
summary.zh: 把数列 a₀, a₁, a₂, … 编码成幂级数 Σaₙxⁿ，再用代数运算来计数、解递推。

explain.en: The ordinary generating function of a sequence (aₙ) is the formal power series A(x) = Σ aₙxⁿ; Herbert Wilf called it a clothesline on which we hang up a sequence for display. The basic example is 1/(1 − x) = 1 + x + x² + …, which generates 1, 1, 1, …. Multiplying generating functions convolves their coefficients: the coefficient of xⁿ in A(x)B(x) is Σ aₖbₙ₋ₖ, which counts the ways to split n between two independent choices. Recurrences become algebraic equations: for Fibonacci, Σ Fₙxⁿ = x/(1 − x − x²), and partial fractions recover Binet's formula. As formal series they need no convergence; analysis enters only when we plug in numbers.
explain.zh: 数列 (aₙ) 的普通生成函数是形式幂级数 A(x)=Σaₙxⁿ；赫伯特·威尔夫（Herbert Wilf）把它比作一根晾衣绳，把数列挂出来展示。最基本的例子是 1/(1−x)=1+x+x²+…，它生成 1, 1, 1, …。生成函数相乘就是系数做卷积：A(x)B(x) 中 xⁿ 的系数是 Σaₖbₙ₋ₖ，正好计数把 n 分给两个独立选择的方式。递推变成代数方程：斐波那契数列的生成函数是 x/(1−x−x²)，部分分式分解即得比内公式。形式级数不必考虑收敛，只有代入数值时才需要分析。

example.en: Ways to pay n cents with 1¢ and 2¢ coins: (1 + x + x² + …)(1 + x² + x⁴ + …) = 1/((1 − x)(1 − x²)) = 1 + x + 2x² + 2x³ + 3x⁴ + …, so 4¢ can be paid in 3 ways (1+1+1+1, 1+1+2, 2+2), and n cents in ⌊n/2⌋ + 1 ways. Likewise (1 + x)ⁿ = Σ C(n, k)xᵏ generates the binomial coefficients.
example.zh: 用 1 分和 2 分硬币凑 n 分：(1+x+x²+…)(1+x²+x⁴+…)=1/((1−x)(1−x²))=1+x+2x²+2x³+3x⁴+…，所以凑 4 分有 3 种方法（1+1+1+1、1+1+2、2+2），凑 n 分有 ⌊n/2⌋+1 种。同理 (1+x)ⁿ=ΣC(n,k)xᵏ 生成二项式系数。

image.en: A low number line, like a clothesline, is marked 1, x, x², x³, x⁴, and behind each mark rises a tower of gold coins, 1, 1, 2, 2 and 3 stacks high. A robot cashier takes coins from two jars, copper 1¢ coins and silver 2¢ coins; every way of combining a handful from each jar adds one stack to the tower over its total.
image.zh: 一条像晾衣绳的矮数轴上标着 1、x、x²、x³、x⁴，每个刻度后面立着一座金币塔，高 1、1、2、2、3 摞。机器人收银员从两个罐子里取币：一罐铜色 1 分币，一罐银色 2 分币；两罐各取一把的每种组合，都给对应总额的那座塔添上一摞。

thing.zh: 标着 x 幂次的数轴

means.en: the clothesline: the slot xⁿ holds the n-th term
means.zh: 晾衣绳：xⁿ 的位置挂第 n 项

means.en: coefficients: the ways to pay 0 to 4 cents
means.zh: 系数：凑 0 到 4 分的方法数

means.en: the factors 1/(1 − x) and 1/(1 − x²)
multiplying series convolves the counts
means.zh: 级数相乘就是系数卷积

summary.en: Vertices and edges on the waterfront: degrees, trees, tours across bridges and colourings.
summary.zh: 码头上的顶点与边：度数、树、过桥的回路与着色。

summary.en: In every graph the degrees add up to twice the number of edges, so the number of odd-degree vertices is even.
summary.zh: 任何图中各顶点的度数之和等于边数的两倍，因此奇度顶点的个数必为偶数。

explain.en: A graph G = (V, E) consists of vertices and edges, each edge joining two vertices; the degree deg(v) is the number of edges at v. Handshake lemma: Σ deg(v) = 2|E|, because each edge has two ends and is counted once at each, a typical double-counting argument. (A loop counts twice at its vertex, so the identity holds for multigraphs too.) Consequence: the degree sum is even, so the number of vertices of odd degree is even. Graphs model networks, maps, dependencies and state spaces; degrees are the first thing to compute, and this parity fact drives proofs about Euler tours and planar graphs.
explain.zh: 图 G=(V,E) 由顶点和边组成，每条边连接两个顶点；顶点 v 的度 deg(v) 是与它相连的边数。握手引理：Σdeg(v)=2|E|，因为每条边有两个端点，在两端各被数一次，这是典型的“算两次”论证。（自环在其顶点处算两次，所以对多重图同样成立。）推论：度数之和是偶数，所以奇度顶点的个数是偶数。图可以刻画网络、地图、依赖关系和状态空间；度数是首先要算的量，而这个奇偶性事实是欧拉回路和平面图证明的基础。

example.en: Can 7 guests at a party each shake hands with exactly 3 others? No: the degree sum would be 7 × 3 = 21, which is odd, but it must equal 2|E|. In the scene's graph the degrees are 2, 2, 3 and 1: the sum 8 = 2 × 4 edges, and exactly two vertices have odd degree. A cube has 8 corners of degree 3, so it has 8 × 3/2 = 12 edges.
example.zh: 派对上 7 位客人能否每人恰好与 3 人握手？不能：度数和将是 7×3=21，为奇数，而它必须等于 2|E|。场景中的图度数为 2、2、3、1：和为 8=2×4 条边，且恰有两个奇度顶点。立方体有 8 个 3 度顶点，所以有 8×3/2=12 条棱。

image.en: On the dock, three sailors and a dog are linked by heavy iron chains. The sailors form a triangle, and one of them also holds the dog's chain. Every chain has two ends, one at each of two sailors (or the dog). The sailor with three chains wears red, and so does the red setter on its single chain: the odd-degree vertices always come in pairs.
image.zh: 码头上，三名水手和一条狗被粗铁链连在一起。三名水手连成三角形，其中一人还牵着狗的链子。每根铁链都有两端，分别连着两名水手（或那条狗）。握着三根链子的水手穿红衣，只连一根链子的红毛猎犬也是红色：奇度顶点总是成对出现。

means.en: vertices
edges: each has exactly two ends
degrees 2, 2, 3, 1; sum 8 = 2 × 4 edges
odd-degree vertices come in pairs

summary.en: A tree is a connected graph with no cycles: on n vertices it has exactly n − 1 edges and a unique path between any two vertices.
summary.zh: 树是没有圈的连通图：n 个顶点的树恰有 n−1 条边，任意两点之间路径唯一。

explain.en: A tree is a connected acyclic graph. For a graph T on n vertices the following are equivalent: T is a tree; any two vertices are joined by exactly one path; T is connected with n − 1 edges; T is acyclic with n − 1 edges. A tree is minimally connected (removing any edge disconnects it) and maximally acyclic (adding any edge creates exactly one cycle). Every tree with n ≥ 2 has at least two leaves, vertices of degree 1; removing a leaf leaves a tree, which proves the n − 1 count by induction. A spanning tree of a connected graph G is a tree containing all of G's vertices. One always exists: delete an edge of some cycle until none remain. BFS, DFS, Kruskal and Prim all build them.
explain.zh: 树是连通且无圈的图。对 n 个顶点的图 T，下列说法等价：T 是树；任意两顶点之间恰有一条路径；T 连通且有 n−1 条边；T 无圈且有 n−1 条边。树是“最小连通”的（删去任一条边就不再连通），也是“最大无圈”的（添上任一条边恰好产生一个圈）。n≥2 的树至少有两片叶子（度为 1 的顶点）；删去一片叶子仍是树，归纳即得边数 n−1。连通图 G 的生成树是包含 G 全部顶点的树。它总是存在：不断删去某个圈上的一条边，直到没有圈。BFS、DFS、Kruskal 和 Prim 算法都能构造生成树。

example.en: A 3 × 3 fishing net has 9 knots and 12 strings. Any spanning tree keeps all 9 knots and exactly 8 strings, so 12 − 8 = 4 strings must be cut, one for each square mesh. A directory tree with 1,000 folders has 999 parent links. The complete graph K₄ has 4⁴⁻² = 16 spanning trees (Cayley's formula nⁿ⁻²).
example.zh: 3×3 的渔网有 9 个结、12 根绳。任何生成树都保留全部 9 个结和恰好 8 根绳，所以要剪断 12−8=4 根，每个方格网眼剪一根。有 1000 个文件夹的目录树有 999 条父子链接。完全图 K₄ 有 4⁴⁻²=16 棵生成树（凯莱公式 nⁿ⁻²）。

image.en: On the quay a square fishing net hangs on its frame, full of loops. A fisherman with giant scissors snips one string out of every mesh, careful never to cut the net in two. Beside it stands the result: a branching frame with no loops left that still holds every knot. Cut strings lie in a little heap on the boards.
image.zh: 码头上，一张方格渔网挂在架子上，满是网眼。渔夫拿着巨大的剪刀，从每个网眼剪掉一根绳，小心不把网剪成两半。旁边立着成品：一副分叉的绳架，一个圈也没有了，却仍连着每一个结。剪下的绳头在木板上堆成一小堆。

means.en: a connected graph full of cycles
delete an edge on a cycle: the graph stays connected
means.zh: 删去圈上的一条边，图仍连通

means.en: a spanning tree: every knot kept, n − 1 strings
means.zh: 生成树：保留所有结，只剩 n−1 根绳

means.en: the |E| − (n − 1) edges removed

summary.en: An Euler circuit uses every edge once and exists iff the graph is connected with all degrees even; a Hamilton cycle visits every vertex once.
summary.zh: 欧拉回路经过每条边恰好一次，存在当且仅当图连通且度数全为偶数；哈密顿圈经过每个顶点恰好一次。

explain.en: An Euler circuit is a closed walk that uses every edge exactly once. Euler (1736) showed that a connected graph has one if and only if every vertex has even degree: each visit to a vertex uses two of its edges, and conversely, when all degrees are even, cycles can be spliced together until every edge is used (Hierholzer's algorithm, linear time). A connected graph has an open Euler trail exactly when it has two odd vertices, which are its ends. A Hamilton cycle visits every vertex exactly once instead. It sounds similar but is far harder: deciding whether one exists is NP-complete, and there is no simple degree test (Dirac's condition, n ≥ 3 and every degree ≥ n/2, is sufficient but not necessary).
explain.zh: 欧拉回路是经过每条边恰好一次的闭合路线。欧拉（1736）证明：连通图有欧拉回路当且仅当每个顶点的度都是偶数——每次经过一个顶点都要用掉它的两条边；反过来，度数全为偶数时，可以把若干个圈拼接起来直到用完所有边（Hierholzer 算法，线性时间）。连通图恰有两个奇度顶点时，有不闭合的欧拉路径，两端正是这两个顶点。哈密顿圈则要求经过每个顶点恰好一次。听起来相似，难度却天差地别：判定它是否存在是 NP 完全问题，也没有简单的度数判据（狄拉克条件“n≥3 且每个顶点度≥n/2”是充分而非必要条件）。

example.en: Königsberg had four land masses joined by seven bridges, with degrees 5, 3, 3 and 3. All four are odd, so no walk crosses every bridge exactly once, closed or not.
