A Hamilton cycle is easy, though: north bank, big island, south bank, east island, back to the north bank. The complete graph Kₙ (n ≥ 3) always has a Hamilton cycle, and has an Euler circuit exactly when n is odd.
example.zh: 柯尼斯堡有四块陆地、七座桥，各陆地的度数为 5、3、3、3。四个都是奇数，所以不存在每座桥恰好走一次的路线，无论是否回到起点。哈密顿圈却很容易：北岸、大岛、南岸、东岛，再回北岸。完全图 Kₙ（n≥3）总有哈密顿圈，而有欧拉回路当且仅当 n 为奇数。

image.en: A stone-rimmed pool plays the river Pregel. Two rocky islands sit in it, joined to each other and to the near and far banks by seven little wooden bridges. A gentleman in a top hat stands on the big island and shrugs: wherever he starts, some bridge is left uncrossed. Meanwhile a duck paddles round, calmly visiting each of the four land masses once and returning home.
image.zh: 一方石沿水池扮作普雷格尔河。池中两座石岛，由七座小木桥彼此相连，并连到前后两岸。戴高礼帽的绅士站在大岛上耸肩：无论从哪里出发，总有一座桥走不到。一只鸭子却悠闲地划水，四块陆地各到一次，又回到原处。

means.en: 4 vertices (the land masses)
7 edges; degrees 5, 3, 3, 3
odd degrees: no Euler circuit or trail
means.zh: 有奇度顶点：没有欧拉回路或路径

means.en: a Hamilton cycle: each vertex exactly once
means.zh: 哈密顿圈：每个顶点恰好一次

summary.en: A connected plane graph has V − E + F = 2; K₅ and K₃,₃ cannot be drawn without crossings; four colours suffice for any map.
summary.zh: 连通平面图满足 V−E+F=2；K₅ 与 K₃,₃ 无法无交叉地画出；任何地图四种颜色就够。

explain.en: A graph is planar if it can be drawn in the plane with no crossing edges. For a connected planar drawing with V vertices, E edges and F faces (counting the outer face), Euler's formula V − E + F = 2 holds. If V ≥ 3, every face is bounded by at least 3 edges and every edge borders at most 2 faces, so E ≤ 3V − 6; K₅ has 10 > 9 edges, so it is not planar. Without triangles the bound is E ≤ 2V − 4, which rules out K₃,₃ (9 > 8). By Kuratowski's theorem these two are essentially the only obstructions. The four colour theorem (Appel and Haken, 1976, computer-assisted) says every planar graph can be properly coloured with 4 colours. A graph is 2-colourable exactly when it is bipartite: it has no odd cycle.
explain.zh: 能画在平面上且边互不交叉的图叫平面图。对连通的平面画法，设有 V 个顶点、E 条边、F 个面（含外部面），则欧拉公式 V−E+F=2 成立。若 V≥3，每个面至少由 3 条边围成，每条边至多与 2 个面相邻，故 E≤3V−6；K₅ 有 10>9 条边，不是平面图。无三角形时界变为 E≤2V−4，从而排除 K₃,₃（9>8）。由库拉托夫斯基定理，本质上只有这两种障碍。四色定理（1976 年 Appel 与 Haken 借助计算机证明）：每个平面图都能用 4 种颜色正常着色。图可 2 着色当且仅当它是二部图，即没有奇圈。

example.en: A cube drawn flat has V = 8, E = 12, F = 6, and 8 − 12 + 6 = 2. The three-utilities puzzle (join 3 houses to water, gas and electricity without crossings) asks for a planar drawing of K₃,₃, so it has no solution on a plane, though it does on a mug with a handle (a torus). Colouring a map is colouring the graph of neighbouring countries, so four colours suffice.
example.zh: 立方体压平后 V=8、E=12、F=6，8−12+6=2。三家三供问题（把 3 座房子分别接上水、煤气和电，管线互不交叉）就是要把 K₃,₃ 画成平面图，所以在平面上无解；但在带把手的杯子（环面）上可以做到。给地图上色就是给“国家相邻图”着色，四种颜色足够。

image.en: Three cottages stand at the back of the quay; in front of them are a well for water, a blue gas flame and a glowing light bulb. A plumber in a hard hat has laid eight pipes and shrugs at the ninth: every route crosses a pipe already laid. Four paint buckets, red, yellow, green and blue, wait along the front, enough to colour any map.
image.zh: 码头后排立着三座小屋，前面是供水的井、一簇蓝色煤气火焰和一只发光的灯泡。戴安全帽的水管工已经铺好八根管子，对着第九根耸肩：怎么走都会和已有的管子交叉。前排摆着红、黄、绿、蓝四桶油漆，足以给任何地图上色。

means.en: the two sides of K₃,₃

thing.en: the plumber stuck on pipe nine
thing.zh: 卡在第九根管的水管工

means.en: K₃,₃ is not planar: E = 9 > 2V − 4 = 8
the four colour theorem: 4 colours suffice for planar graphs
means.zh: 四色定理：平面图 4 色足够

summary.en: Limits made rigorous with ε and δ, and the two great operations built on them: differentiation and integration.
summary.zh: 用 ε 与 δ 把极限说严格，再在其上建立两大运算：微分与积分。

summary.en: The completeness of the real line, and the ε-language of limits and continuity.
summary.zh: 实数轴的完备性，以及描述极限与连续的 ε 语言。

summary.en: Every non-empty set of reals that is bounded above has a least upper bound; the rationals have gaps, such as at √2.
summary.zh: 实数中每个有上界的非空集合都有最小上界（上确界）；有理数却有缺口，比如 √2 处。

explain.en: The least upper bound property (completeness axiom): if S ⊆ ℝ is non-empty and bounded above, there is a real number sup S that is an upper bound of S and is ≤ every other upper bound. ℚ fails this: S = {q ∈ ℚ : q² < 2} is bounded above in ℚ but has no least upper bound in ℚ, because its supremum would have to be √2, which is irrational. A key consequence: every monotone bounded sequence converges, an increasing one to the supremum of its terms. Completeness has several equivalent forms, such as the nested interval property or the convergence of every Cauchy sequence (each together with the Archimedean property). The intermediate value theorem, extreme values and integrals all depend on it.
explain.zh: 确界原理（完备性公理）：若 S⊆ℝ 非空且有上界，则存在实数 sup S，它是 S 的上界，且不大于 S 的任何其他上界。ℚ 不满足这一点：S={q∈ℚ : q²<2} 在 ℚ 中有上界，却没有有理的最小上界，因为上确界只能是无理数 √2。重要推论：单调有界数列必收敛，递增数列收敛到其各项的上确界。完备性有多种等价形式，例如闭区间套性质、柯西数列必收敛（各自配合阿基米德性质）。介值定理、最值定理和积分的存在都依赖它。

example.en: The increasing rational sequence 1, 1.4, 1.41, 1.414, 1.4142, … (decimal truncations of √2) is bounded above by 1.5, so in ℝ it converges, to its supremum √2; inside ℚ it has no limit at all. Likewise aₙ = (1 + 1/n)ⁿ is increasing and bounded above by 3, so it converges, and its limit defines e ≈ 2.71828.
example.zh: 递增的有理数列 1, 1.4, 1.41, 1.414, 1.4142, …（√2 的十进制截断）以 1.5 为上界，所以在 ℝ 中收敛，极限是上确界 √2；在 ℚ 中它却根本没有极限。同理，aₙ=(1+1/n)ⁿ 递增且以 3 为上界，所以收敛，其极限就定义了 e≈2.71828。

image.en: A frog hops to the right in front of the rational number line, marked 1, 1.4, 1.41, 1.414 …; each hop is half the one before, so its snapshots shrink and crowd together. Just where it is heading, a stone well gapes, with a sign: √2 ∉ ℚ. An astronomer in a wizard's hat points at the hole that only the real line can fill.
image.zh: 一只青蛙在有理数轴前向右跳，数轴上标着 1、1.4、1.41、1.414……；每一跳都只有上一跳的一半，它的身影越来越小、越挤越密。就在它要去的地方，一口石井张着嘴，旁边立牌写着 √2∉ℚ。戴巫师帽的天文学家指着这个洞：只有实数轴能把它填上。

means.en: an increasing sequence that is bounded above
means.zh: 单调递增且有上界的数列

thing.en: the well where it is heading

means.en: the gap in ℚ: the supremum √2 is missing
means.zh: ℚ 的缺口：上确界 √2 不在其中

thing.en: the astronomer pointing at the hole

means.en: ℝ is complete: every bounded set has a sup
means.zh: ℝ 完备：有上界的集合必有上确界

summary.en: aₙ → L means: for every ε > 0 there is an N such that |aₙ − L| < ε for all n > N.
summary.zh: aₙ→L 的意思是：对任意 ε>0，存在 N，使得当 n>N 时总有 |aₙ−L|<ε。

explain.en: A sequence (aₙ) converges to L if ∀ε > 0 ∃N such that n > N ⇒ |aₙ − L| < ε. Read it as a game: whatever tolerance ε a sceptic names, you can name a point N after which every term stays within ε of L. N may depend on ε, smaller ε usually needs a larger N, and finitely many early terms never matter. Limits are unique, convergent sequences are bounded, and limits respect sums, products and quotients (when the limit of the denominator is nonzero). To show that aₙ does not converge to L, negate the definition: ∃ε > 0 such that for every N some n > N has |aₙ − L| ≥ ε. For example, (−1)ⁿ diverges: its terms keep jumping 2 apart, so with ε = 1 no L can hold them all.
explain.zh: 数列 (aₙ) 收敛到 L，是指 ∀ε>0 ∃N，使得 n>N ⇒ |aₙ−L|<ε。可以把它看成一场游戏：无论质疑者给出多小的容差 ε，你都能指出一个位置 N，此后每一项与 L 的距离都小于 ε。N 可以依赖 ε，ε 越小通常 N 越大，前面有限多项无关紧要。极限唯一，收敛数列有界，极限与加、乘、除（分母极限非零）可交换。要证明 aₙ 不收敛到 L，就取否定：∃ε>0，使对每个 N 都有某个 n>N 满足 |aₙ−L|≥ε。例如 (−1)ⁿ 发散：各项不停地相差 2，取 ε=1 时没有哪个 L 能把它们全部框住。

example.en: Claim: 1/n → 0. Given ε > 0, choose N ≥ 1/ε, which exists by the Archimedean property. Then n > N gives |1/n − 0| = 1/n < 1/N ≤ ε. For ε = 0.01, N = 100 works: every term after the 100th is below 0.01. Likewise (n + 1)/n → 1, since |(n + 1)/n − 1| = 1/n.
example.zh: 命题：1/n→0。任给 ε>0，取 N≥1/ε（由阿基米德性质可以取到）。当 n>N 时 |1/n−0|=1/n<1/N≤ε。若 ε=0.01，取 N=100 即可：第 100 项之后的每一项都小于 0.01。同理 (n+1)/n→1，因为 |(n+1)/n−1|=1/n。

image.en: A huge archery target stands under the dome. Two early darts fell short and lie on the floor, but the later ones cluster in the bullseye. A sceptic with a megaphone calls out a ring, ε = 0.01, and the dart thrower chalks her answer on the scoreboard, N = 100: every dart after the hundredth lands inside that ring. Whatever ring is named, she has an answer.
image.zh: 穹顶下立着一面巨大的箭靶。早先两支飞镖没射到，掉在地上，后来的飞镖却都扎在靶心周围。拿扩音器的质疑者喊出一圈：ε=0.01；投镖手在记分板上写下答案 N=100——第一百支以后的每一支都落在这圈之内。无论点哪一圈，她都答得上来。

means.en: the limit L
a tolerance ε; any positive number may be named
means.zh: 容差 ε，可以是任意正数

means.en: a point after which all terms stay within ε
means.zh: 此后所有项都落在 ε 之内

means.en: finitely many early terms don't matter
means.zh: 前面有限多项无关紧要

summary.en: f(x) → L as x → a if for every ε > 0 some δ > 0 keeps |f(x) − L| < ε whenever 0 < |x − a| < δ.
summary.zh: x→a 时 f(x)→L：对任意 ε>0，存在 δ>0，使得当 0<|x−a|<δ 时 |f(x)−L|<ε。

explain.en: lim f(x) = L as x → a means ∀ε > 0 ∃δ > 0 such that 0 < |x − a| < δ ⇒ |f(x) − L| < ε. It is a challenge and a response: the challenger demands an output tolerance ε, and the responder must find an input tolerance δ that guarantees it. The condition 0 < |x − a| ignores the point a itself, so f need not even be defined there. f is continuous at a if f(a) is defined and the limit equals f(a); equivalently, the same condition holds with |x − a| < δ. Sums, products, quotients (where the denominator is nonzero) and compositions of continuous functions are continuous, so every polynomial is continuous everywhere. Continuity is the hypothesis of the intermediate and extreme value theorems.
explain.zh: x→a 时 lim f(x)=L 的含义是：∀ε>0 ∃δ>0，使得 0<|x−a|<δ ⇒ |f(x)−L|<ε。这是一问一答：挑战者要求输出误差小于 ε，应答者必须找到能保证它的输入误差 δ。条件 0<|x−a| 不看 a 点本身，所以 f 在 a 处甚至可以没有定义。若 f(a) 有定义且极限等于 f(a)，就说 f 在 a 处连续；等价地，把条件换成 |x−a|<δ。连续函数的和、积、商（分母不为零处）与复合仍连续，所以多项式处处连续。连续性是介值定理与最值定理的前提。

example.en: f(x) = 2x + 1 at a = 3: |f(x) − 7| = 2|x − 3|, so δ = ε/2 works. f(x) = x² at a = 2: if |x − 2| < 1 then |x + 2| < 5, so |x² − 4| = |x − 2|·|x + 2| < 5|x − 2|, and δ = min(1, ε/5) works. The step function equal to 1 for x ≥ 0 and 0 for x < 0 is not continuous at 0: for ε = 1/2 no δ works.
example.zh: f(x)=2x+1 在 a=3 处：|f(x)−7|=2|x−3|，取 δ=ε/2 即可。f(x)=x² 在 a=2 处：若 |x−2|<1，则 |x+2|<5，于是 |x²−4|=|x−2|·|x+2|<5|x−2|，取 δ=min(1, ε/5) 即可。x≥0 时取 1、x<0 时取 0 的阶跃函数在 0 处不连续：取 ε=1/2，任何 δ 都不行。

image.en: Under the dome, a sceptic in a beret calls out "ε = 0.01": the star must stay within ε of the crosshair. The astronomer at the brass telescope opens a giant drawing compass and answers "δ = 0.005": aim within δ of the right angle and the star's image is guaranteed to stay within ε. However small the sceptic's ε, she always finds a δ.
image.zh: 穹顶下，戴贝雷帽的质疑者喊道：“ε=0.01”——星星必须待在十字线 ε 范围之内。黄铜望远镜旁的天文学家张开一把巨大的圆规回答：“δ=0.005”——只要瞄准偏差小于 δ，星像就一定偏不出 ε。无论质疑者的 ε 多小，她总能找到一个 δ。

means.en: the output tolerance around L, demanded first
means.zh: 先提出的输出误差（L 附近）

thing.zh: 张开到 δ 的圆规

means.en: the input tolerance around a, found in reply
means.zh: 随后找到的输入误差（a 附近）

means.en: the function f: aiming angle in, image position out
means.zh: 函数 f：输入瞄准角，输出星像位置

thing.en: the star held in the crosshair

summary.en: A continuous function on [a, b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b); a sign change forces a root.
summary.zh: 闭区间 [a,b] 上的连续函数取遍 f(a) 与 f(b) 之间的每一个值；变号必有零点。

explain.en: If f is continuous on [a, b] and y lies between f(a) and f(b), then f(c) = y for some c in [a, b]. In particular, if f(a) < 0 < f(b), then f has a root in (a, b). The proof takes c = sup{x ∈ [a, b] : f(x) < y} and needs completeness; over ℚ the theorem fails, since x² − 2 changes sign on [1, 2] but has no rational root. Bisection turns it into an algorithm: test the sign at the midpoint and keep the half on which the sign changes; after k steps the root is trapped in an interval of length (b − a)/2ᵏ. Its companion, the extreme value theorem, says that a continuous function on a closed bounded interval attains a maximum and a minimum.
explain.zh: 若 f 在 [a,b] 上连续，y 介于 f(a) 与 f(b) 之间，则存在 c∈[a,b] 使 f(c)=y。特别地，若 f(a)<0<f(b)，则 f 在 (a,b) 内有零点。证明取 c=sup{x∈[a,b] : f(x)<y}，要用到完备性；在 ℚ 上定理不成立：x²−2 在 [1,2] 上变号，却没有有理根。二分法把它变成算法：看中点的符号，保留变号的那一半；k 步之后，根被锁定在长为 (b−a)/2ᵏ 的区间里。它的姊妹定理是最值定理：有界闭区间上的连续函数必取到最大值与最小值。

example.en: f(x) = x³ − x − 1 has f(1) = −1 and f(2) = 5, so it has a root in (1, 2). Bisection: f(1.5) = 0.875 > 0, so the root is in (1, 1.5); f(1.25) ≈ −0.297 < 0, so it is in (1.25, 1.5); continuing gives the root ≈ 1.3247. The same argument shows that every real polynomial of odd degree has a real root.

image.en: A mountain rises under the dome, with a flat bank of cloud lying across its middle. A hiker with a lantern sets off from the foot, below the cloud, for the flag on the summit, far above it. However the trail twists, he cannot reach the top without passing through the cloud layer: a continuous climb hits every height in between. The flag marks the highest point, and the climb does reach it.
image.zh: 穹顶下耸立着一座山，一层平平的云横在半山腰。提灯的登山者从云层下方的山脚出发，要去云层上方的山顶插旗处。无论山路怎样曲折，他都必须穿过云层才能登顶：连续的攀登会经过中间的每一个高度。山顶的旗标出最高点，而这一点确实能够到达。

thing.en: the trail from foot to summit

means.en: a continuous f on [a, b]
a value y between f(a) and f(b)
means.zh: 介于 f(a) 与 f(b) 之间的值 y

means.en: some c with f(c) = y
extreme value theorem: the maximum is attained
means.zh: 最值定理：最大值能取到

summary.en: Instantaneous rates of change, from the speed of a galloping horse to polynomial copies of a function.
summary.zh: 瞬时变化率：从奔马的速度，到函数的多项式仿制品。

summary.en: f′(a) is the limit of (f(a + h) − f(a))/h as h → 0: the slope of the tangent and the instantaneous rate of change.
summary.zh: f′(a) 是差商 (f(a+h)−f(a))/h 在 h→0 时的极限：切线的斜率，瞬时变化率。

explain.en: The derivative of f at a is f′(a) = lim (f(a + h) − f(a))/h as h → 0, if the limit exists. Geometrically, the slopes of secant lines through (a, f(a)) approach the slope of the tangent line; physically, average velocities over shorter and shorter intervals approach the instantaneous velocity. Differentiability at a implies continuity at a, but not conversely: |x| is continuous at 0 and has no derivative there. The rules follow from the definition: (f + g)′ = f′ + g′, the product rule (fg)′ = f′g + fg′, and the chain rule (f ∘ g)′(x) = f′(g(x))·g′(x). Near a, f(a + h) ≈ f(a) + f′(a)h is the best linear approximation.
explain.zh: f 在 a 处的导数是 f′(a)=lim(f(a+h)−f(a))/h（h→0，若极限存在）。几何上，过 (a,f(a)) 的割线斜率趋于切线斜率；物理上，越来越短的时段内的平均速度趋于瞬时速度。在 a 处可导蕴含在 a 处连续，反之不然：|x| 在 0 处连续却不可导。运算法则都由定义推出：(f+g)′=f′+g′，乘积法则 (fg)′=f′g+fg′，链式法则 (f∘g)′(x)=f′(g(x))·g′(x)。在 a 附近，f(a+h)≈f(a)+f′(a)h 是最好的线性近似。

example.en: A chariot's position is s(t) = t² metres after t seconds. Its average speed on [3, 3 + h] is ((3 + h)² − 9)/h = 6 + h: 7 m/s for h = 1, 6.1 for h = 0.1, 6.01 for h = 0.01, tending to s′(3) = 6 m/s. Chain rule: d/dx sin(x²) = cos(x²)·2x. Product rule: d/dx (x·eˣ) = eˣ + x·eˣ.
example.zh: 战车 t 秒时的位置是 s(t)=t² 米。区间 [3,3+h] 上的平均速度为 ((3+h)²−9)/h=6+h：h=1 时 7 米/秒，h=0.1 时 6.1，h=0.01 时 6.01，趋于 s′(3)=6 米/秒。链式法则：d/dx sin(x²)=cos(x²)·2x。乘积法则：d/dx(x·eˣ)=eˣ+x·eˣ。

image.en: A horse gallops across the arena sand. In front of it stand three giant stopwatches, each smaller than the last: the first timed the horse over a whole second, the next over a tenth, the smallest over a hundredth. Their average speeds, 7, 6.1 and 6.01 metres per second, close in on a single number. A referee in a cap points at the horse: that limit is its speed at this very instant.
image.zh: 一匹马在竞技场的沙地上疾驰。它前面立着三只巨大的秒表，一只比一只小：第一只计了整整一秒，第二只计十分之一秒，最小的计百分之一秒。它们测得的平均速度 7、6.1、6.01 米/秒向同一个数逼近。戴帽子的裁判指着马：这个极限就是它此时此刻的速度。

means.en: position s(t); its speed right now is s′(t)
means.zh: 位置 s(t)；此刻速度是 s′(t)

means.en: h → 0: intervals of 1, 0.1 and 0.01 s
difference quotients (s(3 + h) − s(3))/h → 6

thing.en: the referee pointing at the horse

means.en: the derivative is the limit of those averages
means.zh: 导数就是这些平均值的极限

summary.en: If f is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), then f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a) for some c in (a, b).
summary.zh: f 在 [a,b] 连续、在 (a,b) 可导，则有 c∈(a,b) 使 f′(c)=(f(b)−f(a))/(b−a)。

explain.en: If f is continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), some c in (a, b) has f′(c) = (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a): somewhere the tangent is parallel to the chord. The case f(a) = f(b) is Rolle's theorem, proved with the extreme value theorem: unless f is constant, it attains a maximum or minimum at an interior point, where the derivative is 0. The general case applies Rolle to f minus the chord. The theorem turns facts about f′ into facts about f: f′ = 0 on an interval makes f constant, f′ > 0 makes f increasing, and |f′| ≤ M gives |f(x) − f(y)| ≤ M|x − y|. The hypotheses matter: |x| on [−1, 1] has equal end values but no point with zero derivative.
explain.zh: 若 f 在 [a,b] 上连续、在 (a,b) 内可导，则存在 c∈(a,b) 使 f′(c)=(f(b)−f(a))/(b−a)：某处的切线与弦平行。f(a)=f(b) 的特例是罗尔定理，用最值定理证明：若 f 不是常数，它在内部某点取到最大值或最小值，该点导数为 0。一般情形对“f 减去弦”用罗尔定理即可。它把关于 f′ 的事实变成关于 f 的事实：区间上 f′=0 则 f 为常数，f′>0 则 f 递增，|f′|≤M 则 |f(x)−f(y)|≤M|x−y|。条件不能少：|x| 在 [−1,1] 两端取值相等，却没有导数为 0 的点。

example.en: Speed cameras 10 km apart photograph a car at 12:00 and at 12:05. Its average speed was 10/(5/60) = 120 km/h, so at some instant the speedometer read exactly 120 km/h, and in a 100 km/h zone the car is fined although nobody saw it speeding. For f(x) = x² on [0, 2], the chord slope is 2, and f′(c) = 2c = 2 at c = 1.
example.zh: 两台相距 10 公里的测速相机在 12:00 和 12:05 拍到同一辆车。平均速度为 10÷(5/60)=120 公里/小时，所以某一瞬间车速表恰好指着 120；在限速 100 的路段，即使没人看见它超速，也照样罚款。对 f(x)=x² 在 [0,2] 上，弦的斜率是 2，而 f′(c)=2c=2 在 c=1 处成立。

image.en: A race car tears across the arena between two speed cameras on poles: one stamped 12:00, the other 12:05, ten kilometres apart in the story. A police officer with a stopwatch does the sum, 120 km/h on average, and writes a ticket: somewhere in between, the speedometer must have read exactly 120. The crowd in the stands boos.
image.zh: 一辆赛车在两根立杆上的测速相机之间飞驰：一台记下 12:00，另一台记下 12:05，按故事设定相距 10 公里。拿秒表的警察一算，平均 120 公里/小时，当场开罚单：途中某一刻，车速表一定恰好指着 120。看台上一片嘘声。

means.en: the endpoints a and b, with f(a) and f(b)
means.zh: 端点 a、b 及其函数值

means.en: the chord slope (f(b) − f(a))/(b − a)
some instant c has f′(c) = 120, though we can't say when
means.zh: 必有某刻 c 使 f′(c)=120，但不知是哪刻

means.en: hypotheses: continuous on [a, b], differentiable inside
means.zh: 条件：闭区间连续，开区间可导

title.zh: 泰勒多项式与泰勒级数

summary.en: Near a, approximate f by the polynomial that matches its value and first n derivatives at a; the error is the remainder.
summary.zh: 在 a 附近，用与 f 在 a 处的函数值及前 n 阶导数都相同的多项式逼近 f，误差就是余项。

explain.en: The degree-n Taylor polynomial at a is Tₙ(x) = Σ f⁽ᵏ⁾(a)(x − a)ᵏ/k! for k = 0..n, the unique polynomial of degree ≤ n whose value and first n derivatives at a match f's. The error is the remainder Rₙ = f − Tₙ; in Lagrange's form Rₙ(x) = f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)(x − a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1)! for some ξ between a and x, a direct generalisation of the mean value theorem. Where Rₙ(x) → 0, f equals its Taylor series: eˣ = Σ xⁿ/n! and sin x = x − x³/3! + x⁵/5! − … for every real x. Smoothness alone is not enough: f(x) = e^(−1/x²) with f(0) = 0 has every derivative 0 at 0, so its Taylor series there is identically 0 and equals f only at 0.
explain.zh: f 在 a 处的 n 次泰勒多项式 Tₙ(x)=Σf⁽ᵏ⁾(a)(x−a)ᵏ/k!（k 从 0 到 n），是在 a 处函数值与前 n 阶导数都与 f 相同的唯一一个次数不超过 n 的多项式。误差是余项 Rₙ=f−Tₙ；拉格朗日型余项 Rₙ(x)=f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾(ξ)(x−a)ⁿ⁺¹/(n+1)!（ξ 在 a 与 x 之间），是中值定理的直接推广。在 Rₙ(x)→0 的地方，f 等于它的泰勒级数：对一切实数 x，eˣ=Σxⁿ/n!，sin x=x−x³/3!+x⁵/5!−…。光滑还不够：f(x)=e^(−1/x²)（f(0)=0）在 0 处各阶导数都是 0，其泰勒级数恒为 0，只在 0 点等于 f。

example.en: e ≈ T₄(1) = 1 + 1 + 1/2 + 1/6 + 1/24 ≈ 2.7083. Lagrange's bound puts the error below 3/5! = 0.025, and the true error is about 0.0099. For small angles sin x ≈ x − x³/6: sin 0.1 ≈ 0.0998333, off by only about 8 × 10⁻⁸, roughly the size of the next term, 0.1⁵/5!.

image.en: A bronze champion strikes a fighting pose in the middle of the arena. Three apprentices copy him: the first only stands on the right spot, the second also points the right way, the third matches the crouch as well, and all of them look most like him right at his spot. Behind them hovers a pale ghost that is perfectly flat at that spot, so the apprentices copy it as nothing at all, yet away from the spot it rises.
image.zh: 竞技场中央，一尊青铜冠军像摆出格斗姿势。三名学徒模仿他：第一个只站对了位置，第二个连指的方向也对了，第三个连下蹲的架势都学到了；在冠军站的那一点上，他们最像。后面飘着一个淡淡的幽灵，它在那一点上扁平得看不出任何形状，学徒们照着学，学到的全是“无”；可一离开那一点，它就升了起来。

means.en: the function f near the point a
means.zh: a 点附近的函数 f

means.en: T₀, T₁, T₂: matching value, slope, then curvature at a
means.zh: T₀、T₁、T₂：依次匹配函数值、斜率、弯曲

means.en: the remainder is small near a, not necessarily far away
means.zh: 余项在 a 附近小，远处未必

means.en: e^(−1/x²): all derivatives 0 at 0, series ≡ 0 ≠ f

summary.en: Accumulation as a limit of sums, its link to derivatives, and when infinite sums converge.
summary.zh: 作为和的极限的累积、它与导数的联系，以及无穷求和何时收敛。

summary.en: ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx is the limit of Riemann sums Σ f(xᵢ*)Δxᵢ, areas of thin rectangles, as the partition gets finer.
summary.zh: ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx 是黎曼和 Σf(xᵢ*)Δxᵢ（细长矩形的面积之和）在分割越来越细时的极限。

explain.en: Cut [a, b] into pieces of widths Δxᵢ, pick a sample point xᵢ* in each, and form the Riemann sum Σ f(xᵢ*)Δxᵢ, the signed area of rectangles of height f(xᵢ*). f is Riemann integrable if these sums approach one number as the widest piece shrinks to 0, whatever sample points are chosen; that number is ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx, the signed area between the graph and the x-axis (area below the axis counts as negative). Equivalently, upper and lower sums, using sup and inf on each piece, squeeze together. Continuous functions on [a, b] are integrable, and so are bounded functions with finitely many discontinuities; the indicator of ℚ on [0, 1] is not, since all its upper sums are 1 and all its lower sums 0.
explain.zh: 把 [a,b] 分成宽 Δxᵢ 的小段，每段取一点 xᵢ*，作黎曼和 Σf(xᵢ*)Δxᵢ，即高为 f(xᵢ*) 的矩形的有向面积之和。若无论样本点怎样取，只要最宽的小段趋于 0，这些和都趋于同一个数，就说 f 黎曼可积；这个数记作 ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx，是图像与 x 轴之间的有向面积（轴下方算负）。等价地，上和与下和（每段取上确界与下确界）被夹到一起。[a,b] 上的连续函数可积，只有有限个间断点的有界函数也可积；[0,1] 上 ℚ 的示性函数不可积：上和恒为 1，下和恒为 0。

example.en: ∫₀¹ x² dx with n equal strips and right endpoints: Σ (i/n)²·(1/n) = (n + 1)(2n + 1)/(6n²). For n = 4 this is 45/96 ≈ 0.469, for n = 100 it is 0.33835, and the limit is 1/3. A car with speed v(t) covers a distance ∫ v(t) dt: speed × time, added up over thin slices of time.
example.zh: ∫₀¹x²dx：分成 n 个等宽条、取右端点，Σ(i/n)²·(1/n)=(n+1)(2n+1)/(6n²)。n=4 时为 45/96≈0.469，n=100 时为 0.33835，极限是 1/3。速度为 v(t) 的汽车走过的路程是 ∫v(t)dt：把很短时段内的“速度×时间”加起来。

image.en: A curved garden bridge arches across the back of the stage. In front of it a gardener has stacked wooden crates into six thin columns whose tops climb and fall in steps that follow the arch, a staircase standing in for the curve. The thinner he makes the columns, the smaller the gaps between steps and arch, and the crates' total area closes in on the area under the curve.
image.zh: 一座弧形园林小桥横跨舞台后方。桥前，园丁把木箱垒成六根细柱，柱顶一级级升高又降低，顺着桥拱的弧线，用台阶代替曲线。柱子分得越细，台阶与桥拱之间的缝隙越小，木箱的总面积就越逼近曲线下的面积。

means.en: the graph of f over [a, b]
rectangles of width Δx and height f(xᵢ*)
means.zh: 宽 Δx、高 f(xᵢ*) 的矩形

means.en: the error, which vanishes as the pieces shrink
adding up the Riemann sum Σ f(xᵢ*)Δxᵢ

summary.en: Integration and differentiation undo each other: (d/dx)∫ₐˣ f = f(x), and ∫ₐᵇ f = F(b) − F(a) for any antiderivative F.
summary.zh: 积分与微分互为逆运算：(d/dx)∫ₐˣf=f(x)，且对任一原函数 F 有 ∫ₐᵇf=F(b)−F(a)。

explain.en: Part 1: if f is continuous on [a, b], the accumulation function A(x) = ∫ₐˣ f(t) dt is differentiable with A′(x) = f(x): area piles up at a rate equal to the height of the graph at the moving edge. Part 2: if F is any antiderivative of f, meaning F′ = f on [a, b], then ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). Part 2 replaces a limit of sums by two evaluations; it holds whenever f is integrable and has an antiderivative, and its proof applies the mean value theorem to F on each piece of a partition. Together the parts say that differentiation and integration are inverse operations, linking rates of change to accumulated totals: velocity to distance, density to mass.
explain.zh: 第一部分：若 f 在 [a,b] 上连续，则累积函数 A(x)=∫ₐˣf(t)dt 可导，且 A′(x)=f(x)：面积增长的速率等于移动边界处图像的高度。第二部分：若 F 是 f 的任一原函数，即在 [a,b] 上 F′=f，则 ∫ₐᵇf(x)dx=F(b)−F(a)。第二部分把“和的极限”换成两次代值；只要 f 可积且有原函数就成立，证明是在分割的每一小段上对 F 用中值定理。两部分合起来说明微分与积分互为逆运算，把变化率与累积总量联系起来：速度与路程，密度与质量。

example.en: ∫₀¹ x² dx = [x³/3]₀¹ = 1/3, the same value as the limit of the Riemann sums, with no limit taken. ∫₀^π sin x dx = [−cos x]₀^π = 1 − (−1) = 2. A rain gauge that reads 12 mm at 2 pm and 19 mm at 3 pm means 7 mm fell in that hour, however the rainfall rate varied in between.
example.zh: ∫₀¹x²dx=[x³/3]₀¹=1/3，与黎曼和的极限相同，却不用再求极限。∫₀^π sin x dx=[−cos x]₀^π=1−(−1)=2。雨量计下午 2 点读数 12 毫米、3 点读数 19 毫米，说明这一小时下了 7 毫米，不管中间雨势怎样变化。

image.en: A rain cloud hangs over a wooden rain barrel in the garden, and a tall gauge tube beside it shows the water level. The gardener watches with a stopwatch: the level rises exactly as fast as the rain falls. At 2 pm it read 12 mm and at 3 pm 19 mm, and the sign by the barrel says 19 − 12 = 7: the hour's rain is simply the difference of two readings.
image.zh: 花园里，一朵雨云悬在木制雨水桶上方，桶旁一根高高的刻度管显示水位。园丁拿着秒表观察：水位上升的速度恰好等于下雨的速度。下午 2 点读数 12 毫米，3 点读数 19 毫米，桶边的牌子写着 19−12=7：这一小时的雨量就是两次读数之差。

means.en: the rate f(t)

thing.en: the level in the gauge tube

means.en: the accumulation A(t) = ∫ f, an antiderivative of f
means.zh: 累积量 A(t)=∫f，f 的一个原函数

thing.en: level rising as fast as the rain

means.en: Part 1: A′(t) = f(t)
Part 2: ∫ₐᵇ f = F(b) − F(a)

summary.en: A series converges when its partial sums have a limit: Σ 1/2ⁿ = 1, while the harmonic series Σ 1/n diverges.
summary.zh: 级数收敛，指部分和数列有极限：Σ1/2ⁿ=1，而调和级数 Σ1/n 发散。

explain.en: Σ aₙ converges to S if the partial sums Sₙ = a₁ + … + aₙ converge to S. The terms must tend to 0, but that is not enough. The geometric series Σ rⁿ (n ≥ 0) converges, to 1/(1 − r), exactly when |r| < 1. The harmonic series Σ 1/n diverges: group its terms as 1/2, then 1/3 + 1/4 ≥ 1/2, then four terms ≥ 1/2, and so on. The p-series Σ 1/nᵖ converges iff p > 1. Ratio test: if |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| → L, the series converges absolutely when L < 1 and diverges when L > 1; L = 1 decides nothing. Absolute convergence (Σ |aₙ| converges) implies convergence. The alternating harmonic series 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − … converges to ln 2 only conditionally, and rearranging it can give any sum (Riemann).
explain.zh: 级数 Σaₙ 收敛到 S，是指部分和 Sₙ=a₁+…+aₙ 收敛到 S。通项必须趋于 0，但这还不够。几何级数 Σrⁿ（n≥0）当且仅当 |r|<1 时收敛，和为 1/(1−r)。调和级数 Σ1/n 发散：分组为 1/2，1/3+1/4≥1/2，再四项≥1/2……p 级数 Σ1/nᵖ 当且仅当 p>1 时收敛。比值判别法：若 |aₙ₊₁/aₙ|→L，则 L<1 时绝对收敛，L>1 时发散，L=1 无法判断。绝对收敛（Σ|aₙ| 收敛）蕴含收敛。交错调和级数 1−1/2+1/3−… 收敛到 ln 2，但只是条件收敛，重排后可以得到任意的和（黎曼重排定理）。

example.en: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + … = 1: the partial sums 0.5, 0.75, 0.875, … fall short of 1 by exactly 1/2ⁿ. Harmonic partial sums grow like ln n: H₄ ≈ 2.08 and H₁₀₀₀₀₀₀ ≈ 14.4. So identical blocks, the k-th from the top overhanging the one below by 1/(2k) of a block, can reach out as far as you like; with 4 blocks the top one already clears the edge, since (1/2)(1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4) = 25/24 > 1.
example.zh: 1/2+1/4+1/8+…=1：部分和 0.5、0.75、0.875……与 1 恰好差 1/2ⁿ。调和部分和像 ln n 一样增长：H₄≈2.08，H₁₀₀₀₀₀₀≈14.4。所以一摞相同的积木，从上往下第 k 块比下面一块多伸出 1/(2k) 块长，就能伸到任意远；只用 4 块，顶块就已越过边缘，因为 (1/2)(1+1/2+1/3+1/4)=25/24>1。

image.en: On a garden bench, toy bricks are stacked into a crazy leaning tower: counting from the top, each brick juts out past the one below by 1/2, 1/4, 1/6 and 1/8 of its length, so the top brick hangs wholly beyond the edge. With enough bricks it could reach across the garden: the harmonic series has no finite sum. In front, a runner heads for a dozing tortoise, covering half the remaining distance with each stride; infinitely many strides add up to exactly 1.

summary.en: Vectors, linear maps and the matrices that represent them: from span and basis, through elimination and determinants, to eigenvalues, orthogonality and the SVD.
summary.zh: 向量、线性映射以及表示它们的矩阵：从张成与基，到消元与行列式，再到特征值、正交与奇异值分解。

summary.en: Everything is built from linear combinations: what they reach, and the smallest kit that reaches everything.
summary.zh: 一切都由线性组合搭成：组合能到达哪里，以及能搭出一切的最小零件包。

summary.en: Vectors can be added and scaled; a linear combination a₁v₁ + … + aₖvₖ uses nothing but those two operations.
summary.zh: 向量可以相加，也可以数乘；线性组合 a₁v₁+…+aₖvₖ 只用到这两种运算。

explain.en: A vector in ℝⁿ is an ordered list of n real numbers, drawn as an arrow from the origin. Vectors are added componentwise (tip to tail) and multiplied by scalars (stretched, shrunk or reversed). A linear combination of v₁, …, vₖ is a₁v₁ + … + aₖvₖ for scalars aᵢ. A vector space is any set with these two operations obeying a short list of axioms: addition is associative and commutative, with a zero vector and negatives; scaling distributes, a(u + v) = au + av and (a + b)v = av + bv; and (ab)v = a(bv), 1v = v. Polynomials, matrices and functions ℝ → ℝ obey the same axioms, so every theorem of linear algebra applies to them too. The scalars can come from any field, such as ℝ, ℂ or ℤₚ.
explain.zh: ℝⁿ 中的向量是 n 个实数组成的有序数组，可以画成从原点出发的箭头。向量按分量相加（首尾相接），也可以乘以标量（拉长、缩短或反向）。v₁,…,vₖ 的线性组合（linear combination）就是 a₁v₁+…+aₖvₖ。向量空间是带有这两种运算并满足几条公理的任意集合：加法满足结合律和交换律，有零向量和负向量；数乘满足 a(u+v)=au+av、(a+b)v=av+bv、(ab)v=a(bv)、1v=v。多项式、矩阵、函数 ℝ→ℝ 也满足这些公理，所以线性代数的定理对它们同样成立。标量可以取自任何域，如 ℝ、ℂ 或 ℤₚ。

example.en: Let u = (1, 2) and v = (3, −1). Then u + v = (4, 1), 3u = (3, 6) and 2u − v = (−1, 5). To reach w = (7, 0), solve a + 3b = 7 and 2a − b = 0: a = 1, b = 2, so w = u + 2v. The same moves work for polynomials: (1 + x²) + 2(x − x²) = 1 + 2x − x².

image.en: On the workshop floor a carpenter has nailed giant arrows tip to tail into a path: one blue arrow, then two identical red ones. A green turtle plods along the path, already on the first red arrow, heading for a gold flag planted where the last arrow ends. The kneeling carpenter, hammer in hand, has used the blue arrow once and the red one twice: that recipe is the whole trip.
image.zh: 工坊地板上，木匠把几支巨大的箭头首尾相接钉成一条路：先是一支蓝箭，再接两支一模一样的红箭。一只绿乌龟沿路慢慢爬，已经爬上第一支红箭，目标是最后一支箭尖处的金旗。跪着的木匠握着锤子：蓝箭用一次，红箭用两次，这份配方就是全程。

means.zh: 系数为 1 的向量 u

summary.en: The span of some vectors is everything their combinations reach; they are independent when none of them is a combination of the others.
summary.zh: 一组向量的张成是它们的线性组合能到达的一切；若没有哪个向量是其余向量的组合，它们就线性无关。

explain.en: The span of v₁, …, vₖ is the set of all their linear combinations. It is always a subspace: it contains 0 and is closed under addition and scaling. In ℝ³ one nonzero vector spans a line through the origin and two non-parallel vectors span a plane. The vectors are linearly independent if a₁v₁ + … + aₖvₖ = 0 forces every aᵢ = 0. Equivalently, none of them is a combination of the others, so removing any one shrinks the span. If they are dependent, some vector is redundant and can be dropped without changing the span. Independence also makes representations unique: each vector in the span is a combination in exactly one way. To test vectors in ℝⁿ, make them the columns of a matrix and row-reduce: they are independent iff every column has a pivot.
explain.zh: v₁,…,vₖ 的张成（span）是它们全部线性组合的集合，它总是子空间：含零向量，对加法和数乘封闭。在 ℝ³ 中，一个非零向量张成过原点的直线，两个不平行的向量张成一个平面。若 a₁v₁+…+aₖvₖ=0 只有全零解，就称这组向量线性无关（linearly independent）；等价地说，没有哪个向量是其余向量的组合，去掉任何一个，张成都会变小。线性相关时必有多余的向量，删掉它张成不变。线性无关还保证表示唯一。检验 ℝⁿ 中的向量：把它们排成矩阵的列做行化简，每列都有主元当且仅当线性无关。

example.en: In ℝ³, (1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0) span the xy-plane. Adding (1, 1, 0) adds nothing: it equals (1, 0, 0) + (0, 1, 0), so the three are dependent, with the non-trivial relation v₁ + v₂ − v₃ = 0. Adding (0, 0, 1) instead lifts the span to all of ℝ³, and those three vectors are independent.
example.zh: 在 ℝ³ 中，(1,0,0) 和 (0,1,0) 张成 xy 平面。再加 (1,1,0) 毫无新意：它等于 (1,0,0)+(0,1,0)，三者线性相关，有非平凡关系 v₁+v₂−v₃=0。若改加 (0,0,1)，张成就扩大为整个 ℝ³，这三个向量线性无关。

image.en: A big flat rug lies on the workshop floor, and two chunky arrows, one blue and one red, point across it in different directions: combined, they can reach every spot on the rug. A worker proudly adds a purple arrow, but it lies flat on the same rug, pointing between the other two, so he shrugs: it reaches nothing new. At the far corner of the rug a yellow balloon tugs straight up, the one direction the rug cannot hold.
image.zh: 工坊地上铺着一张大地毯，一支蓝箭和一支红箭朝不同方向躺在上面：两者组合，能到达地毯上每一处。工人得意地添上一支紫箭，可它照样平躺在这张地毯上，指向前两支之间，于是他耸耸肩：什么新地方也到不了。地毯远角上一只黄气球笔直往上拽，那是地毯容纳不了的方向。

means.zh: w=u+v 在张成之内：{u,v,w} 线性相关

means.zh: 多余的向量删去后张成不变

means.zh: 平面外的向量：与前两者无关，张成随之扩大

summary.en: A basis is an independent set that spans the space; every basis has the same size, the dimension, and gives each vector unique coordinates.
summary.zh: 基是张成整个空间的线性无关组；所有基的大小相同，即维数；基给每个向量唯一的坐标。

explain.en: A basis of a vector space V is a list of vectors that is linearly independent and spans V. Spanning means every vector is a combination of the basis; independence means it is a combination in only one way, so each v has unique coordinates (a₁, …, aₙ) relative to the basis. The key fact, the Steinitz exchange lemma, is that in a space spanned by n vectors any independent list has at most n vectors. Hence all bases have the same size, called the dimension. ℝⁿ has dimension n, polynomials of degree ≤ 2 have dimension 3 (basis 1, x, x²) and m×n matrices have dimension mn. In an n-dimensional space, n independent vectors automatically span and n spanning vectors are automatically independent. Some spaces, such as all polynomials, are infinite-dimensional.
explain.zh: 向量空间 V 的基（basis）是一组既线性无关又张成 V 的向量。张成保证每个向量都能由基组合出来，无关保证组合方式唯一，所以每个向量在这组基下有唯一的坐标 (a₁,…,aₙ)。关键事实是施泰尼茨替换引理：若 V 能由 n 个向量张成，则其中任何线性无关组至多含 n 个向量。由此所有基的大小相同，称为维数（dimension）。ℝⁿ 是 n 维的，次数 ≤2 的多项式构成 3 维空间（基为 1, x, x²），m×n 矩阵构成 mn 维空间。在 n 维空间里，n 个无关向量必定张成，n 个张成向量必定无关。全体多项式构成的空间是无穷维的。

example.en: In ℝ², take the basis B = {(1, 1), (1, −1)}. Then (5, 1) = 3·(1, 1) + 2·(1, −1), so its coordinates in B are (3, 2), while in the standard basis they are (5, 1): one vector, two coordinate labels. Any third vector would make either set dependent, because dim ℝ² = 2.
example.zh: 在 ℝ² 中取基 B={(1,1),(1,−1)}，则 (5,1)=3·(1,1)+2·(1,−1)，它在 B 下的坐标是 (3,2)，在标准基下是 (5,1)：同一个向量，两套坐标。无论哪组基，再加第三个向量都会线性相关，因为 dim ℝ²=2。

image.en: Two surveyors in the workshop argue about one gold flag. The one on the left has laid two blue arrows at her feet, one pointing right and one pointing back, and shouts “(5, 1)!”. The one on the right has set two orange arrows along the diagonals and shouts “(3, 2)!”. Both are right: the same flag in two coordinate systems, and each kit has exactly two arrows.
image.zh: 工坊里两位测量员为同一面金旗争个不停。左边那位脚下摆着两支蓝箭，一支朝右、一支朝后，她喊“(5,1)！”；右边那位把两支橙箭沿两条对角线斜放，喊“(3,2)！”。两人都对：同一面旗，两套坐标系，而每套工具都恰好是两支箭。

summary.en: Machines that preserve linear combinations: matrices, elimination, rank and nullity, and the determinant as a volume factor.
summary.zh: 保持线性组合的机器：矩阵、消元、秩与零化度，以及作为体积缩放因子的行列式。

summary.en: A linear map preserves linear combinations, so it is fixed by where it sends a basis; those images are the columns of its matrix.
summary.zh: 线性映射保持线性组合，因此完全由基向量的像决定；这些像就是矩阵的各列。

explain.en: A map T: V → W is linear if T(au + bv) = aT(u) + bT(v) for all vectors u, v and scalars a, b. Every x in ℝⁿ is x₁e₁ + … + xₙeₙ, so linearity gives T(x) = x₁T(e₁) + … + xₙT(eₙ): the map is completely determined by the images of the basis vectors. Put those images side by side as columns and you get the matrix A with T(x) = Ax. Rotations, reflections, projections, shears and differentiation of polynomials are linear; a translation x ↦ x + b with b ≠ 0 is not, because it moves 0. Doing T (matrix A) and then S (matrix B) is the map S∘T, whose matrix is the product BA. That is why matrix multiplication is defined row by column, and why it is associative but not commutative.
explain.zh: 若对所有向量 u、v 和标量 a、b 都有 T(au+bv)=aT(u)+bT(v)，映射 T 就是线性映射（linear map）。ℝⁿ 中每个 x 都是 x₁e₁+…+xₙeₙ，由线性得 T(x)=x₁T(e₁)+…+xₙT(eₙ)：映射完全由基向量的像决定。把这些像作为列并排，就得到矩阵 A，且 T(x)=Ax。旋转、反射、投影、剪切和多项式求导都是线性的；平移 x↦x+b（b≠0）不是，因为它把 0 移走了。先做 T（矩阵 A）再做 S（矩阵 B）得到 S∘T，其矩阵是乘积 BA。这正是矩阵乘法“行乘列”的由来，也解释了它满足结合律却不满足交换律。

example.en: A rotation by 90° anticlockwise sends e₁ = (1, 0) to (0, 1) and e₂ = (0, 1) to (−1, 0). Those are the columns, so A = [0 −1; 1 0]. Check: A(3, 2) = (−2, 3). Rotating twice gives A² = [−1 0; 0 −1] = −I, the rotation by 180°: composing maps is multiplying matrices.
example.zh: 逆时针旋转 90° 把 e₁=(1,0) 送到 (0,1)，把 e₂=(0,1) 送到 (−1,0)。它们就是矩阵的两列，所以 A=[0 −1; 1 0]。验证：A(3,2)=(−2,3)。转两次得 A²=[−1 0; 0 −1]=−I，即旋转 180°：映射的复合就是矩阵的乘法。

image.en: A grey conveyor runs through the factory. A worker in a hard hat feeds in just two test arrows: a blue one pointing right and a red one pointing back. A robot arm gives each a quarter turn, so blue comes out pointing back and red pointing left. At the exit a board records the results as the two columns of the machine's matrix: 0 −1 over 1 0.
image.zh: 灰色传送带穿过工厂。戴安全帽的工人只放进两支测试箭：一支朝右的蓝箭，一支朝后的红箭。机械臂把它们各转四分之一圈，蓝箭出来时朝后，红箭出来时朝左。出口处的牌子把结果记成机器矩阵的两列：上行 0 −1，下行 1 0。

the basis vectors e₁ and e₂
means.zh: 基向量 e₁ 与 e₂

means.en: their images T(e₁) and T(e₂)
the matrix A whose columns are T(e₁), T(e₂)
means.zh: 以 T(e₁)、T(e₂) 为列的矩阵 A

summary.en: Row operations reduce a linear system to echelon form without changing its solutions; the number of pivots is the rank.
summary.zh: 初等行变换把线性方程组化为阶梯形而不改变解；主元的个数就是秩。

explain.en: To solve Ax = b, row-reduce the augmented matrix [A | b] with three elementary row operations: swap two rows, multiply a row by a nonzero scalar, add a multiple of one row to another. Each is reversible, so the solution set never changes. Forward elimination produces echelon form: each row's first nonzero entry, its pivot, lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below. Back substitution then reads off the solution. A row 0 = c with c ≠ 0 means there is no solution; otherwise each non-pivot column gives a free variable, so there is exactly one solution or infinitely many. The rank of A is the number of pivots; it equals the dimension of both the column space and the row space. Elimination on an n×n matrix costs O(n³) operations.
explain.zh: 求解 Ax=b 时，对增广矩阵 [A|b] 做三种初等行变换：交换两行、某行乘以非零常数、把某行的倍数加到另一行。每种变换都可逆，所以解集不变。前向消元得到行阶梯形：每行第一个非零元（主元，pivot）都在上一行主元的右边，主元下方全是零，再回代求解。若出现 0=c（c≠0）的行则无解；否则每个非主元列对应一个自由变量，解要么唯一，要么无穷多。A 的秩（rank）是主元个数，等于列空间和行空间的维数。n×n 矩阵消元需要 O(n³) 次运算。

example.en: Solve x + y + z = 6, 2x + y − z = 1, x − y + 2z = 5. R₂ − 2R₁ gives −y − 3z = −11 and R₃ − R₁ gives −2y + z = −1; then R₃ − 2R₂ gives 7z = 21. Back substitution: z = 3, y = 2, x = 1. Three pivots, so the rank is 3 and the solution is unique.
example.zh: 解方程组 x+y+z=6，2x+y−z=1，x−y+2z=5。R₂−2R₁ 得 −y−3z=−11，R₃−R₁ 得 −2y+z=−1；再用 R₃−2R₂ 得 7z=21。回代：z=3，y=2，x=1。有三个主元，秩为 3，解唯一。

image.en: Crates stand on the factory floor in three rows like a 3×3 matrix, the back row being the top row. A worker in a hard hat has hammered away every crate below the diagonal and left wooden zero blocks in their place, so what remains steps down to the right like a staircase. The first crate on each step is painted gold: three pivots, so the rank is 3.
image.zh: 工厂地上的木箱摆成三排，像一个 3×3 矩阵，最靠后的一排是第一行。戴安全帽的工人抡锤砸掉了对角线以下的所有木箱，换上写着 0 的木块，剩下的木箱向右下方一级级排成阶梯。每级台阶上的第一只箱子漆成金色：三个主元，所以秩为 3。

means.en: the coefficient matrix, back row = first row
means.zh: 系数矩阵，后排是第一行

thing.zh: 对角线下方的 0 木块

means.en: entries eliminated by row operations
row echelon form
pivots; their number is the rank

means.zh: 把一行的倍数减到另一行上

summary.en: For a linear map T on an n-dimensional space, dim ker T + dim im T = n: every input dimension is either crushed to zero or carried through.
summary.zh: 对 n 维空间上的线性映射 T，dim ker T+dim im T=n：每个输入维度要么被压成零，要么被保留下来。

explain.en: Let T: V → W be linear with V finite-dimensional. The kernel ker T = {v : T(v) = 0} is a subspace of V; its dimension is the nullity. The image im T is a subspace of W; its dimension is the rank. The theorem says rank + nullity = dim V. Proof idea: extend a basis of the kernel to a basis of V; the images of the added vectors form a basis of the image. For an m×n matrix A, rank A + dim N(A) = n, the number of columns, and the nullity is the number of free variables after elimination. Consequences: the solutions of Ax = b, if any exist, are one particular solution plus the null space; a linear map ℝⁿ → ℝᵐ with n > m has a nonzero kernel; and a map between spaces of equal finite dimension is injective iff it is surjective.
explain.zh: 设 T: V→W 线性，V 有限维。核 ker T={v : T(v)=0} 是 V 的子空间，其维数叫零化度（nullity）；像 im T 是 W 的子空间，其维数叫秩（rank）。定理：秩+零化度=dim V。证明思路：把核的一组基扩充为 V 的基，新添向量的像恰好构成像空间的基。对 m×n 矩阵 A，rank A+dim N(A)=n（列数），零化度就是消元后自由变量的个数。推论：Ax=b 若有解，全部解是一个特解加上零空间；n>m 时 ℝⁿ→ℝᵐ 的线性映射必有非零的核；有限维且维数相同的空间之间，线性映射是单射当且仅当是满射。

example.en: Projecting ℝ³ onto the floor, P(x, y, z) = (x, y, 0), has kernel the z-axis (nullity 1) and image the xy-plane (rank 2): 1 + 2 = 3. For A = [1 2 3; 2 4 6], the second row is twice the first, so the rank is 1, and the null space is the plane x + 2y + 3z = 0, of dimension 2: 1 + 2 = 3 columns.
example.zh: 把 ℝ³ 投影到地面 P(x,y,z)=(x,y,0)：核是 z 轴（零化度 1），像是 xy 平面（秩 2），1+2=3。对 A=[1 2 3; 2 4 6]，第二行是第一行的 2 倍，秩为 1；零空间是平面 x+2y+3z=0，维数为 2：1+2=3，恰为列数。

image.en: Three blue parcels wait in a stack at the factory entrance. In the middle of the line a heavy anvil keeps slamming down on a red parcel, flattening it to nothing. Only two parcels, now green, come out stacked at the far end. The foreman checks the books and calls out “2 + 1 = 3”: everything that came in is accounted for.
image.zh: 工厂入口摞着三个蓝色包裹。生产线中间，一块沉重的铁砧不停砸向一个红包裹，把它压得什么都不剩。只有两个包裹变成绿色，摞在出口处。工头核对账目，高声报出“2+1=3”：进来的每一份都有着落。

means.zh: 核：被映成 0 的方向（零化度 1）

summary.en: det A is the factor by which A scales signed volume; it multiplies under composition and is zero exactly when A squashes space flat.
summary.zh: det A 是 A 对有向体积的缩放倍数；复合时相乘，并且恰在 A 把空间压扁时为零。

explain.en: For a 2×2 matrix, det [a b; c d] = ad − bc. Geometrically, A maps the unit square to the parallelogram spanned by its columns (in n dimensions, the unit cube to a parallelepiped), whose signed area or volume is det A; every region's volume is multiplied by |det A|. A negative sign means orientation is flipped, as in a mirror. Scale factors compose, so det(AB) = det A · det B. A is invertible iff det A ≠ 0: a zero determinant means some direction is crushed, the columns are dependent and Ax = 0 has nonzero solutions. Row operations change det predictably: a swap flips the sign, scaling a row by c scales det by c, and adding a multiple of one row to another changes nothing, so elimination gives det as ± the product of the pivots. Also det Aᵀ = det A.
explain.zh: 2×2 矩阵的行列式 det[a b; c d]=ad−bc。几何上，A 把单位正方形变成由其列张成的平行四边形（n 维时把单位立方体变成平行六面体），其有向面积（体积）就是 det A；任何区域的体积都乘以 |det A|。负号表示定向翻转，就像照镜子。缩放倍数可以连乘，所以 det(AB)=det A·det B。A 可逆当且仅当 det A≠0：行列式为零说明某个方向被压扁，列向量线性相关，Ax=0 有非零解。行变换对行列式的影响很规整：交换两行变号，某行乘 c 则行列式乘 c，把一行的倍数加到另一行不变。因此消元后 det 等于 ± 主元之积。另有 det Aᵀ=det A。

example.en: A = [3 1; 1 2] has det A = 3·2 − 1·1 = 5: it turns the unit square into the parallelogram spanned by its columns (3, 1) and (1, 2), of area 5. B = [2 4; 1 2] has det B = 4 − 4 = 0: its columns are parallel, the plane collapses onto a line, and B has no inverse. For any 2×2 matrix C, det(AC) = 5·det C.
example.zh: A=[3 1; 1 2] 的行列式为 3·2−1·1=5：它把单位正方形变成由列 (3,1)、(1,2) 张成的平行四边形，面积为 5。B=[2 4; 1 2] 的行列式为 4−4=0：两列平行，平面被压成一条直线，B 不可逆。对任意 2×2 矩阵 C，det(AC)=5·det C。

image.en: A small blue unit cube sits at a fork on the factory floor. Along one orange arrow, machine A pumps it up into a gold cube five times its volume, and a bubble says “×5”. Along the grey arrow, machine B squashes it into a flat grey pancake marked “×0”. A worker beside the pancake shrugs: nothing can turn a pancake back into a cube.
image.zh: 工厂地上，一个蓝色小单位立方体停在岔路口。顺着橙色箭头，机器 A 把它吹成体积是原来五倍的金立方体，气泡里写着“×5”；顺着灰色箭头，机器 B 把它压成一张扁平的灰煎饼，标着“×0”。煎饼旁的工人耸耸肩：煎饼再也变不回立方体了。

means.en: the unit cube, volume 1
means.zh: 体积为 1 的单位立方体

det B = 0: space is squashed flat
det = 0 means no inverse

summary.en: The directions a map only stretches, perpendicular projection, and the spectral theorem and SVD that combine them.
summary.zh: 映射只伸缩不转向的方向、垂直投影，以及把两者结合起来的谱定理与奇异值分解。

summary.en: An eigenvector of A is a nonzero v with Av = λv: A only stretches it, by the eigenvalue λ, without turning it off its line.
summary.zh: 特征向量是满足 Av=λv 的非零向量 v：A 只把它伸缩 λ 倍，不让它离开所在的直线。

explain.en: A nonzero vector v is an eigenvector of the square matrix A with eigenvalue λ if Av = λv. The map turns most vectors off their line through the origin, but eigenvectors stay on theirs, scaled by λ (and reversed if λ < 0). Rewriting as (A − λI)v = 0 shows that λ is an eigenvalue exactly when A − λI is singular, that is, when det(A − λI) = 0, the characteristic equation. For an n×n matrix it is a polynomial of degree n, so there are at most n eigenvalues. For each λ, the eigenvectors together with 0 form the eigenspace ker(A − λI). Real matrices can have complex eigenvalues: a 90° rotation of the plane keeps no real direction, and its eigenvalues are ±i. Counted with multiplicity, the eigenvalues sum to the trace and multiply to the determinant.
explain.zh: 若非零向量 v 满足 Av=λv，就称 v 是方阵 A 的特征向量（eigenvector），λ 是对应的特征值（eigenvalue）。A 会把大多数向量转离原来过原点的直线，特征向量却留在自己的直线上，只被伸缩 λ 倍（λ<0 时反向）。改写成 (A−λI)v=0 可知：λ 是特征值当且仅当 A−λI 奇异，即 det(A−λI)=0，这就是特征方程。n×n 矩阵的特征多项式是 n 次的，所以至多有 n 个特征值。每个 λ 的特征向量连同零向量构成特征空间 ker(A−λI)。实矩阵也可能只有复特征值：平面上旋转 90° 不保留任何实方向，特征值是 ±i。按重数计，特征值之和等于迹，之积等于行列式。

example.en: A = [2 1; 1 2]: det(A − λI) = (2 − λ)² − 1 = 0 gives λ = 3 and λ = 1. Check: A(1, 1) = (3, 3) = 3·(1, 1) and A(1, −1) = (1, −1). Every other direction is turned: A(1, 0) = (2, 1). Also trace 4 = 3 + 1 and det 3 = 3·1.

image.en: A spotlight on the theatre stage throws its beam along one line across the floor. A magician in a wizard's hat casts the same spell on every arrow: two grey arrows spin round to new headings, but the gold arrow lying in the beam does not turn at all. The magician simply pulls it out along the beam to three times the length of its small gold twin, and calls out “λ = 3”.
image.zh: 剧院舞台上，一盏聚光灯沿地面上的一条直线投下光柱。戴巫师帽的魔术师对每支箭念同一句咒语：两支灰箭被转得团团转，换了方向；躺在光柱里的金箭却纹丝不转。魔术师只是顺着光柱把它拉长到旁边那支小金箭的三倍，高喊“λ=3”。

means.en: the matrix A acting on all vectors
means.zh: 矩阵 A 作用于所有向量

means.en: ordinary vectors: A turns them off their line
means.zh: 普通向量：被 A 转离原来的直线

thing.en: the gold arrow in the beam

means.en: an eigenvector: Av stays on the line of v
means.zh: 特征向量：Av 仍在 v 的直线上

means.en: the eigenvalue λ = 3

summary.en: With n independent eigenvectors, A = PDP⁻¹: in the eigenvector basis A just scales each axis, so Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹ is cheap to compute.
summary.zh: 若有 n 个线性无关的特征向量，则 A=PDP⁻¹：在特征向量基下 A 只是逐轴伸缩，于是 Aᵏ=PDᵏP⁻¹ 很好算。

explain.en: An n×n matrix A is diagonalizable if it has n linearly independent eigenvectors v₁, …, vₙ. Make them the columns of P and put the eigenvalues on the diagonal of D; then AP = PD, so A = PDP⁻¹. Read right to left: P⁻¹ converts to eigen-coordinates, D scales each coordinate by its own eigenvalue with no mixing, and P converts back. Powers become easy: Aᵏ = PDᵏP⁻¹, where Dᵏ just raises each diagonal entry to the k-th power, and the eigenvalue of largest absolute value typically dominates the long-run behaviour of xₖ₊₁ = Axₖ. n distinct eigenvalues guarantee diagonalizability, but repeated ones may not: the shear [1 1; 0 1] has the single eigenvalue 1 with only one independent eigenvector, so it cannot be diagonalized.
explain.zh: 若 n×n 矩阵 A 有 n 个线性无关的特征向量 v₁,…,vₙ，就称 A 可对角化（diagonalizable）。把它们排成 P 的列，特征值放在对角阵 D 上，则 AP=PD，即 A=PDP⁻¹。从右往左读：P⁻¹ 换到特征向量坐标，D 把每个坐标各乘自己的特征值、互不干扰，P 再换回来。幂运算因此变简单：Aᵏ=PDᵏP⁻¹，Dᵏ 只需把对角元各自取 k 次方；迭代 xₖ₊₁=Axₖ 的长期行为通常由绝对值最大的特征值主导。n 个特征值互不相同时一定可对角化，有重根时则未必：剪切矩阵 [1 1; 0 1] 只有特征值 1，且只有一个无关的特征向量，不能对角化。

example.en: Fibonacci: (Fₖ₊₁, Fₖ) = A(Fₖ, Fₖ₋₁) with A = [1 1; 1 0]. Its eigenvalues solve λ² − λ − 1 = 0: φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618 and ψ = (1 − √5)/2 ≈ −0.618. Diagonalizing and taking powers gives Binet's formula Fₙ = (φⁿ − ψⁿ)/√5, so F₁₀ = (122.992 − 0.008)/2.236 = 55, and Fₙ grows like φⁿ because |ψ| < 1.

image.en: In front of a red theatre curtain two rabbits perform separate solo acts. A giant golden rabbit has grown by a factor of φ ≈ 1.618, and a tiny grey one has shrunk to 0.618 of its size and turned to face backwards, since ψ is negative. They came in through the open door on the left (P⁻¹) and will leave through the door on the right (P), where a magician in a top hat waits. A sign between them shows the whole act: the diagonal matrix φ 0; 0 ψ.
image.zh: 红色大幕前，两只兔子各演各的独角戏：金兔被放大到原来的 φ≈1.618 倍，成了巨兔；灰兔缩小到原来的 0.618 倍，还掉头背对观众，因为 ψ 是负数。它们从左边敞开的门（P⁻¹）进场，将从右边的门（P）退场，戴高礼帽的魔术师在那里等着。两兔之间的牌子写明整场演出：对角矩阵 φ 0; 0 ψ。

means.en: P⁻¹: switch to eigenvector coordinates
D: each coordinate scales by its own eigenvalue, no mixing
means.zh: D：每个坐标只乘自己的特征值，互不混合

means.en: φ ≈ 1.618 dominates the powers Aᵏ
means.zh: φ≈1.618 主导 Aᵏ 的增长

means.en: ψ ≈ −0.618: shrinks and flips sign
P: switch back to standard coordinates

summary.en: The projection of b onto a subspace is its closest point there; the error is perpendicular to the subspace, the idea behind least squares.
summary.zh: b 在子空间上的正交投影是子空间中离它最近的点；误差与子空间垂直，这正是最小二乘的原理。

explain.en: The dot product u·v = Σuᵢvᵢ = |u||v|cos θ measures alignment; u and v are orthogonal when u·v = 0. The orthogonal complement W⊥ of a subspace W consists of the vectors orthogonal to all of W, and every b splits uniquely as b = p + e with p in W and e in W⊥. This p is the projection of b onto W and the closest point of W to b. Onto the line through a: p = (a·b / a·a) a. Onto the column space of a matrix A with independent columns: p = Ax̂, where AᵀAx̂ = Aᵀb (the normal equations). When Ax = b has no solution, x̂ is the least-squares solution, minimising |Ax − b|. Gram–Schmidt turns any basis into an orthonormal one by subtracting from each vector its projections onto the earlier ones and normalising.
explain.zh: 点积 u·v=Σuᵢvᵢ=|u||v|cos θ 衡量方向一致的程度，u·v=0 时两向量正交（orthogonal）。子空间 W 的正交补 W⊥ 由与 W 中所有向量都正交的向量组成，每个 b 都能唯一地分解为 b=p+e，其中 p∈W，e∈W⊥。这个 p 就是 b 在 W 上的投影，也是 W 中离 b 最近的点。投影到过 a 的直线：p=(a·b/a·a)a。投影到列线性无关的矩阵 A 的列空间：p=Ax̂，其中 AᵀAx̂=Aᵀb（正规方程）。Ax=b 无解时，x̂ 就是使 |Ax−b| 最小的最小二乘解。格拉姆–施密特正交化让每个向量减去它在前面各向量上的投影再单位化，把任意一组基变成标准正交基。

example.en: Fit a line y = c + mt to the points (0, 6), (1, 0), (2, 0). No line passes through all three, so solve the normal equations: AᵀA = [3 3; 3 5] and Aᵀb = (6, 0) give c = 5, m = −3. The best line is y = 5 − 3t. Its errors (1, −2, 1) are orthogonal to both columns, (1, 1, 1) and (0, 1, 2).
example.zh: 用直线 y=c+mt 拟合三点 (0,6)、(1,0)、(2,0)。没有直线能同时穿过三点，于是解正规方程：AᵀA=[3 3; 3 5]，Aᵀb=(6,0)，得 c=5，m=−3，最佳直线是 y=5−3t。误差向量 (1,−2,1) 与两列 (1,1,1)、(0,1,2) 都正交。

image.en: A lamp hangs straight above the theatre stage. Under it an acrobat balances on top of a ladder, and the lamp throws her shadow as a black spot on the floor directly beneath her. From the corner of the stage, where a child stands pointing, a gold arrow runs across the floor to the shadow: the closest the floor can get to her. The ladder, at a right angle to the floor, is the leftover error.
image.zh: 舞台正上方吊着一盏灯。灯下，一位杂技演员在梯子顶端保持平衡，灯光把她的影子投成正下方地板上的一个黑点。台角站着一个指着她的孩子，从那里一支金箭沿地板直指影子：地板上离她最近的地方就是这里。与地板成直角的梯子，就是剩下的误差。

means.en: the subspace W

thing.en: the acrobat up in the air

means.en: the vector b, outside W

thing.en: her shadow and the gold arrow

means.en: the projection p: the closest point of W to b
means.zh: 投影 p：W 中离 b 最近的点

means.en: the error e = b − p, perpendicular to W
means.zh: 误差 e=b−p，与 W 垂直

summary.en: A real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and an orthonormal eigenbasis; every matrix factors as A = UΣVᵀ: rotate, stretch, rotate.
summary.zh: 实对称矩阵的特征值都是实数，并有标准正交的特征向量基；任何矩阵都可分解为 A=UΣVᵀ：旋转、拉伸、再旋转。

explain.en: Spectral theorem: if A is real and symmetric (Aᵀ = A), its eigenvalues are real and it has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors, so A = QΛQᵀ with Q orthogonal (Q⁻¹ = Qᵀ). Geometrically, A stretches space along perpendicular axes. The singular value decomposition extends this to every real m×n matrix: A = UΣVᵀ with U and V orthogonal and Σ diagonal, carrying the singular values σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ … ≥ 0, the square roots of the eigenvalues of AᵀA. So every linear map is a rotation (possibly with a reflection), an axis-aligned stretch, and another rotation. Keeping the k largest terms, Aₖ = σ₁u₁v₁ᵀ + … + σₖuₖvₖᵀ, gives the best rank-k approximation of A in both the spectral and Frobenius norms (Eckart–Young), the basis of PCA and of image compression.
explain.zh: 谱定理：若 A 是实对称矩阵（Aᵀ=A），则其特征值都是实数，并有一组标准正交的特征向量基，于是 A=QΛQᵀ，Q 为正交矩阵（Q⁻¹=Qᵀ）。几何上，A 沿几条互相垂直的轴拉伸空间。奇异值分解（SVD）把这一点推广到任意实 m×n 矩阵：A=UΣVᵀ，U、V 正交，Σ 是对角阵，对角线上是奇异值 σ₁≥σ₂≥…≥0，即 AᵀA 特征值的平方根。所以任何线性映射都是“旋转（可能带反射）—沿轴拉伸—再旋转”。只保留最大的 k 项 Aₖ=σ₁u₁v₁ᵀ+…+σₖuₖvₖᵀ，就得到谱范数和弗罗贝尼乌斯范数意义下最佳的秩 k 逼近（Eckart–Young 定理），这是主成分分析和图像压缩的基础。

example.en: The shear A = [1 1; 0 1] is not symmetric, but AᵀA = [1 1; 1 2] has eigenvalues (3 ± √5)/2, so the singular values of A are about 1.618 and 0.618: A turns the unit circle into an ellipse with those semi-axes. Compression: a 1000×1000 image kept as its top 50 singular triples needs 50 × 2001 = 100,050 numbers instead of 1,000,000.
example.zh: 剪切矩阵 A=[1 1; 0 1] 不对称，但 AᵀA=[1 1; 1 2] 的特征值为 (3±√5)/2，所以 A 的奇异值约为 1.618 和 0.618：A 把单位圆变成以它们为半轴的椭圆。压缩：1000×1000 的图像只保留前 50 组奇异三元组，需要 50×2001=100050 个数，而不是 1000000 个。

image.en: Five things stand in a row across the theatre stage. On the left a round blue ball waits. A ballerina pirouettes to turn it, a strongman pulls hard to stretch it along two perpendicular axes, and a second ballerina spins to turn it again. On the far right the ball has become a giant blue egg: every matrix is turn, stretch, turn.
image.zh: 舞台上一字排开五样东西。最左边是一只圆圆的蓝球。一位芭蕾舞者旋转着把它转个方向，一位大力士使劲把它沿两条互相垂直的轴拉伸，第二位芭蕾舞者再把它转一次。到了最右边，球变成了一只巨大的蓝蛋：任何矩阵都是“转、拉、转”。

means.en: the unit circle (unit sphere)
Vᵀ: a rotation (orthogonal matrix)
Σ: stretch along perpendicular axes by σ₁ ≥ σ₂
means.zh: Σ：沿垂直轴按 σ₁≥σ₂ 拉伸

means.en: U: another rotation; for symmetric A it undoes the first, up to sign flips
means.zh: U：再一次旋转；A 对称时它抵消第一次（至多差符号）

means.en: the image: an ellipse with semi-axes σᵢ
means.zh: 像：以 σᵢ 为半轴的椭圆

summary.en: Reasoning under uncertainty and learning from data: axioms and conditioning, expectation and spread, and the limit theorems behind statistical inference.
summary.zh: 在不确定中推理、从数据中学习：公理与条件概率，期望与离散程度，以及支撑统计推断的极限定理。

summary.en: Outcomes, events and their probabilities; conditioning on evidence and Bayes' rule; random variables and their distributions.
summary.zh: 结果、事件与概率；依据证据求条件概率与贝叶斯公式；随机变量及其分布。

summary.en: A probability gives each event a number in [0, 1], with P(Ω) = 1 and additivity over disjoint events; every other rule follows from these.
summary.zh: 概率给每个事件一个 [0,1] 中的数，满足 P(Ω)=1 及互斥事件可加；其余规则都由此推出。

explain.en: A random experiment has a sample space Ω, the set of all possible outcomes. An event is a subset of Ω (when Ω is infinite, only the sets in a suitable family count as events). Kolmogorov's axioms: P(A) ≥ 0 for every event, P(Ω) = 1, and for pairwise disjoint events P(A₁ ∪ A₂ ∪ …) = P(A₁) + P(A₂) + … (countable additivity). Everything else is derived: P(∅) = 0, P(Aᶜ) = 1 − P(A), P(A) ≤ 1, A ⊆ B implies P(A) ≤ P(B), and P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B), which is inclusion–exclusion. When Ω is finite and all outcomes are equally likely, P(A) = |A| / |Ω|, so probability becomes counting. The complement rule is often the shortest route: find the chance that something never happens and subtract it from 1.
explain.zh: 随机试验的样本空间 Ω 是全部可能结果的集合，事件是 Ω 的子集（Ω 无限时取自一族合适的子集）。柯尔莫哥洛夫公理：每个事件 P(A)≥0；P(Ω)=1；对两两互斥的事件，P(A₁∪A₂∪…)=P(A₁)+P(A₂)+…（可数可加性）。其余性质都可推出：P(∅)=0，P(Aᶜ)=1−P(A)，P(A)≤1，A⊆B 则 P(A)≤P(B)，以及容斥公式 P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B)。若 Ω 有限且各结果等可能，则 P(A)=|A|/|Ω|，概率问题就成了计数问题。补集法常是捷径：先算“一次也不发生”的概率，再用 1 去减。

example.en: Roll two fair dice: Ω has 36 equally likely outcomes. P(sum = 7) = 6/36 = 1/6, from (1, 6), (2, 5), …, (6, 1). P(at least one six) is easiest by the complement: 1 − (5/6)² = 11/36. Check by counting: 36 − 25 = 11 outcomes contain a six.
example.zh: 掷两颗均匀骰子，Ω 有 36 个等可能结果。P(点数和=7)=6/36=1/6，来自 (1,6)、(2,5)、…、(6,1)。P(至少一个六) 用补集最快：1−(5/6)²=11/36。用计数验证：含六的结果有 36−25=11 个。

image.en: A cake as big as a table stands on the red casino carpet. The croupier in a top hat slices it with a sword into equal slices, one for each equally likely outcome, and two huge red dice sit on top like decorations. A gambler cheers and claims his share, but however the slices are handed out, together they never make more or less than one whole cake.
image.zh: 赌场红地毯上立着一个桌子那么大的蛋糕。戴高礼帽的庄家挥剑把它切成大小相等的块，每块对应一个等可能的结果；两颗巨大的红骰子像装饰一样摆在蛋糕顶上。一位赌客欢呼着要他的那一份。可无论怎么分，所有蛋糕块加起来永远不多不少正好一整个。

means.en: the sample space Ω, with P(Ω) = 1
equally likely outcomes: P(A) = |A|/|Ω|

summary.en: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) is the chance of A once we know B happened; A and B are independent when knowing B changes nothing.
summary.zh: P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B) 是已知 B 发生后 A 的概率；若知道 B 不改变 A 的概率，A 与 B 就相互独立。

explain.en: Learning that B occurred shrinks the sample space to B. The conditional probability of A given B, defined when P(B) > 0, is P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B): the share of B that also lies in A. Rearranged, it gives the multiplication rule P(A ∩ B) = P(B)·P(A | B), which chains: P(A ∩ B ∩ C) = P(A)·P(B | A)·P(C | A ∩ B). Events A and B are independent if P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B), which for P(B) > 0 means P(A | B) = P(A). Independence is not the same as being disjoint: two disjoint events with positive probabilities are strongly dependent, since if one happens the other cannot. And three events can be pairwise independent without being mutually independent.
explain.zh: 得知 B 发生后，样本空间缩小为 B。当 P(B)>0 时，已知 B 时 A 的条件概率定义为 P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B)，即 B 中同时属于 A 的比例。移项得乘法公式 P(A∩B)=P(B)·P(A|B)，还可以连乘：P(A∩B∩C)=P(A)·P(B|A)·P(C|A∩B)。若 P(A∩B)=P(A)·P(B)，就称 A、B 相互独立（independent）；P(B)>0 时这等价于 P(A|B)=P(A)。独立不等于互斥：两个概率为正的互斥事件高度相关，一个发生，另一个就不可能发生。三个事件两两独立，也未必相互独立。

example.en: Draw two cards without replacement: P(both aces) = P(first ace)·P(second ace | first ace) = (4/52)·(3/51) = 1/221. Roll one die, with A = even and B = at most 4: P(A ∩ B) = P({2, 4}) = 1/3 = (1/2)·(2/3) = P(A)P(B), so A and B are independent. But A and C = {1, 3} are disjoint, and P(A | C) = 0 ≠ 1/2.
example.zh: 不放回地抽两张牌：P(两张都是 A)=P(第一张是 A)·P(第二张是 A|第一张是 A)=(4/52)·(3/51)=1/221。掷一颗骰子，A=偶数，B=不超过 4：P(A∩B)=P({2,4})=1/3=(1/2)·(2/3)=P(A)P(B)，所以 A、B 独立。而 A 与 C={1,3} 互斥，P(A|C)=0≠1/2。

Nearby a gambler rolls a big red die, and the ace changes nothing for it: still one chance in six.

summary.en: Bayes' theorem turns P(B | A) into P(A | B) = P(B | A)P(A)/P(B), weighting the evidence by the prior; forgetting the prior is the base-rate fallacy.
summary.zh: 贝叶斯定理把 P(B|A) 翻转为 P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B)，用先验给证据加权；忘了先验就是基础比率谬误。

explain.en: From P(A ∩ B) = P(A | B)P(B) = P(B | A)P(A) comes Bayes' theorem: P(A | B) = P(B | A)·P(A) / P(B). The denominator comes from the law of total probability: if A₁, …, Aₙ partition Ω, then P(B) = Σ P(B | Aᵢ)P(Aᵢ). In words, the posterior is proportional to the likelihood times the prior. Bayes tells us how to update our belief in a hypothesis A after seeing evidence B, and it warns that P(B | A) and P(A | B) can be very different. The base-rate fallacy is to judge P(disease | positive test) by the test's accuracy alone and forget how rare the disease is. Spam filters, medical diagnosis and the whole of Bayesian statistics rest on this update.
explain.zh: 由 P(A∩B)=P(A|B)P(B)=P(B|A)P(A) 立即得到贝叶斯定理：P(A|B)=P(B|A)·P(A)/P(B)。分母用全概率公式计算：若 A₁,…,Aₙ 构成 Ω 的划分，则 P(B)=ΣP(B|Aᵢ)P(Aᵢ)。一句话：后验正比于似然乘先验。贝叶斯定理告诉我们，看到证据 B 之后该如何更新对假设 A 的信念，也提醒我们 P(B|A) 与 P(A|B) 可能相差悬殊。只看检测的准确率、忘了疾病本身有多罕见，就是基础比率谬误（base-rate fallacy）。垃圾邮件过滤、医学诊断和整个贝叶斯统计都建立在这种更新之上。

example.en: A disease affects 1% of people. The test catches 99% of cases and wrongly flags 1% of healthy people. Among 10,000 people, 100 are ill and 99 of them test positive; of the 9,900 healthy, 99 also test positive. So P(ill | +) = 99/198 = 50%: for a “99% accurate” test, a positive result is a coin flip. By the formula: 0.99·0.01 / (0.99·0.01 + 0.01·0.99) = 0.5.
example.zh: 某病患病率 1%。检测能查出 99% 的病人，但也会把 1% 的健康人误判为阳性。1 万人中有 100 名病人，其中 99 人阳性；9900 名健康人中也有 99 人阳性。所以 P(患病|阳性)=99/198=50%：一个“准确率 99%”的检测，阳性结果也不过是抛硬币。用公式：0.99·0.01/(0.99·0.01+0.01·0.99)=0.5。

image.en: At the back of the casino stands a big crowd of healthy gamblers. A red test lamp has lit up above two people in front: a man in red who really is ill, and a perfectly healthy man in grey, one of the rare false alarms from the huge healthy crowd, who shrugs in surprise. Between them a brass balance hangs perfectly level: given a positive test, being ill is only a fifty-fifty bet.

summary.en: A random variable assigns a number to each outcome; its distribution, given by a pmf or density and the cdf, says how likely each value is.
summary.zh: 随机变量给每个结果赋一个数；它的分布由概率质量函数或密度函数以及分布函数描述，说明各个取值有多大可能。

explain.en: A random variable is a function X: Ω → ℝ; the randomness lives in the outcome, not in the function. A discrete X has a probability mass function p(x) = P(X = x) with Σ p(x) = 1. A continuous X has a density f with P(a ≤ X ≤ b) = ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx; f(x) itself is not a probability and can exceed 1. Both have a cdf F(x) = P(X ≤ x), non-decreasing from 0 to 1. Standard families: Bernoulli(p), one trial; binomial(n, p), successes in n independent trials, P(X = k) = C(n, k)pᵏ(1 − p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ; geometric(p), trials until the first success; Poisson(λ), counts of rare events, P(X = k) = e^(−λ)λᵏ/k!; uniform on [a, b]; and exponential(λ), waiting times, memoryless like the geometric.
explain.zh: 随机变量是函数 X: Ω→ℝ；随机性来自试验结果，而不在函数本身。离散型 X 有概率质量函数 p(x)=P(X=x)，Σp(x)=1；连续型 X 有密度 f，P(a≤X≤b)=∫ₐᵇf(x)dx，f(x) 本身不是概率，可以大于 1。两者都有分布函数 F(x)=P(X≤x)，从 0 单调不减到 1。常见分布：伯努利 (p)，一次试验；二项 (n,p)，n 次独立试验的成功次数，P(X=k)=C(n,k)pᵏ(1−p)ⁿ⁻ᵏ；几何 (p)，首次成功所需次数；泊松 (λ)，稀有事件计数，P(X=k)=e^(−λ)λᵏ/k!；[a,b] 上的均匀分布；指数 (λ)，等待时间，与几何分布一样无记忆。

example.en: Toss 3 fair coins and let X = number of heads, so X(HHT) = 2 and X(TTT) = 0. X is binomial(3, 1/2): P(X = 0, 1, 2, 3) = 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8, and the cdf steps up to 1/8, 1/2, 7/8, 1. An exponential waiting time with rate 2 per hour has density 2e^(−2t), which equals 2 at t = 0: a density, not a probability.
example.zh: 掷 3 枚均匀硬币，X=正面个数，如 X(正正反)=2，X(反反反)=0。X 服从二项分布 (3,1/2)：P(X=0,1,2,3)=1/8、3/8、3/8、1/8，分布函数依次跳到 1/8、1/2、7/8、1。速率为每小时 2 次的指数等待时间密度为 2e^(−2t)，在 t=0 处等于 2：它是密度，不是概率。

image.en: A croupier robot flips three giant coins: two land gold side up for heads, one silver for tails. It pays out not in coins but in a single number, the count of heads, here 2. After every throw it adds a stack of gold to the pile above that number on a scale marked 0, 1, 2, 3, and the four piles have grown 1, 3, 3 and 1 stacks high. Those piles are the distribution of X.
image.zh: 机器人庄家抛出三枚巨大的硬币：两枚金面朝上算正面，一枚银面算反面。它不赔硬币，只报一个数：正面的个数，这次是 2。每抛一轮，它就往刻度 0、1、2、3 中对应数字上方的金堆添一摞金币；四堆金子已经长到 1、3、3、1 摞高。这几堆金子就是 X 的分布。

summary.en: Averages and spread: expectation and its linearity, variance with Chebyshev's bound, and the normal curve.
summary.zh: 平均与离散：期望及其线性性、方差与切比雪夫界，以及正态曲线。

summary.en: E[X] is the probability-weighted average of the values of X; E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] always holds, even for dependent variables.
summary.zh: E[X] 是 X 各取值按概率加权的平均；E[X+Y]=E[X]+E[Y] 总是成立，即使变量彼此相关。

explain.en: The expectation of a discrete random variable is E[X] = Σ x·P(X = x), its long-run average value (for a continuous one, ∫ x f(x) dx); it exists when Σ |x|·P(X = x) converges. Expectation is linear: E[aX + bY] = aE[X] + bE[Y] for any random variables with finite means, independent or not. This makes indicator variables powerful: write a count as X = I₁ + … + Iₙ, where Iᵢ is 1 if event Aᵢ happens and 0 otherwise; then E[X] = P(A₁) + … + P(Aₙ), with no need for the distribution of X. By contrast E[XY] = E[X]E[Y] needs independence (or at least zero covariance), and in general E[g(X)] ≠ g(E[X]). The expected value need not be a possible value: a fair die averages 3.5.
explain.zh: 离散随机变量的期望是 E[X]=Σx·P(X=x)，即长期平均值（连续型为 ∫x f(x)dx）；要求 Σ|x|·P(X=x) 收敛，否则期望不存在。期望是线性的：只要期望有限，E[aX+bY]=aE[X]+bE[Y]，无论是否独立。这让指示变量威力十足：把计数写成 X=I₁+…+Iₙ，事件 Aᵢ 发生时 Iᵢ=1，否则为 0，则 E[X]=P(A₁)+…+P(Aₙ)，根本不必求 X 的分布。相比之下，E[XY]=E[X]E[Y] 需要独立（至少协方差为零），而且一般 E[g(X)]≠g(E[X])。期望不一定是能取到的值：均匀骰子的期望是 3.5。

example.en: Hat check: n people leave their hats and get them back in random order. Let Iᵢ = 1 if person i gets their own hat, so P(Iᵢ = 1) = 1/n. The number of correct hats is X = I₁ + … + Iₙ, and E[X] = n·(1/n) = 1 for every n, although the Iᵢ are dependent. (The chance that nobody gets their own hat tends to 1/e ≈ 0.368.)
example.zh: 帽子问题：n 个人寄存帽子，取回时顺序完全随机。若第 i 人拿回自己的帽子则 Iᵢ=1，P(Iᵢ=1)=1/n。拿对帽子的人数 X=I₁+…+Iₙ，于是 E[X]=n·(1/n)=1，对任何 n 都成立，尽管各 Iᵢ 并不独立。（没有人拿对的概率趋于 1/e≈0.368。）

image.en: In the bank vault's cloakroom the hats have come back at random. The chef now wears the king's crown, the king a builder's hard hat, the builder a graduate's mortarboard and the graduate the chef's toque, and all four shrug. Only the wizard in the middle got his own pointed hat back, and he cheers. However many guests there are, on average exactly one gets their own hat.

thing.en: each guest: own hat or not

on average exactly one match: E[X] = 1

title.zh: 方差与切比雪夫不等式

summary.en: Variance E[(X − μ)²] measures spread; it adds for independent variables, and Chebyshev bounds how often X lands far from its mean μ.
summary.zh: 方差 E[(X−μ)²] 衡量离散程度；独立变量的方差可以相加，切比雪夫不等式限制 X 远离均值 μ 的概率。

explain.en: With μ = E[X], the variance is Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − μ², the mean squared distance from the mean; its square root σ, the standard deviation, has the same units as X. Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X): shifting changes nothing and scaling multiplies σ by |a|. In general Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2Cov(X, Y), so variances add when X and Y are independent, or merely uncorrelated; hence the mean of n i.i.d. variables has variance σ²/n. Chebyshev's inequality holds for every distribution with finite variance: P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k² for every k > 0. It is crude but universal, and it is all you need to prove the weak law of large numbers.
explain.zh: 记 μ=E[X]，方差 Var(X)=E[(X−μ)²]=E[X²]−μ²，即到均值距离平方的平均；其平方根 σ 称为标准差，与 X 同单位。Var(aX+b)=a²Var(X)：平移不改变方差，放缩使 σ 乘以 |a|。一般地 Var(X+Y)=Var(X)+Var(Y)+2Cov(X,Y)，所以 X、Y 独立（甚至只需不相关）时方差可加；n 个独立同分布变量的平均值方差为 σ²/n。切比雪夫不等式对任何方差有限的分布成立：对任意 k>0，P(|X−μ|≥kσ)≤1/k²。它粗糙却普适，足以证明弱大数定律。

example.en: A fair die has μ = 3.5 and E[X²] = 91/6, so Var = 91/6 − 12.25 = 35/12 ≈ 2.92 and σ ≈ 1.71. The sum of 100 dice has mean 350 and variance 100·35/12 ≈ 292, so σ ≈ 17.1. Chebyshev with k = 3: the sum lands more than about 51 away from 350 with probability at most 1/9. The true chance is far smaller, about 0.3%.

image.en: Gold coins lie scattered across the vault floor around a red flag marked μ, most close by, a few far out. A gold chain lies on the floor in a wide circle two standard deviations out, and only two coins have rolled beyond it. A guard kneels at the chain with a magnifying glass and counts them, quoting Chebyshev: “at most a quarter”.
image.zh: 金库地板上，金币散落在一面写着 μ 的红旗周围：多数离得近，少数滚得远。地上一条金链围成一个大圈，半径是两个标准差，只有两枚金币滚到了圈外。一名守卫跪在链边，举着放大镜清点，口中念着切比雪夫：“最多四分之一”。

means.en: the mean μ = E[X]
the spread: variance σ² and standard deviation σ
means.zh: 离散程度：方差 σ² 与标准差 σ

means.en: the boundary |X − μ| = kσ with k = 2

thing.zh: 守卫说的“最多四分之一”

means.en: Chebyshev: P(|X − μ| ≥ 2σ) ≤ 1/4

summary.en: The bell curve N(μ, σ²) is fixed by its mean and standard deviation; about 68%, 95% and 99.7% of it lies within 1, 2 and 3σ of μ.
summary.zh: 钟形曲线 N(μ,σ²) 由均值和标准差决定；约 68%、95%、99.7% 的概率落在 μ 的 1、2、3 个 σ 之内。

explain.en: The normal distribution N(μ, σ²) has density f(x) = e^(−(x − μ)²/(2σ²)) / (σ√(2π)): a symmetric bell centred at μ, whose width is set by σ, with inflection points at μ ± σ. The 68–95–99.7 rule: P(|X − μ| < kσ) ≈ 0.683, 0.954 and 0.997 for k = 1, 2, 3. Any normal variable can be standardised: Z = (X − μ)/σ is N(0, 1), so one table of Φ(z) = P(Z ≤ z) serves them all. Sums of independent normal variables are normal, with means and variances adding. The normal curve is everywhere because of the central limit theorem: a sum of many small independent effects is approximately normal. Its tails are thin, so it underestimates extreme events when real data are heavy-tailed.
explain.zh: 正态分布 N(μ,σ²) 的密度为 f(x)=e^(−(x−μ)²/(2σ²))/(σ√(2π))：以 μ 为中心的对称钟形，宽度由 σ 决定，拐点在 μ±σ。68–95–99.7 法则：k=1、2、3 时 P(|X−μ|<kσ) 约为 0.683、0.954、0.997。任何正态变量都能标准化：Z=(X−μ)/σ 服从 N(0,1)，所以一张 Φ(z)=P(Z≤z) 表就够用。独立正态变量之和仍是正态的，均值与方差分别相加。正态分布无处不在，要归功于中心极限定理：许多微小独立因素之和近似正态。它的尾部很薄，真实数据重尾时会低估极端事件。

example.en: Suppose adult heights in a population are N(170 cm, 10²). A height of 190 cm has z = (190 − 170)/10 = 2, so about 2.3% of people are taller: half of the 4.6% outside ±2σ. The middle 95% lie between 150 and 190 cm, and about 68% between 160 and 180 cm.
example.zh: 设某人群成年人身高服从 N(170 cm, 10²)。身高 190 cm 对应 z=(190−170)/10=2，所以约 2.3% 的人高于 190 cm：恰是 ±2σ 之外 4.6% 的一半。中间 95% 的人身高在 150 到 190 cm 之间，约 68% 在 160 到 180 cm 之间。

image.en: Gold bars stand in six columns on the vault floor, 1, 4, 10, 10, 4 and 1 bars high, rising and falling like a bell, and a golden bell hangs right above the middle. A brass ruler in front marks one σ to each side of the centre. A banker in a top hat points at the two tall middle columns: they hold two thirds of the gold, and the middle four nearly all of it.
image.zh: 金库地上，金条码成六列，高度依次为 1、4、10、10、4、1 根，起伏如钟，正中上方还悬着一口金钟。前面一把黄铜尺从中心向两侧各量出一个 σ。戴高礼帽的银行家指着中间两根高柱：它们装着约三分之二的金子，中间四列则几乎装下全部。

the peak at the mean μ

summary.en: What large samples guarantee, and how to estimate parameters and test claims from data.
summary.zh: 大样本能保证什么，以及如何用数据估计参数、检验论断。

summary.en: The average of many independent trials converges to the expected value by dilution, not compensation, so the gambler's fallacy is still a fallacy.
summary.zh: 大量独立试验的平均值收敛到期望值；它靠稀释而不是补偿，所以赌徒谬误依然是谬误。

explain.en: Let X₁, X₂, … be i.i.d. with mean μ, and let X̄ₙ = (X₁ + … + Xₙ)/n. The weak law says that for every ε > 0, P(|X̄ₙ − μ| > ε) → 0; if the variance σ² is finite, Chebyshev proves it at once, since Var(X̄ₙ) = σ²/n. The strong law says X̄ₙ → μ with probability 1. A finite mean is enough for both. This is why frequencies estimate probabilities and why Monte Carlo simulation works. It does not say that luck evens out: after 10 heads in a row, a fair coin is still 50:50 on the next toss. Early deviations are not cancelled; they are swamped by later trials. The difference between the count of heads and n/2 typically grows like √n, while the proportion still converges.
explain.zh: 设 X₁,X₂,… 独立同分布，均值为 μ，记 X̄ₙ=(X₁+…+Xₙ)/n。弱大数定律：对任意 ε>0，P(|X̄ₙ−μ|>ε)→0；方差 σ² 有限时，用切比雪夫不等式立即可证，因为 Var(X̄ₙ)=σ²/n。强大数定律：X̄ₙ 以概率 1 收敛到 μ。两者都只需均值有限。这就是频率能估计概率、蒙特卡罗模拟能奏效的原因。但它并不是说运气会“扯平”：公平硬币连出 10 次正面后，下一次仍是五五开。早期偏差不会被抵消，而是被后来的大量试验稀释。正面次数与 n/2 之差通常按 √n 增长，比例却照样收敛。

example.en: Toss a fair coin. After 10 tosses, 7 heads (70%) is unremarkable: 7 or more heads happens about 17% of the time. After 10,000 tosses the share of heads is within one percentage point of 50% with probability about 95%, since its standard deviation is 0.5%. Yet the gap between heads and tails has standard deviation √10,000 = 100, far larger than after 10 tosses.
example.zh: 抛公平硬币。抛 10 次得 7 次正面（70%）毫不稀奇：至少 7 次正面的概率约 17%。抛 1 万次后，正面比例落在 50%±1 个百分点内的概率约 95%，因为比例的标准差是 0.5%。可正反面次数之差的标准差是 √10000=100，比抛 10 次时大得多。

image.en: Four lab flasks stand in a row, each much bigger than the last. Every coin toss adds a drop: red dye for heads, clear water for tails. The small first flask, after 10 tosses with 7 heads, is deep red; each bigger flask holds far more tosses and is closer to the even pink of a 50:50 mix. A gambler shouts “Tails is due!”, but the scientist just keeps pouring: the early red is never cancelled, only diluted.
image.zh: 实验台上一排四只烧瓶，一只比一只大得多。每抛一次硬币就滴一滴：正面滴红色染料，反面滴清水。第一只小瓶装着 10 次抛掷、7 次正面，颜色深红；越往后的瓶子装的抛掷越多，颜色越接近五五开的均匀粉红。赌徒大喊“该出反面了！”，科学家却只管继续往里倒：早先的红色从未被抵消，只是被稀释了。

means.en: few trials: the average can stray far from μ
means.zh: 试验少：平均值可能远离 μ

thing.zh: 越来越大、越来越粉的烧瓶

means.en: X̄ₙ → μ = 1/2 as n grows
early deviations are diluted, not cancelled
means.zh: 早期偏差被稀释，而非被抵消

means.en: the gambler's fallacy: the coin has no memory
means.zh: 赌徒谬误：硬币没有记忆

summary.en: Standardised sums of many i.i.d. variables with finite variance are approximately normal, whatever the shape of the original distribution.
summary.zh: 大量独立同分布、方差有限的随机变量之和，标准化后近似服从正态分布，与原分布的形状无关。

explain.en: Let X₁, …, Xₙ be i.i.d. with mean μ and finite variance σ² > 0, and let Sₙ = X₁ + … + Xₙ. The central limit theorem says that (Sₙ − nμ)/(σ√n) converges in distribution to N(0, 1): for every z, its cdf at z tends to Φ(z). Equivalently, the sample mean X̄ₙ is approximately N(μ, σ²/n). The starting distribution can be skewed or discrete; the classical i.i.d. version needs only a finite variance. Where the law of large numbers says X̄ₙ → μ, the CLT describes the fluctuations around μ, of size σ/√n. A Galton board shows it: each ball is knocked left or right at every row of pegs, so its final slot is a sum of independent ±1 steps, and the slots fill into a bell. Distributions with infinite variance, such as the Cauchy, escape the theorem.
explain.zh: 设 X₁,…,Xₙ 独立同分布，均值 μ，方差 σ² 有限且大于 0，Sₙ=X₁+…+Xₙ。中心极限定理：(Sₙ−nμ)/(σ√n) 依分布收敛到 N(0,1)，即对每个 z，其分布函数趋于 Φ(z)。等价地，样本均值 X̄ₙ 近似服从 N(μ,σ²/n)。原分布可以偏斜，也可以离散；经典的独立同分布版本只要求方差有限。大数定律说 X̄ₙ→μ，中心极限定理则刻画围绕 μ 的波动，量级为 σ/√n。高尔顿板直观地演示了它：小球在每排钉子处随机向左或向右，落点是许多独立 ±1 步之和，槽里的球堆成钟形。方差无穷的分布（如柯西分布）不受此定理约束。

example.en: Single waiting times are very skewed: exponential with mean 10 min and SD 10 min. The average of 36 of them is approximately N(10, (10/6)²), so P(average > 13.3 min) ≈ P(Z > 2) ≈ 2.3%; the exact value is about 3.1%, since some skew remains at n = 36. On a Galton board with 12 rows, a ball lands in slot k with probability C(12, k)/4096.
example.zh: 单次等待时间很偏斜：服从均值 10 分钟、标准差 10 分钟的指数分布。36 次的平均值近似服从 N(10,(10/6)²)，所以 P(平均值>13.3 分钟)≈P(Z>2)≈2.3%；精确值约 3.1%，因为 n=36 时还残留一些偏斜。12 排钉子的高尔顿板上，小球落入第 k 个槽的概率是 C(12,k)/4096。

image.en: A Galton board is laid out on the lab floor. At the back a scientist tosses red balls into a brass funnel on a lab table; each ball bounces forward through four rows of upright pencils, knocked left or right at every row, and one is caught mid-bounce. In front the balls pile up in five slots, 1, 4, 6, 4 and 1 high: a sum of many random left-right steps settles into a bell.
image.zh: 实验室地上摆着一块高尔顿板。后方的科学家把红球抛进实验桌上的黄铜漏斗，每个球都向前穿过四排竖立的铅笔，在每一排都被随机撞向左或右，其中一个正弹在半空。前方五个槽里的球分别堆了 1、4、6、4、1 个高：许多随机左右步之和，最终堆成一口钟。

thing.en: the funnel dropping balls one by one

means.en: independent repetitions: each ball is one sample of the sum
means.zh: 独立重复：每个球都是和的一个样本

means.en: one random ±1 step, an i.i.d. term of the sum
means.zh: 一个随机的 ±1 步，和中的一项

means.en: a sum Sₙ being built
the distribution of the sum: already bell-shaped

summary.en: Maximum likelihood picks the parameter value under which the observed data are most probable; for a coin, it is the observed share of heads.
summary.zh: 最大似然估计选取使观测数据出现概率最大的参数值；对硬币来说，就是观测到的正面比例。

explain.en: Given data x₁, …, xₙ and a model with parameter θ, the likelihood L(θ) = P(data | θ), or the product of densities for continuous data, is viewed as a function of θ with the data fixed. It is not a probability distribution over θ. The maximum likelihood estimate θ̂ maximises L. In practice one maximises the log-likelihood ℓ(θ) = Σ log f(xᵢ; θ), which turns products into sums, by solving ℓ′(θ) = 0 and checking that it is a maximum. For a normal model the MLE of μ is the sample mean, while the MLE of σ² divides by n rather than n − 1 and is biased. Under regularity conditions the MLE is consistent and asymptotically normal, with the smallest possible asymptotic variance. Training a classifier by minimising cross-entropy is maximum likelihood.
explain.zh: 给定数据 x₁,…,xₙ 和含参数 θ 的模型，似然函数 L(θ)=P(数据|θ)（连续数据时为密度之积）把数据固定、看作 θ 的函数，它不是 θ 的概率分布。最大似然估计 θ̂ 使 L 最大。实践中改为最大化对数似然 ℓ(θ)=Σlog f(xᵢ;θ)，把乘积变成求和：解 ℓ′(θ)=0 并确认是极大值。正态模型中 μ 的最大似然估计是样本均值，而 σ² 的估计除以 n 而非 n−1，是有偏的。在正则条件下，最大似然估计相合、渐近正态，且渐近方差达到最小。训练分类器时最小化交叉熵，就是在做最大似然。

example.en: A coin gives 7 heads in 10 tosses. L(p) = p⁷(1 − p)³ and ℓ(p) = 7 log p + 3 log(1 − p). Setting ℓ′(p) = 7/p − 3/(1 − p) = 0 gives p̂ = 7/10. Compare L(0.7) ≈ 0.00222 with L(0.5) ≈ 0.00098: the data are about 2.3 times as likely under p = 0.7 as under a fair coin.
example.zh: 硬币抛 10 次得 7 次正面。L(p)=p⁷(1−p)³，ℓ(p)=7 log p+3 log(1−p)。令 ℓ′(p)=7/p−3/(1−p)=0，得 p̂=7/10。比较：L(0.7)≈0.00222，L(0.5)≈0.00098，这组数据在 p=0.7 下出现的可能性约是公平硬币的 2.3 倍。

image.en: A model mountain stands in the lab. Its height above each point of the scale in front, from 0 to 1, shows how probable 7 heads and 3 tails would be if the coin's chance of heads were that point. A climber has reached the summit, right above 0.7, and waves a flag, calling “p̂ = 0.7”. At the foot of the scale lie the data: seven gold coins and three silver.
image.zh: 实验室里立着一座模型山。山在前方 0 到 1 刻度上每一点的高度，表示硬币正面概率取该值时，出现 7 正 3 反的可能性有多大。一位登山者登上了顶峰，正对着 0.7，挥舞旗子高喊“p̂=0.7”。刻度尺前摆着数据：七枚金币、三枚银币。

thing.en: seven gold and three silver coins

means.en: the fixed data: 7 heads, 3 tails
means.zh: 固定的数据：7 正 3 反

means.en: the likelihood L(p) as a function of p
means.zh: 似然函数 L(p)，自变量是 p

means.en: maximising: the top is where ℓ′(p) = 0
the estimate p̂ = 7/10

summary.en: A 95% interval comes from a method that covers the true value 95% of the time; a p-value measures how surprising the data are under H₀.
summary.zh: 95% 置信区间来自一种 95% 的情况下能套住真值的方法；p 值衡量原假设成立时数据有多出人意料。

explain.en: For n observations from a normal population with known σ (or large n), x̄ ± 1.96·σ/√n is a 95% confidence interval for μ; when σ is estimated, use the t distribution. The 95% belongs to the method: over many samples, 95% of such intervals cover μ, while any single interval either does or does not. A hypothesis test starts from a null hypothesis H₀ and computes the p-value, the probability, assuming H₀, of data at least as extreme as those observed. If p < α, often 0.05, reject H₀. A p-value is not the probability that H₀ is true, not the size or importance of an effect, and 1 − p is not the chance of replication. Running many tests inflates false positives. A two-sided test at level α rejects μ = μ₀ exactly when μ₀ lies outside the 1 − α interval.
explain.zh: 对来自正态总体、σ 已知（或 n 很大）的 n 个观测，x̄±1.96·σ/√n 是 μ 的 95% 置信区间；σ 需要估计时改用 t 分布。这个 95% 属于方法：反复抽样时，约 95% 的区间会覆盖 μ，而任何一个具体区间要么覆盖，要么没覆盖。假设检验从原假设 H₀ 出发计算 p 值：在 H₀ 成立的前提下，得到至少和观测一样极端的数据的概率。若 p<α（常取 0.05），就拒绝 H₀。p 值不是 H₀ 为真的概率，不代表效应的大小或重要性，1−p 也不是重复实验成功的概率。检验做得越多，假阳性越多。水平 α 的双侧检验拒绝 μ=μ₀，当且仅当 μ₀ 落在 1−α 置信区间之外。

example.en: A machine should fill bags with μ₀ = 500 g, and σ = 10 g is known. A sample of 25 bags has x̄ = 496 g. The 95% interval is 496 ± 1.96·10/5 = 496 ± 3.92, or [492.1, 499.9], which excludes 500. The test agrees: z = (496 − 500)/2 = −2 gives a two-sided p ≈ 0.046 < 0.05, so H₀ is rejected at the 5% level.

image.en: Five identical white lab rabbits sit in a row, one for each repetition of the experiment, and the rabbit never moves. Each time, a scientist drops a cage at a fresh random spot: four cages are coming down right over their rabbits, but the fifth has landed beside its rabbit, empty and red. “95%,” says the scientist: in the long run, 19 cages out of 20 catch the rabbit.
image.zh: 五只一模一样的白色实验兔排成一排，每只代表一次重复实验，而兔子本身从不挪动。科学家每次都在一个随机的新位置放下笼子：四只笼子正罩向各自的兔子，第五只却落在兔子旁边，空空的，漆成红色。科学家说“95%”：长期来看，20 只笼子里有 19 只能罩住兔子。

means.en: the true μ: fixed, not random

thing.en: a cage dropped at a random spot

means.en: one sample's interval x̄ ± 1.96σ/√n
in the long run 95% of intervals cover μ
means.zh: 长期来看 95% 的区间覆盖 μ
